after four month sail and many a storm they be carry to a island of round form five thousand furlong in compass when they draw near to the island jambu^^ some of the inhabitant send forth a boat to meet they other run to they wonder at these new come stranger and entertain they very kind and courteous impart to they such thing as they have the man of this island be not like to we either in their body or manner yet all have the same form inhabitant describe but they exceed we four cubit in stature they wind their bone this way and that way as they please a a so do the now like sinew their body be strong and nimble than we for if they have take any thing into their hand no man can pull it out of their finger they have no hair except on their head eyebrow eyelid and chin on the other part of their body they be so smooth that there do not appear the least down they be fair comely and have well shape body the hole of their ear be much wide than we also their tongue differ from we for their tongue have somewhat peculiar by nature or Art cleave tongue liar emblem nature have give they a cleave tongue which be divide in the bottom so that it seem double from the root so they use a diverse speech and do not only speak with the voice of man but imitate the sing of bird but that which seem most notable they speak at one time perfect with two man both answer and discourse for with one part of their tongue they speak to one and with the other to the other temperate air Homer the air be very clear all the year long as the poet have write that the pear do ripen upon the pear and the apple upon the apple and the grape upon the grape and the fig upon the fig. also they say the day and night be always equal about noon when the sun be over their head it make no shadow they live according to their kindred and society which yet exceed not four hundred they dwell in meadow the earth bring forth plentiful fruit free without any tillage for the goodness of the island and temperature of the air make the earth of it own accord wonderful fertile this reed be a just description of Maiz or indian wheat there grow many reed bear plentiful fruit like to a white vetch when they have gather these they steep they in water till each of they be swell to the quantity of a dove egg afterward of these beat they make bread of a wonderful sweetness there be also in that island great spring of water whereof some flow forth very hot for the use of bath and cure disease and some be cold very sweet and wholesome they respect all kind of learning especial astrology they use letter whereof they have eight and twenty according to the value of signification their letter yet but seven character each whereof be vary four way they live very long namely one hundred and fifty year and for the most part without any sickness if any have a fever or be sick in his body they enforce he to die according to their Law they write not by the side China form of line in writing common woman as we do but from the top in a straight line to the bottom they have a custom to live to a certain age which be finish they diverse of their own accord kill themselves they have a double plant upon which whosoever lie down be bring into a sweet sleep and die the woman marry not but be common to all in like manner the male be bring up and common to all they often take away the child from the mother that they may not know they whereby it come to pass that there be no ambition among they or factious affection but they live peaceable without jar there be small creature in the island who blood be of a admirable nature and virtue their body be round fabulous creature and like to tortoise two streak cross one another on the middle of they in the extremity of each of which be a ear and a eye so that they see with four eye and hear with so many ear they have but one belly wherein they convey that which they eat they have many foot round about wherewith they go both way the blood of this beast be affirm to be of a wonderful efficacy for any body cut with gash while it breathe sprinkle with this blood present cleave together and in like manner if a hand be cut off or any other member while life last the part will be join together if it be apply to the wound while it be fresh every family nourish great bird of a diverse nature wherewith they try what their son will be for set their child on these fowl if they be not affright while they be carry through the air they bring they up but if they faint through fear or cowardliness they cast they down as unworthy to live any long and unprofitable for any exerciese the elder of every family as king command the rest who all obey he when he be one hundred and fifty year old they take away his life according to their law and the elder next he take the principality the sea wherewith the island be environ be very tempestuous and cause great wave the water be fresh the bear and many star which appear to we be not see of they there be seven land of the Xe^a or sua. a abassine priest in their behalf to Rome who before the cardinal make answer as follow july 1. 1594. the reverend brother Tecla Maria son of Tecla Nebiat of the city Henza Mariam of the and most reverend lord cardinal of saint Severine protector of the ethiopian nation to certain interrogatory make in the Arabic to he thus answer be ask what the ethiopian believe of God and the holy trinity he answer of God and the holy Trinity we believe in one God and three person the father son and holy ghost the father be unbegotten the son beget only of the father the holy ghost proceed from the father and the son be ask whether the holy ghost proceed from the father and the son as from two beginning and two spiration or as from one beginning and one spiration he answer as from one beginning and one only spiration be ask of the incarnation he answer that the person of the son the word of God the father be incarnate by the holy ghost of the virgin Mary be ask how many nature will abassine be monothelite and operations the ethiopian profess to be in Christ our lord he answer that the ethiopian believe after the union one nature one Will and one operation yet without mixtion and without confusion in which opinion he confess that the ethiopian and Cophti and other eastern nation err from the truth be ask whether they hold one nature in Christ result from two he answer the ethiopian say not so but simple profess one nature without mixtion and without confusion and affirm that to be divine be question of image he answer picture incense that among the ethiopian they be Basil the great greekish Monk^ but this order be divide into three order the first be call monastical the second be anachoreticall which live apart the three asceticall or if you will exerciticall the first order which be call monastical be in this manner there be monastery among the greek both great and little some of they have fifty monk other a hundred order monastical some one hundred and fifty some two hundred other three hundred other four hundred and other more but the monk of this first order live a common life for they all dine and sup together with their governor at the same table and neither the governor meat nor drink differ from the rest of the monk whether they be illiterate or wise their life in common and whensoever the governor eat or drink they all eat the same bread and the same meat and drink the same drink but for decency the governor senior and priest differ in their garment most of the monk of this first order labour with their hand but the priest and deacon labour not but attend to read and ecclesiastical function but the rest live by the labour of their hand some make the monk shoe some spin sheep wool and goat hair some be brazier and make hatchet of brass hand-labour other betake themselves to keep flock of sheep and hire mercenary shepherd to serve they and be conversant with they a year and when a year be past they go to the monastery and tarry there other go to keep horse and remain out a year and then other be send out by the ancient of the monastery and according to this manner the ancient send out monk yearly to keep horse ox bee sheep and other business and after a year they return to the monastery and in this manner live the monk in the monastery many priest also be send by the ancient into Walachia Moscovia and Iberia that whatsoever the king give they they may carry to the monastery and they abide in the monastery and other be send forth and thus live the monk of the first order in their monastery their habit they wear a hat on their head which hide their ear signify that they hear nothing neither learn man vice but be account as deaf man as Paul say be child in maliciousness they wear also another hat upon that which represent the figure of a sepulchre and hide the head and hang down almost to the girdle intimate that he which wear this figure be dead from worldly thing neither ought he which be clothe in this habit to be careful about worldly affair that be about honour riches kindred friend favour with man nor cherish the body but account himself to be dead not as if he be real dead but with a kind of preoccupated opinion of death as the lord say whosoever will come after i let he deny himself and take up his cross and follow i and David we be kill all the day long for thy sake the second order of monk be call anachoreticall or heremeticall that be when there be any rich man monk eremitical that can live in the monastery than he give as much money to the monastery as will buy a house and the monk live in the monastery give he some great house which be distant two or three mile from the monastery wherein he live with two or three poor monk as the monastical do in monastery but that house have a church vine-yard oliveyard nut cherry almond and other thing necessary to live on abundant and this be the second order of monk of Basil the great the three order of monk be call asceticall or exerciticall that be the order give to exercise monk asceticall or vacant to strict exercise for these be exceed exercise in virtue these live a strict and rigid life they be content only with little Eden 1577 to our most dear belove son in CHRIST king Ferdinando and to our dear belove daughter in CHRIST Elizabeth queen of Castille legion Arragon Sicily and Granata most noble prince greeting and apostolical benediction among other work acceptable to the divine majesty and according to our heart desire this certain be the chief that the catholic faith and christian religion special in this our time may in all place be exalt amplify and enlarge whereby the health of soul may be procure and the barbarous nation subdue and bring to the Faith and therefore whereas by the favour of God clemency although not without equal desert we be call to this holy seat of PETER and understand you to be true catholic prince as we have ever know you and as your noble and worthy fact have declare in manner to the whole world in that with all your study diligence and industry you have spare no travail charge or peril adventure even the shed of your own blood with apply your whole mind and endeavour hereunto as your noble expedition achieve in recover the kingdom of Granata from the tyranny of the sarracen in these our day do plain declare your fact with so great glory of the divine name for the which as we think you worthy so ought we of our own free will favourable to grant you all thing whereby you may daily with more fervent mind to the honour of God and enlarge the christian empire prosecute your devout and laudable purpose most acceptable to the immortal God we be credible inform that whereas of late you be determine to seek and find certain land and firm land far remote and unknown and not heretofore find by any other to the intent to bring the inhabitant of the same to honour our redeemer and to profess the catholic faith you have hitherto be much occupy in the expugnation and recovery of the kingdom of Granata by reason whereof you can not bring your say laudable purpose to the end desire nevertheless as it have please almighty God the foresay kingdom be recover willing to accomplish your say desire you have not without great labour peril and charge appoint our well-beloved son Christopher colonus a man certes well commend as most worthy and apt for so great a matter well furnish with man and ship and other necessary to seek by the sea where hitherto no man have sail such firm land and land far remote and hitherto unknown who by God help make diligent search in the ocean sea have find certain remote land and firm land which be not heretofore find by any other in the which as be say many nation inhabit live peaceable and go naked not accustom to eat flesh and as far as your messenger can conjecture the nation inhabit the foresay land and land believe that there be one God creator in heaven and seem apt to be bring to the embrace of the catholic faith and to be endue with good manner by reason whereof we may hope that if they be well instruct they may easy be induce to receive the name of our saviour JESUS CHRIST we be further advertise that the forenamed Christopher have now build and erect a fortress with good munition in one of the foresay principal land in the which he have place a garrison of certain of the christian man that go thither with he as well to the intent to defend the same as also to search other land and firm land far remote and yet unknown we also understand that in these land and land late find be great plenty of gold and spice with diverse and many other precious thing of sundry kind and quality therefore all thing diligent consider especial the amplify and enlarge of the catholic faith as it behove catholic prince follow the example of your noble progenitor of famous memory you have determine by the favour of almighty God to subject unto you the firm land and land aforesaid and the dweller and inhabitant thereof and to bring they to the catholic Faith we great commend this your godly and laudable purpose in our lord and desirous to have the same bring to a due end and the name of our saviour to be know in those part do exhort you in our lord and by the receive of your holy baptism whereby you be find to apostolical obedience and earnest require you by the bowel of mercy of our lord JESUS CHRIST that when you intend for the zeal of the catholic faith to prosecute the say expedition to reduce the people of the foresay land and land to the christian religion you shall spare no labour at any time or be deter with any peril conceive firm hope and confidence that the omnipotent God will give good success to your godly attempt and that be authorise by the privilege of the apostolical grace you may the more free and bold take upon you the enterprise of so great a matter we of our own motion and not either at your request or at the instant petition of any other person but of our own mere liberality and certain science and by the fullness of apostolical power do give grant and assign to you your heir and successor all the firm land and land find or to be find discover or to be discover towards the west and south draw a line from the pole arctic to the pole antarctic that be from the north to the south contain in this donation whatsoever firm land or land be find or to be find towards India or towards any other part whatsoever it be be distant from or without the foresay line draw a hundred league towards the west and south from any of the land which be common call and Capo Verde all the land therefore and firm land find and to be find discover and to be discover from the say line towards the west and south such as have not actual be heretofore possess by any other christian king or prince until the day of the nativity of our lord JESV CHRIST last pass from the which begin this present year be the year of our lord a thousand four hundred ninety three when soever any such shall be find by your messenger and captain we by the authority of almighty GOD grant unto we in saint PETER and by the vicarship of JESUS CHRIST which we bear on the earth do for ever by the tenor of these present give grant assign unto you your heir and successor the king of Castille and legion all those land and land with their dominion territory city castle tower place and village with all the right and jurisdiction thereunto pertain constitute assign and depute you your heir and successor the lord thereof with full and free power authority and jurisdiction decree nevertheless by this our donation grant and assignation that from no christian prince which actual have possess the foresay land and firm land unto the day of the nativity of our lord beforesaid their right obtain to be understand hereby to be take away or that it ought to be take away furthermore we command you in the virtue of holy obedience as you have promise and as we doubt not you will do upon mere devotion and princely magnimitie to send to the say firm land and land honest virtuous and learned man such as fear God and be able to instruct the inhabitant in the catholic faith and good manner apply all their possible diligence in the premise we furthermore strait inhibit all manner of person of what state degree order or condition soever they be although of imperial and regal dignity under the pain of the sentence of excommunication which they shall incur if they do to the contrary that they in no case presume without special licence of you your heir and successor to travail for merchandise or for any other cause to the say land or land find or to be find discover or to be discover towards the west and south draw a line from the pole arctic to the pole antarctic whether the firm land and land find and to be find be situate towards India or towards any other part be distant from the line draw a hundred league towards the west from any of the butter when they intend to make vinegar they suffer only the water to putrify and then set it to the sun where it become vinegar like unto that which be make of white wine and when they mingle the kernel with the water which be in the midst of the fruit and strain it through a cloth they make a milk thereof like unto goat milk these date-tree be like unto they that bear date but be not so full of knot with the juice of two of these date-tree a whole family of ten person may be maintain with wine use one eight day and the other other eight day for they shall else be dry and wither these tree continue for the space of a hundred year this island where they find this human and gentle people be call zuluan the island of Zuluan and be not very big they invite the general to their boat in which be their merchandise viz. clove cinnamon ginger pepper nutmeg mace gold make in diverse thing which they carry to and fro with their bark he have they also aboard the ship and cause a piece of in two bark the man be naked have two gold ring at their ear and many jewel fasten with gold to their arm with these they refresh their sick man they tell of people in near land with ear down to their name this sea Archipelago San Lazaro that be the great sea of saint Lazarus be ten degree above the equinoctial towards our pole and a hundred threescore and one from the place from whence they depart the people of this island be gentile they go naked save that they cover their privy part with a cloth make of the rind of a certain tree the chief man have about their head a silken cloth of Buthuan the eight and twenty day of march they come to the island of Buthuan where they be honourable entertain of the king and the prince his son who give they much gold and spice the captain give one man offer for six thread of crystal bead a crown of massy gold with a collar but the general will not permit such barter that they shall not perceive more account to be make of their gold by the one then by the other of the spanish ware the people be nimble naked paint the woman go clothe from the waste downward with their long black hair hang to the ground they wear earring of gold in diverse form they always be chew Arecca a certain fruit like a pear cut in quarter and roll up in leaf of a tree call good or vetele like bay leaf which have chew they spit forth it make the mouth red they say they do it to comfort the heart nor can live without it the captain or general cause a cross to be bring forth with nail and a crown of thorn give commandment to all his man to give reverence thereunto and signify to the king by the interpreter that that banner be give he by the emperor his lord and master with commandment to leave the same in all place where he come to the great commodity and profit of all such as will reverendly receive it as a assure token of friendship and that he will therefore leave it there as well to accomplish his lord commandment as also that if at any time any ship of christian shall chance to come that way they may by see that cross perceive that our man have be well entertain there and will therefore not only abstain from do they any hurt or displeasure but also help to aid they against their enemy and that therefore it shall be requisite to erect that cross upon the top of the high mountain that may be see from the sea on every side also to pray unto it reverent and that in so do they shall not be hurt with thunder lightning and tempest when the king hear these word they give the captain great thanks promise glad to observe and fulfil all such thing as he require then the captain demand whether they be Moor or gentile they answer mores and gentile that they have none other kind of religion but that lift up their hand join together and their face towards heaven they call upon their god abba which answer like the captain very well because the gentile be soon persuade to our faith then the moor depart from hence they come to the land of Zeilon Zubut messana and Calaghan by the conduct of certain pilot of the say king of these Zubut be the best many land and have the trade of best traffic in the island of messana they find dog Zubut and pass by many village and habitation in tree they come to the city where the captain give commandment to the mariner to strike their sail and to set themselves in order in manner of battell-ray cause all the ordnance to be shoot off wherewith all the people be put in great fear after this the captain send a ambassador with the interpreter to the king of Zubut when they approach near to the city they find the king with a great company of man sore astony at the noise of the gun but the interpreter advertise they that it be the custom of our man in all such place where they come to discharge their ordnance in token of friendship and to honour the lord of the city with which word the king and his company be well quiet after this the interpreter declare that his master be the captain of the ship of the great prince in the world and that they go to discover the land of Molucca and further that hear of his good name and fame by the report of the king of messana they determine to visit he and to have victual for exchange of their merchandise the king answer that he be well content therewith and that they be hearty welcome nevertheless that it be a custom in that place that all such ship as enter into that haven shall pay tribute and that there be not many day past since a ship lade with gold and slave do so pay in token whereof he cause to come before he certain merchant of that company which yet remain with he a ship lade with gold and slave to this the interpreter answer that for as much as his lord be the captain of so mighty a prince he never pay tribute to any king in the world and will not now begin will he to take this for a resolute answer that if he will accept the peace that be proffer he he shall enjoy it and if he rather desire wa^re he shall have his hand full when the interpreter have say these word one of the say merchant who be a more speak to the king in this manner Catacaia Chita that be take heed sir for these man be they that have conquer Calcutta Malacha and all the great India and be of such power that if you entreat they otherwise then well you may too late know what they be able to do Calcutta Malacha more than they have do at Calcutta and malacca when the interpreter hear these word he say that the king his lord be of much great puissance and more dominion and lord of more ship than be the king of Portugal declare further that he be king of Spain and emperor of all Christendom add hereunto that if he will not be his friend he will hereafter send thither such a power of arm man as shall destroy his country the more confer all these word with the king who say that he will further deliberate with his council and give they a full answer the day follow in the mean time he send they certain victual and wine when all these thing be declare to the king of messana who be the chief thereabouts next unto he and lord of many land he go a land and repair to the king of Zubut and declare unto he the and this be a manifest miracle wrought in our time whereby diverse infidel be convert to our faith and their idol destroy and also their altar overthrow on the which they be accustom to eat the HACKLVYT and now review and correct the fifteen day of November in the year of our lord 1577. m. Francis drake with a fleet of five ship and bark and to the number of a hundred sixty four man gentleman and sailor depart from Plymouth give out his pretend voyage for Alexandria but the wind fall contrary he be force the next morning to put into Falmouth haven in Cornwall where such and so terrible a tempest take we as few man have see the like and be indeed so vehement that all our ship be like to have go to wrack but it please God to preserve we from that extremity and to afflict we only for that present with these two particular the mast of our admiral which be the pelican be cut overboard for the safeguard of the ship and the marigold be drive ashore and somewhat bruise for the repair of which damage we return again to Plymouth and have recover those harm and bring the ship again to good state we set forth the second time from Plymouth and set sail the thirteen day of December follow the five and twenty day of the same month we fall with the cape cantin upon the coast of Barbary and coast along the seven and twenty day we find a island call mogador lie one mile distant from the main between which island and the main the isle of mogador on the coast of Barbary we find a very good and safe harbour for our ship to ride in as also very good entrance and void of any danger on this island our general erect a pinnace whereof he bring out of England with he four ready frame while these thing be in do there come to the water side some of the inhabitant of the country show forth their flag of truce which be see of our general he send his shippe-boat to the shore to know what they will they be willing to come aboard our man leave there one man of our company for a pledge and bring two of they aboard our ship which by sign show our general that the next day they will bring some provision as sheep capon and hen and such like whereupon our general bestow among they some linen cloth and shoe and a javelin which they very joyful receive and depart for that time the next morning they fail not to come again to the water side and our general again set out our boat one of our man leap over-rash ashore and offer friendly to embrace they they lay violent hand on he offer a dagger to his throat if he have make any resistance and so lay he on a horse carry he away so that a man can be too circumspect and wary of himself among such miscreant our pinnace be finish januarie we depart from this place the thirty and last day of December and coast along the shore we do descry not contrary to our expectation certain canter which be spanish fisherman to who we give chase and take three of they and proceed further we meet with three caravel and take they also the seventeen day of january we arrive at cape blanco where we find a ship ride at anchor within the cape and but two simple mariner in she which ship we take and carry she further into the harbour where we remain four day and in that space our general muster and train his man on land in warlike manner to make they fit for all occasion in this place we take of the fisherman such necessary as we want and they can yield we and leave here one of our little bark call the Benedict we take with we one of they which they call canter be of the burden of forty ton or thereabouts all these thing be finish we depart this harbour the two and twenty of january carry along with we one of the Portugal caravel which be find to the land of cape Verde for salt whereof good store be make in one of those land the master or pilot of that caravell do advertise our general that upon one of those land call mayo there be great store of dry cabrito which a few inhabitant the isle of mayo there dwell do yearly make ready for such of the king ship as do there touch be find for his country of Brasile or elsewhere we fall with this island the seven and twenty of january but the inhabitant will in no case traffic with we be thereof forbid by the king edict yet the next day our general send to view the island and the likely hood that may be there of provision of victual about threescore and two man under the conduct and government of master winter and master Doughtie and march towards the chief place of habitation in this island as by the Portugal we be inform have travel to the mountain the space of three mile and arrive there somewhat before the day break we rest ourselves to see day before we which appear we find the inhabitant to be flee but the place by reason that it be manure we find to be more fruitful than the other part especial the valley among the hill here we give ourselves a little refresh as by very ripe and sweet grape which the fruitfulness of the earth at that season of the year yield we ripe grape in winter and that season be with we the depth of winter it may seem strange that those fruit be then there grow but the reason thereof be this because they be between the tropic and the equinoctial the sun pass twice in the year through their zenith over their head by mean whereof they have two summer and be so near the heat of the line they never lose the heat of the sun so much but the fruit have their increase and continuance in the midst of winter the island be wonderful store with goat and wild hen and it have salt also without labour save only that the people gather it into heap which continual in great quantity be increase upon the sand by the flow of the sea and the heat of the sun kern the same so that of the increase thereof they keep a continual traffic with their neighbour among other thing we find here a kind of fruit call which because it be not common know with we in England I think good to make some description of it the description of the tree that bear the tree bear no leave nor branch but at the very top the fruit grow in cluster hard at the top of the stem of the tree as big every several fruit as a man head but have take off the uttermost bark which you shall find to be very full of string or sinew as I may term they you shall come to a hard shell which may hold of quantity in liquor a pint common or some a quart and some less within that shell of the thickness of half a inch good you shall have a kind of hard substance and very white no less good and sweet then almond within that again a certain clear liquor which be drink you shall not only find it very delicate and sweet but most comfortable and cordial after we have satisfy ourselves with some of these fruit we march further into the island and see great store of * * or goat cabritos alive which be so chase by the inhabitant that we can do no good towards our provision but they have lay out as it be to stop our mouth withal certain old dry cabrito which be but ill and small and few we make no account of be return to our ship our general depart hence the one and thirty of this month the isle of s. jago and sail by the island of saint jago but far enough from the danger of the inhabitant who shot and discharge at we three piece but they all fall short of we and do we no harm the island be fair and large and as it seem rich and fruitful and inhabit by the portugal but the mountain and high place of the island be say to be possess by the moor who have be slave to the portugal to ease themselves make escape to the desert place of the island where they abide with great strength be before this island we espy two ship under sail to the one of which we give chase and in the end board she with a shipboat without resistance which we find to be a good prize a pri^e and Nuno da Si^ua a Portugal pilot take and she yield unto we good store of wine which prize our general commit to the custody of master Doughtie and retain the pilot send the rest away with his pinnace give they a but of wine and some victual and their wear clothes and so they depart the same night we come with the island call by the portugal Ilha that be the burn island the isle of fogo in the north side whereof be a consume fire the matter be say to be of sulphur but notwithstanding it be like to be a commodious island because the portugal have build and do inhabit there upon the south side thereof lie a most pleasant and sweet island the tree whereof be always green and fair to look upon in respect whereof they call it ilha Brava that be the brave island from the bank thereof into the sea do run in many place reasonable stream of fresh water easy to be come by but there be no convenient road for our ship for such be the depth that no ground can be have for anchor and it be report that ground be never find in that place so that the top of fogo burn not so high in the air but the root of Brava be drench as low in the Sea be depart from these land we draw towards the line where we be becalm the space of three week but yet subject to diverse great storm terrible lightning and much thunder but with this misery we have the commodity of great store of fish as dolphin bonito and fly fish whereof some fall into our ship wherehence they can not it be then the winter sea on in those part can not possible escape the other cause be the dangerous situation of the mouth of the straits in the south sea where continual storm reign and bluster as he sixteenth of April till the three of june june sir Francis Drake sail on the backside of America to 43. degree of northerly latitude 38. degree the five day of june be in three and forty degree towards the pole arctic we find the air so cold that our man be grievous pinch with the same complain of the extremity thereof and the further we go the more the cold increase upon we whereupon we courteous entreat they and liberal bestow on they necessary thing to cover their nakedness whereupon they suppose we to be god and will not be persuade to the contrary the present which they send to our general be feather and kawles of network their house be dig round about with earth and have from the uttermost brim of the circle cliff of wood set upon they join close together at the top like a it these woman be very obedient and serviceable to their husband after they be depart from we they come and visit we the second time and bring with they feather and bag of tobacco for present and when they come to the top of the hill at the bottom whereof we have pitch our tent they stay themselves where one appoint for speaker weary himself with make a long oration which do they leave their bow upon the hill and come down with their present in the mean time a long oration the woman remain on the hill torment themselves lamentable tear their flesh from their cheek whereby we perceive that they be about a sacrifice in the mean time our general with his company go to prayer and to read of the scripture at which exercise they be attentive and seem great to be affect with it but when they be come unto we they restore again unto we those thing which before we bestow upon they the news of our be there be spread through the country the people that inhabit round about come down and among our general have satisfy they they return with glad tiding to their king who march to we with a princely majesty the people cry continual after their manner and as they draw near unto we so do they trial januarie in 1579. to the hazard and danger of our ship and life for upon the nine of january in the year 1579. we run sudden upon a rock where we stick fast from eight of the clock at night till confidence in the mercy and protection of God so now he continue in the same and lest he shall seem to perish wilful both he and we do our best endeavour to save ourselves which it please God so to they in for there ebb and flow much water therefore we grave and trim all our ship there here a man and a boy in wash their clothes at a pit they grave and trim their ship be hurt by the savage arrow which be make of cane head with flint they be very wild we take the measure of one of their foot all kind of giant and it be eighteen inch long their use be when any of they die to bring he or they to the cliff by the seaside and upon the top of they they bury they and in their grave be bury with they their bow and arrow and all their jewel which they have in their life time which be fine shell which they find by the sea side which they cut and square after a artificial manner and all be lay under their head the grave be make all with great stone of great length and bigness be set all along full of the dead man dart which he use when he be live and they colour both their dart and their grave with a red colour which they use in colour of themselves their departure from port desire the 48. degree 1/^ to the southward of the line january 1587. the second day of januarie we fall with a very fair white cape which stand in 52. degree and have seven fathom water a league of the land the to the open of the dangerous straight of Magellan which be in diverse place five or six league wide and in two several place more narrow under this cape we anchor and lose a anchor for it be a great the mouth of the straits and the narrow place thereof we take a Spaniard who name be Hernando who be there with three and twenty spaniard more which be all that remain of four hundred which be leave there three year before in these straits of Magellan all the rest be dead with famine and the same day we pass through the narrow of the straits where the aforesaid Spaniard show we the Hull of a the course lie west and by north. the mouth of the straits stand in two and fifty degree from the narrow of the straits unto Pengwin island be ten league and lie west Southwest somewhat to the southward where we anchor the eight day and kill and salt great store of pengwin for victual the nine day we depart from Pengwin island king Philip city leave desolate in the straits of Magellan which our general call port famine and run south Southwest to king Philip city which the spaniard have build which town or city have four fort and every fort have in it one cast piece which piece be bury in the ground the carriage be stand in their place unburied we dig for they and have they all they have contrive their city very well and seat it in the best place of the straits for wood and water they have build up their church by themselves they have law very severe among themselves for they have erect a gibbet whereon they have do execution upon some of their company it seem unto we that their whole live for a great space be altogether upon muskle and lympit for there be not any thing else to be have except some deer which come out of the mountain down to the fresh river to drink these spaniard which be there be only come to fortify the straits to the end that no other nation shall have passage through into the south sea save only their own but as it appear God enemy to the spaniard avarice which will entail the wide world in the east and west to Spain it be not god will so to have it for during the time that they be there which be two year at the least they can never have any thing to grow or in any wise prosper and on the other side the indian oftentimes prey upon they until their victual grow so short their store be spend which they have bring with they out of Spain and have no mean to renew the same that they die like dog in their house and in their clothes wherein we find they still at our come until that in the end the town be wonderful taint with the smell and the savour of the dead people the rest which remain alive be drive to bury such thing as they have there in their town either for provision or for furniture and so to forsake the town and to go along the seaside and seek their victual to preserve they from starve take nothing with they but every man his harquebus and his furniture that be able to carry it for some be not able to carry they for weakness and so live for the space of a year and more with root leave and sometime a fowl which they may kill with their piece to conclude they be determine to have travel towards the river of plate only three and twenty person be leave alive whereof two be woman which be the remainder of four hundred in this place we water and wooded well and quiet our general name this town port famine port before speak of for they have get knife and piece of rapier to make dart of they use all the mean they can possible to have allure we up far into the river of purpose to have betray we which be espy off from the river of saint Jerome about three or four league we run west unto a cape which be on the north side and from that cape unto the mouth of the straits the course lie northwest and by west and northwest between which place and the mouth of the straits to the southward February 1587. we lay in harbour until the three and twenty of February by reason of contrary wind and most vile and filthy foul wether with such rain and vehement stormy wind which come down from the mountain and high hill that they hazard the best cable and anchor that we have for to hold which if they have fail we have be in great danger to have be cast away or at the least famish for during this time which be a full month we feed almost altogether upon muskle and limpit and bird or such as we can get on shore seek every day for they as the fowl of the air do where they can find food in continual rainy wether there be at every mile or two mile end a harbour on both side of the land and there be learn this place which be call Arauco be wonderful rich and full of gold mynes and yet can it not be subdue at any time by the spaniard but they always return with the great loss of man for these indian be desperate and careless of their life to live at their own liberty and freedom in the afternoon we weigh anchor and run under the west side of saint Mary island where we rid very well in six up to a place where the spaniard have erect a church with cross and altar in it a church with cross and altar and there be about this church two or three storehouse which be full of wheat and barley ready thresh and make up in cade of straw to the quantity of a bushel of corn in every Cade the wheat and barley be as fair as clean and every way as good as any we have in England there be also the like cade full of potato rootes which be very good to eat ready make up in the storehouse for the spaniard against they shall come for their tribute this island also yield many sort of fruit hog and hen these indian be hold in such slavery by they that they dare not eat a hen or a hog themselves but the spaniard have make they all in that island christian the indian of s. marry island make all christian thus we fit ourselves here with corn as much as we will have and as many hog as we have salt to powder they withal and great store of hen with a number of bag of potato rootes and about five after the wife of the say king so dead according to the custom and use of their country every one of they go together to a place appoint and the chief of the woman which be near unto he in account the wife kill themselves after their husband death have a ball in her hand and throw it from she and to the place where the ball rest thither they go all and turn their face to the eastward and every one with a dagger in their hand which dagger they call a Crise and be as sharp as a razor stab themselves to the heart and with their hand all to be-bath themselves in their own blood a strange order and fall grovel on their face so end their day this thing be as true as it seem to any hearer to be strange the man of themselves be very politic and subtle and singular valiant be naked man in any action they undertake and wonderful at commandment and fear of their King for example if their king command they to undertake any exploit be it never so dangerous or desperate they dare not refuse it though they die every man in the execution of the same for he will cut off the head of every one of they which return alive without bring of their purpose to pass which be such a thing among they as it make they the most valiant people in all the southeast-part of the world for they never fear any death for be in fight with any nation if any of they feel himself hurt with lance or sword he will willing run himself upon the weapon quite through his body to procure his death the more speedy and in this desperate sort end his day or overcome his enemy moreover although the man be tawny of colour and go continual naked yet their woman be fair of complexion and go more apparel they tell we further that if their king don Antonio will come unto they fair woman in java don Antonio may be receive as (@) Helena the 9 of june our boat be send away before to make the harbour and about one of the clock in the afternoon we come to a anchor in twelve fathom water two or three cable length from the shore in a very fair and smooth bay under the northwest-side of the island this island be very high land and lie in the main sea s. Helena be in the latitude of 15. degree 48. min. to the southward stand as it be in the midst of the sea between the main land of Africa and the main of Brasilia and the coast of Guinea and be in fifteen degree and forty eight minute to the southward of the equinoctial line and be distant from the cape of between five and six hundred league here we go on shore and enter the church which be hang with paint clothes have a altar with a picture of the crucifix and bless virgin in a table there be a causey to the church two house also adjoin a frame with two bell and a cross of freestone the great store of diverse excellent fruit in s. Helena the valley where it stand be pleasant and plant in every place either with fruit tree or with herb there be figtree which bear fruit continual and marvelous plentiful for on every tree you shall have blossom green fig and ripe fig all at once and it be so all the year long the reason be that the island stand so near the sun there be also great store of lymmon-tree orange-tree pomegranate-tree pomecitron-tree date-tree which bear fruit as the figge-tree do and be plant careful and very artificial with very pleasant walk under and between they and the say walk be over-shadowed with the leaf of the tree and in every void place be plant parsley sorrel Basill fenell annis-seed mustardseed radish and many special good herb and the fresh water brook run through diverse place of this orchard and may with very small pain be make to water any one tree in the valley there be also upon this island great store of partridge which be very tame not make any great haste to fly away though one come very near they abundance of partridge in s. Helena but only to run away and get up into the steep cliff we kill some of they with a fowl piece they be within a little as big as a hen and be of a ash-colour and live in covy twelve sixteen and twenty together you can go ten or twelve score but you shall se^ or spring one or two covy at the least great store of feasant turkey in great quantity there be likewise no less store of pheasant in the island which be surpass those which be in our country in bigness and in number of a company we find moreover in this place great store of guinie-cock which we call turkey of colour black and white with red head they be much about the same bigness which we be of in England their egg be white and as big as a Turkey egg there be in this island thousand of goat which the spaniard call cabrito which be very wild exceed number of goat you shall see one or two hundred of they together and sometime you may behold they go in a flock almost a mile long some of they be as big as a ass with a main like a horse and a beard hang down to the very ground we take and kill many of they for all their swiftness for there be thousand of they upon the mountain here be in like manner great store of swine which be very wild fat and large they keep altogether upon the mountain plenty of swine and will very sieldome abide any man to come near they except it be by mere chance when they be find asleep or otherwise according to their kind be take lay in the mire we find in the house at our come three slave which be Negro and one which be bear in the island of java for the portugal use to touch and refresh here at their return from the indies and leave their sick person to be take in by the next Fleet. our departure from s. chap. 7 the six circum-navigation by WILLIAM CORNELISON senouten of horn who southward from the straits of Magelan in terra-del-fuogo find and discover a new passage through the great south-sea and that way sail round about the world describe what island country people and strange adventure he find in his say passage because the general state of the unite nether-land province have grant patent of trade to the east indian company with prohibition to all other to pass the cape of good hope eastward or through the Magelen straits westward Isaak le maier a merchant of Amsterdam and William Cornelison Schouten of horn a man which have be thrice in the east indies devise and consult of some new way without impeachment of the say patent which they confident suppose may be do by some passage southward from the Magelan straits and to that end agree between they to enterprise such a voyage take order that Isaac le Maire shall provide the one half of the money and William Cornelison Schouten the other half to furnish the say voyage by the help and furtherance of their friend the care thereof and to make provision for the say voyage be refer to William Cornelison Schouten and to finish the say voyage the merchant aforesaid prepare and rig a great and a small ship of horn the great ship call the unity of three hundred sixty ton whereof William Cornelison Schouten be master and chief pilot and jacob le more merchant and principal factor in it have sixty five man and nineteen great piece and twelve sling with musket and other munition for war proportionable with a pinnace to sail another to row a boat and a scute anckor cabel rope sail and all other necessary belong thereunto the lesser ship call the horn of a hundred and ten ton whereof John Cornelison Schouten be master and aris clawson merchant in it twenty two man eight great piece four sling and other furniture as need require and be necessary for such a voyage and for that they will not make know to any man as I say before whether they mean to go they hire all their man both common sailor and officer to sail unto every place whether the master and the merchant will go which make the common sailor and people to speak and guess of that voyage diverse and at the last give they the name of the gold-finder but the merchant name they the south company the ship be ready upon the sixteenth of may 1615. the man be muster by the scout and Schepen of horn and the twenty five of the same month the unity set sail and arrive at the tessel upon the twenty seven the three of june the lesser depart from horn and the of our piece and we hoist anchor set forward again on our voyage hold our course west and west and by south we be of opinion that the king at that time have assemble all his force for he have at the go on land to refresh ourselves in regard that we have but little water but the master and the merchant will not the first island that be so high we name island and the other that lay a league distant from it we call traitor island because the most part of the indian that seek to betray we traitor island come from that island the fourteen in the morning we see another island right before we about island and better refresh but come to it can find no ground and therefore put out our Shalop to found a long the shore which about a musket shoot from the land find ground at forty fathom small black and soft stony ground sometime also they have twenty and thirty fathom but as soon as they be a shalop length or two from it they have no ground again then ten or twelve canoas come to our ship but we will not let they come aboard but show they friendly countenance and barter with they for four fly fish for the which we give they some bead which we let down by a rope at the stern of the ship and they take they tie the fish to the rope and we pull they up in the mean time our Shalop found along by the land which they in the canoas see present make towards it and be close by it at first speak unto the man but withal compass they about with fourteen canoas and therewith some of they leap overboard think to fall upon the Shalop or to draw it away with they which our man perceive shoot with their musket among they there be six musket and other arm courtelass and pike in the Shalop and therewith kill two of the indian as they sit in their canoas where of one present fall dead overboard the other sit still with his hand wipe off the blood upon his breast but at last f^ll likewise overboard the rest in the canoas be thereat in so great fear that in all haste they make away at which south-west the better to get to the south hope there to find firm land and it be so rough near to the island that it be a very bad place for a boat to go on shore the island be all full of black cliff thousand six hundred league eastward from the coast of Peru and chili and have not discover any part of as our intent be that there be not any appearance to discover any thing to our contentment that we also have sail further westward than we intend that sail forward in that manner without all doubt we shall fall southward upon Guinea and that if there we shall find no passage or way to get through it be very dangerous uncertain and not know that then both ship and good will be lose and we ourselves likewise shall perish it be unpossible to come eastward back again from thence by reason of the steadfast east-wind that in the west part continual blow that we also have but small store of victual and see no mean as yet to increase they and therefore ask their counsel whether it be not their best way to alter their course and to sail northward thereby to get northward to Guinea and so to the moluccoe which they consider of and well weigh find his reason to be true and think it again and present he that have take it be seek for and although he be go a good way of they bring he back who be come the Courtelasse be lay down at our foot and he be beat with staff they make sign when we show they that we can shoot with the great piece which the king desire we once to do which be do they be all so fearful and abash thereat that all of they as also the king sit under his Belay nail and some bead wherewith they be well please those people be man of good understanding and of great stature for the least man of they be as big as the tall of we and the tall of they be far high hair stand upright upon their head about a quarter of a ell long like hog bristle the king have a long lock of hair on the left side of his head that hang down beneath his hip find up with a knot or both in face and body of small stature their hair cut close to their head as our in Holland their breast long hang down to their belly like leather satchel they be very lecherous for they suffer themselves to be use by their man open in all man sight and in the king own presence only under a mat. we can not perceive that they worship God or any god or use any devotion neither the one nor the into a place where we have the land round about we therefore we hold our course north and that evening past the equinoctial line the second time and be close by the land anchor at twelve fathom good August but at last we get it up we be then fifteen minute northward of the line in the evening with the hard stream we go close to the land and by reason it be calm anchor in uneven ground and not spanish felt. they wear fair clothes about their middle and some have silk breeches on of diverse colour some also have wreath about their head which they say be turk or moor in religion they wear gold and silver ring upon their finger their hair be all coal black they barter their ware with we for bead but rather desire linen they be very wary and fearful of we we ask they what the name of this country be but they will not tell we but by many circumstance we judge and very believe that we be at the east end of Gilolo on the middlemost point of the land Gilolo for Gilolo reach out with
