and the seven of july 1600. I depart from Aleppo in company with many other nation as armenians Persians turk and diverse other to the number of six hundred people in our Carravan and only of english m. John Cartwright preacher from whence we go to by our which be within three day journey and stand upon the edge of the river Euphrates bir. from thence we go to Vrfa which be five day journey which we find very hot Vrfa caracmit from thence we go to caracmit which be four day journey from thence to a city under the government of a nation call the courde yet under the subjection of Constantinople which be seven day journey and from thence to van which be three day journey from van. a great lake of salt water a city of great strength and by the side of the castle be a great lake of salt water navigable and be in compass nine day journey about which I myself have row round about and once a year at the come down of the snow water from the mountain there be abundance of fish which come of themselves to one end of the lake which I may compare to our herring-time at Yermouth where the countrypeople do resort from diverse place and catch the say fish in great abundance which they salt and dry and keep they all the year for their food the fish be as big as pilchard from thence we go to nacshian which be six day journey nacshian Chiulfal Sultania Casbin com. Cashan and from nacshian to Chiulfal which be half a day journey and there we stay eighteen day from thence we go to Sultania and from thence to Casbin in Persia which be fifteen day journey and there we abide thirty day from thence to come which be three day journey from thence we go to Cashan which be seven day journey from thence m. Cartwright depart from we and go to Spauhoan the chief city in Persia from Cashan to yesd which be ten day journey from thence I go to Curman which be ten day journey yesd and from thence to Sigistam which be fourteen day journey and from thence to Candabar which be also fourteen day journey the second letter of JOHN mildenhall to m. richard staper write from Casbin in Persia the three day of October 1606. worshipful sir my duty remember not have any other of more ancient love then yourself I have think good to remember the manifold courtesy receive and partly to requite they with the first news of the success of this my voyage unto the court of the great king of Mogor and Cambaia at my arrival in Lahora the of 1603. I dispatch a post for the king court with my letter to his majesty that I may have his free leave to come unto he and treat of such business as I have to do with he from my prince who forthwith answer my letter and write to the governor of Lahora to use i with all honour and courtesy and to send a guard of horse and foot with i to accompany i to agra he arrive at agra 21 day journey from Lahora his present to the king of Mogor where his court be be one and twenty day journey from Lahora and be near arrive I be very well meet and a house with all thing necessary be appoint for i by the king where repose myself two day the three day I have audience and present his majesty with nine and twenty great horse very fair and good such as be hardly find better in those part some of they cost i fifty or threescore pound a horse with diverse jewel ring and earring to his great like and so I be dismiss with his great favour and content the three day after have make before a great man my friend he call i into his council and come into his presence he demand of i what I will have and what my business be I make he answer that his greatness and renown kindness unto christian be so much blaze through the world that it be come into the furthermost part of the western ocean and arrive in the court of our queen of England most excellent majesty this voyage be make in q Elizabeth reign who desire to have friendship with he and as the portugal and other christian have trade with his majesty so her subject also may have the same with the like favour and far because there have be long war between her majesty and the king of Portugal that if any of their ship or port be take by our nation that he will not take it in evil part but suffer we to enjoy they to the use of our queen majesty all this the king command to be write down by his secretary and say that in short space he will give i answer with that I withdraw myself with leave and go to my house within eight or ten day after he send i home in money to the value of five hundred pound sterling the first time with very comfortable speech short after as I be inform he send to certain jesuite which live there in great honour and credit two in agra and two other in Lahora and show they my demand whereat the jesuite be in a exceed great rage and whereas before we be friend now we grow to be exceed great enemy the jesuite calumniation of our nation and the king ask their opinion in this matter they flat answer he that our nation be all thief and that I be a spy send thither for no other purpose to have friendship with his majesty but that afterward our man may come thither and get some of his port and so put his majesty to much trouble say withal that they have eleven year serve his majesty and be find by their bread and salt that they have eat to speak the truth although it be against christian with these and many more such speech the king and his council be all flat against i and my demand but make no show thereof to i in any respect but I know it by friend which I have in his court. afterward they cause five commandment to be draw and send they i withal thing that I have write save they have leave out the take of the ship and the port of the portugal which when I have read I present go to the court and make demand of the other article the king answer that he will again speak with his council and make answer in this manner rest my business and every day I go to the court and in every eighteen or twenty day I put up ars or petition and still he put i off with good word and promise that this day and tomorrow I shall have they in this manner see myself delay and be at exceed great expense of eighteen or twenty servant horseman and foot I withdraw myself from go to the court in so much that in thirty day I go not at length the king remember i send to call for i at my come he ask the cause why I come not as I be wont I answer that I have come into his country only upon the great renown of his excellency and have waste five year in travail five year spend in travail and can not obtain so much as a commandment at his hand which be whole for his profit and nothing for his loss add that if I have ask some great reward of he he will much more have deny i rich garment bestow by the grand Mogor upon master John mildenhal with that he present call for garment for i of the christian fashion very rich and good and will i not to be sad because every thing that I will have shall be accomplish to my own content so with these sweet word I pass six month more and then see nothing accomplish I be exceed weary of my linger and can do nothing and the rather for that I be out of money I shall have declare before how the jesuite day and night seek how to work my displeasure first they have give to the two chief counsellor that the king have the sundry practice of the jesuite at the least five hundred pound sterling a piece that they shall not in any wise consent to these demand of i so that when I come to present they they will not accept of any thing at my hand although I offer they very large and where I have any friendship they will by all mean seek to disgrace i but God ever keep i in good reputation with all man moreover whereas I have hire in Aleppo a armenian name seffur to who I give twenty ducat the month which serve i very well for my interpreter four year now come near to the point of my special business a armenian serve he four year for interpreter the jesuite have soon wrought with he also in such sort that he quarrel with i and go his way whereby I be destitute of a drugman and myself can speak little or nothing now in what case I be in these remote country without friend money and a interpeter wiseman may judge yet afterward I get a schoolmaster and in my house day and night I so study the persian tongue he study six month the persian tongue in agra that in six month space I can speak it something reasonable then I go in great discontentment to the king and give he to understand how the jesuite have deal with i in all point and desire his majesty licence to depart for my own country where I may have redress for my injury receive and withal tell he how small it will stand with so great a prince honour as his majesty have report to be many year delay to delay i so many year only upon the report of two jesuite who I will prove be not his friend nor care not for his profit nor honour and desire a day of hear that now I myself may make plain unto his majesty which for want of a drugman before I can not do the great abuse of these jesuite in this his court beseech you again to grant i licence to depart and that I may not be keep any long with delay at these word the king be move against the jesuite and promise that upon the Sunday follow I shall be hear and that the jesuite shall be present this speech I have with the king upon the Wednesday come before the place of council the Sunday follow there be meet all the great state of the court to hear the controversy between we at the first the king call i and demand what injury I have receive of the jesuite I answer that they have abuse my prince and country most false call we all thief and if they have be of another sort and calling I will have make they eat their word or I will have lose my life in the quarrel second in say that under colour of merchandise we will invade your country and take some of your fort and put your majesty to great trouble now that your majesty may understand the untruth of these man false suggestion the queen ambassador leaguer at Constantinople know you all that her majesty have her ambassador leaguer in Constantinople and every three year most common do send a new and call home the old and at the first come of every ambassadoor she tend not they empty but with a great and princely present according whereunto her highness intent be to deal with your majesty this profit of rich present and honour like to redound to your majesty by have league of amity and intercourse with christian prince and to have their ambassador Leigers in your court these man by their crafty practice will deprive you of and our ambassador be resident as pledge in your court what dare any of our nation do against your highness or any of your subject upon these and other such like speech of i the king turn to his noble and say that all that I say be reason and so they all answer after this I demand of the jesuite before the king in these twelve year space that you have serve the king how many ambassador and how many present have you procure to the benefit of his majesty with that the king elder son stand out and say unto they name they that it be most true that in a eleven or twelve year not one come either upon ambassage or upon any other profit unto his majesty hereupon the king be very merry and laugh at the jesuite not have one word to answer then I say if it please your majesty I will not only procure a ambassador but also a present at my safe return again into your country diverse other demand and question be at that time propound by the king and his noble unto i and I answer they all in such sort as the king call his viceroy which before be by the jesuite bribe make my great enemy and command he the great Mogor grant large privilege to master John mildenhall he depart from agra John mildenhall return home ward by Casbin the italian be our enemy for seek trade in those part that whatsoever privilege or commandment I will have he shall present write they seal they and give they i without any more delay or question and so within thirty day after I have they sign to my own contentment and as I hope to the profit of my nation afterward I go and present they unto the prince his elder son and demand of he the like commandment which he most willing grant and short after be deliver unto i and so depart from the court I bring they with i into Persia which be here in Casbin with myself ready to do you any service and I will have come myself when I write this letter save that there be two italian merchant in agra that know of all my proceed who I doubt as I have good cause lest they will do i some harm in Bagdet or some other place they always be enemy to our nation that they shall find any new trade this way as to you it be well know and within four month I mean to depart by the way of moscovia where arrive I will not fail but satisfy you at large of all matter your worship to command JOHN mildenhall @. 4 the voyage of captain JOHN Davis to the eastern India pilot in a dutch ship write by himself to the right honourable my exceed good lord and master robert earl of Essex etc. right honourable and my exceed good lord my duty must advise i to present this journal of my east indian voyage to your lordship most judicial view wherein I have use my best diligence to discharge my duty as near as my slender capacity can effect the same according to those direction which your lordship give i in charge at my departure when it please you to employ i in this voyage for the discover of these eastern part of the world to the service of her majesty and the good of our country what I have see I do signify in this journal to your lordship and that which I have learn by the report of other nation when it shall please God to make i happy by your lordship favourable presence I will make far know to your lordship aswell of the king of Portugal his place of trade and strength as of the interchangeable trade of those eastern nation among themselves beginning at Cefala which be his first foot beyond the cape of esperanza and so proceed to Mosambique Ormus Diu Goa onor mangalor Cocbin Columbo Negapatan Porto grande in Bengala and malacca as also to the city of Macao in the province of canton in the famous kingdom of China and to the land of the and Amboyno which place be all in the portugal possession serve for his security and refuge moreover he have trade in Monomotapa melinde Ad^n Arabia Cambaia on the coast of coromandel balaguate and Orixa of all which nation there be some dwell in Achen in the i will of sumatra trade in merchandise where I have meet with arabian and a nation call Rumos who have trade many hundred year to Achen these Rumos * * Constantinople be call new Rome and thence in the east the turk be call Rumos of that their chief city come from the red Sea there be in Achen many chinese that use trade of who I have be kind use and can well inform your lordship of that worthy kingdom of China the trade of Gusarate be very ample all which the portugal with the lock of discretion have provident long conceal which now through God favour be make know unto we I have here enclose send your lordship the alphabet of the achen language with some word of the same which they write after the manner of the hebrew I have also send by master Tomkins of their coin which be in usual payment that of gold be name a master and be nine penny half penny near those of lead be call Caxas whereof a thousand six hundred make one mas. good my lord remember the poor widow mite for sure if I can do more in this service or otherwise it shall not be omit from Middleborough this first of August 1600. your lordship most dutiful servant JOHN Davis a brief relation of master JOHN Davis chief pilot to the zelander in their East-India voyage depart from Middleborough the fifteen of march 1598. the fifteen hereof we depart from Flushing with two ship in consort the lion and lioness the lion be four hundred tun have in she a hundred three and twenty person the lioness two hundred and fifty tun have a hundred person mushroom clerk and monef of Middleborough owner and only adventurer thereof Cornelius Howteman chief commander of both ship have a commission from grave Maurice by the name general the two and twenty we anchor in Tor bay with bad wind the seven we set sail the twenty we have sight of Porto santo the three and twenty we fall with Palma the last hereof we come with the island of cape Verde April the first we anchor at saint Nicholas one of the say land in latitude sixteen degree sixteen minute here we water the seven we depart the nine may. we fall with saint jago the nine we fall with the coast of Brasill in seven degree of south latitude not be able to double cape saint Augustine for be about the line we have very unconstant weather june and bad wind Fernando Loronha be in this desperate case we shape our course for a small i will name Fernando Loronha in four degree of south latitude the fifteen we anchor upon the north-side thereof in eighteen fathom we find in this island twelve negro eight man four woman it be a very fruitful isle and have exceed good water it abound with goat it have also beef hog hen melon and guinea corn with plenty of fish and sea-bird these negro be place here by the portugal to manure the i will three year pass in which there have no ship be with they the six and twenty we depart from this i will the wind at east north-east the last hereof we double cape saint Augustine August the ten we pass the abrollos which be the great of our fear the shold lie from the coast of Brasill far off into the sea in one and twenty degree and be dangerous September abrollos whereupon our baase for so a dutch captain be call choose a master of misrule by the name Kesar now the authority of riot lie in this disorder officer who after dinner can neither salute his friend nor understand the law of reason and those that aught to have be most respective be both lawless and witless in this dissolute manner we waste three day which be end and have again recover our former discretion we shape our course for cape Bona esperanza sail towards the court of Bacchus unto who this idolatrous sacrifice be make as by the end appear November bay of Soldania the eleven we anchor in the bay of Saldania in thirty four degree of the south Pole ten league short of cape Bona esperanza where there be three fresh river the people come to we with ox and sheep in great plenty which they sell for piece of old iron and spike nail the best of that we buy cost not more than the value of one penny in old iron their cattle be large and under several mark have upon the back by the fore shoulder a great lump of flesh like a camel back their sheep have exceed great tail only of fat weigh twelve or fourteen pound they have no wool but a long shag hair the people be not circumcise their colour be olive black black than the brasilian their hair curl and black as the negro of angola their word be for the most part in-articulate and in speak they clock with the tongue like a brood hen which clock and the word be both pronounce together very strange they go all naked have only a short cloak of skin and sandal tie to their foot they paint their face with diverse colour they be a strong active people and run exceed and be subject to the king of Monomotapa who be report to be a mighty king their weapon be only hard dart the fleming offer they some rude wrong they absent themselves three day in which time they make great fire upon the mountain in the country the nineteen hereof there come great troop of they to we bring very much cattle with they and in the time of barter sudden take their advantage they set upon we and stew thirteen of our people with hand dart which at four pike length can not offend notwithstanding the fleming flee before they like mouse before cat throw away their weapon most base and our baase to save himself stay aboard and send we corslet two-hand-sword pike musket and target so we be arm and lade with weapon but there be neither courage nor discretion for we stay by our tent be belegr with cannibal and cow we be in muster giant with great arm body but in action babe with wren heart hereupon master Tomkins and myself undertake to order these fellow m. Tomkins Englishman from that excellent method which we have see in your lordship most honourable action some consent to we but the most part unwilling and diverse run to the pottage pot for they swear it be dinner time this night we go all aboard only leave our great mastiff dog behind we who by no mean will come to we for I think he be ashamed of our company this land be a good soil and a wholesome air full of good herb as mint Calamint Plantine Ribwort scabious and such like the seven and twenty we set sail the last hereof we double cape Bona esperanza December the six we double cape which be the most southerly promontory of Africa where the compass have no variation this cape lie in thirty five degree of the south Pole january 1599 1599 the six we fall with the i will Madagascar short of cape Romano we spend this month to double that cape Madagascar February bay of saint Augustine not be able we bear room with the bay saint Augustine which lie upon the south west part of Madagascar in three and twenty degree fifty minute the three we anchor in the same bay where we see many people upon the shore but when we land they flee from we for the other voyage our baase be in this bay where he great abuse the people and take one of they find he to a post and shoot he to death with other shameful disorder after seven day by much mean that we make some of they come to we and bring we milk and one cow which we buy and after will no more abide we they be a strong well-shaped people and coal black their language sweet and please their weapon halfepike head with iron as a harpon which they keep very bright they go whole naked the country seem to be very fruitful and have great store of Tamaryn tree we find beanes grow upon a high tree the cod be two foot long with answerable bigness and be very good meat here be many chameleon it be no small misery that we english endure especial in this Bay but God the everliving commander be our only succour the eight we come aboard dog hungry and meatlesse the fourteen we set sail from this place which we name hungry bay shape our course upon the north side of the i will the nine and twenty we come with the island Comoro March hungry Bay isle Comoro five lie between twelve and thirteen degree and be five land Mayotta saint Christopher Spirito Sancto the thirty we anchor at Mayotta close by a town where we find many have Rice ox goat orange lemon and citron the inhabitant be negro but smooth haired in religion mahometist their weapon be sword target bow and arrow these island be please in sight and fruitful in island Mascarenhas by the shold do Almirante the three and twenty we fall with the island of Maldivia may. Maldivia which be very low close by the water whole cover with tree so that we see the tree but not the shore here we anchor and refresh ourselves many of the country boats pass by we but none will come to we whereupon our baase send out the ship boat to take one of they the four and twenty they bring a boat aboard we cover with mat like a close barge in this boat be a gentleman and his wife he be apparel in very fine white linen after the turkish manner in his ring be rich stone his behaviour be so sweet and affable his countenance so modest and his speech so graceful as that it make apparent show he can not be less than a nobleman he be unwilling to have his wife see notwithstanding our baase go with he into his boat to see she he also open her casket wherein be some jewel and ambergreese he report that she sit with mournful modesty not uong one word what be take from they I know not but in depart this gentleman show a princely spirit his colour be black with smooth hair a man of middle stature in these island there be great trade by reason of the for they make rope cable sail wine oil and a kind of bread of that tree and his fruit they report that there be 11000. of these island the seven and twenty we set sail this morning there come a old man aboard we that speak a little Portugal he be our pilot through the channel for by chance we fall with the true passable channel name Maldivia in latitude four degree fifteen minute of the north-pole where the compass be vary seventeen degree westerly in miss this channel it be a dangerous place the trade of ship be in this country a kind of seed whereof a little be eat a strange se^d and strange treachery make a man to turn fool all thing seem to he to be metamorphose but above a certain rate it be deadly poison with this all the meat and drink which they bring be infect in banquet the sabandar and secretary send for i m. Tomkins keep i company and use some word to one of his company but what I know not in short time we be foole-frolicke gape one upon a other like antic our baase be prisoner and know it not sudden when a token be give from the other ship for there the like treachery be use by the secretary who go from our ship thither to act the same they set upon we murder our baase and slay diverse other m. Tomkins myself and a Frenchman defend the poop which if they have recover our ship have be lose for they have the cabin and some be below among the ordnance by creep in at the port the master of our ship which they call captain leap into the sea so do diverse other but recover the ship again and come aboard when all be do in the end we put they to flight for our top plague they sore which when I see I leap from the poop to pursue they m. Tomkins leap after i there come a Turk out of the cabin and wound he grievous they lay together tumble each for his life which see I run the Turk in with my rapier and our shipper present with a half pike thrust he down the throat into the body in the other ship all the chief be murder and the ship take we cut our cable and drive to she and with our shot make the indian fly so we recover the ship the galley dare not come near we in this great misery it be some pleasure to see how the base indian do fly how they be kill and how well they be drown the sea be cover with indian head for they swim away by hundred the sabandare Abdala and one of the king near kinsman be slay with many other and the secretary hurt the king be by the seaside with many people when the news come of the sabandar death and their great overthrow the furious infidel murder all our man a shore only eight except who the king fetter for slave we lose in this misfortune threescore and eight person of which we be not a pinnace for rice hope to have news of she but have not the second there come eleven galley with portugal as we think to take our ship we sink one and beat the rest so they flee this afternoon come aboard we the son of lafort a french merchant dwell in seething-lane who be one of the eight prisoner with this message from the King shame you not to be such drunken beast as in drunkenness to murder and fertile soil abound with many rare and excellent fruit of grain they have only rice which be their Bread they plow the ground with buffs of which there be great plenty but with small skill and less diligence Rice the rice grow in all respect as our barley of pepper they have exceed plenty garden of a mile square pepper it grow like hop from a plant root and wind above a stake set by it until it grow to a great bushy tree the pepper hang in small cluster three inch long and a inch about each cluster have forty pepper corn it yield increase equal with mustard seed they be able to lade twenty ship yearly and more might if the people be industrious and laboursome the whole country seem to be a garden of pleasure the air be temperate and wholesome have every morning a fruitful dew or small rain the haven that go to the city of Achien be small have but six foot at the bar and there stand a fort make of stone round without cover battlement or flanker low wall like a pound a worse can be conceive before this fort be a very pleasant road for ship the wind still come from the shore a ship may ride a mile off in eighteen fathom close by in four and six fathom of beast here be elephant horse buff ox and goat with many wild hog the land have plenty of gold and copper mine diverse kind of gum balm mine of gold and other commodity and many kind of drug and much indigo of stone there be ruby saphire and garnets but I know not that they grow there they have pass good timber for ship the city of Achien if it may be so call be very spacious build in a wood city so that we can not see a house till we be upon it neither can we go into any place but we find house and great concourse of people so that I think the town spread over the whole land their house be build eight foot or better from the ground upon post of wood with free passage under the wall and cover of mat the poor and weak thing in the World I see three great market place which be every day frequent as fair with all kind of merchandise to sell. the king be call sultan Aladin and be a hundred year old as they say sultan Aladin yet he be a lusty man but exceed gross and fat in the begin of his life he be a fisherman of which this place have very many for they live most upon fish and go to the war with the former king show himself so valiant and discreet in order the king galley that gain the king favour he be make admiral of his sea-force and by his valour and discretion the king so embrace he that he give he to wife one of his near kinswoman the king have one only daughter marry she to the king of jor by who she have a son this child be send to Achien to be nourish under his grandfather be heir to the kingdom the king that now be be now chief commander both by land and Sea the old king sudden die this king take the protection of the child against which the nobility resist but he have the king force and take opportunity end the life of more than a thousand nobleman and gentleman and of the rascal people make new lord and new law in fine the child be murder and then he proclaim himself king by the right of his wife hereupon arise great war between he and the king of jor which continue to this day these twenty year he have by force hold the kingdom and now seem to be secure in the same his court be from the city half a mile upon the river have three guard before any can come to he and a great Greene between each guard his house be build as the rest be but much high he sit where he can see all that come to any of his guard but none can see he the wall and cover of his house be mat which sometime be hang with cloth of gold sometime with velvet and sometime with damask he sit upon the ground crosslegged like a tailor and so must all those do that be in his presence he always wear four Cresis two before and two behind exceed rich with diamond and ruby and have a sword lie upon his lap he have attend upon he forty woman at the least some with fan to cool he some with clothes to dry his sweat some give he other water the rest sing pleasant song he do nothing all the day but eat and drink from morning to night there be no end of banquet and when his belly be ready to break than he eat Arecca Betula which be a fruit like a nutmeg wrap in a kind of leaf like tobacco with sharp chalk make of pearl oyster-shel chaw this it make the spittle very red draw the rheum exceed and procure a mighty stomach this make the tooth very black and they be the brave that have the black tooth by this mean get again his stomach he go with a fresh courage to eat and for a change with a crack gorge he go into the river where he have a place make of purpose there get a stomach by be in the water he his great man and woman do nothing but eat drink and talk of venery if the poet fable have any show of truth then undoubted this king be the great Bacchus for he hold all the ceremony of gluttony as in all place of Europe the custom be by uncover the head to show reverence in this place it be whole contrary for before any man can come to the king presence he must put of his hose and shoe and come before he barelegged and barefooted hold the palm of the hand together and heave they up above his head bow with the body must say which do duty be discharge and so he sit down crosslegged in the king presence he do only spend the time in eat with woman and cockfighting and such as be the king such be his subject for the whole land be give to no other contentment his state be govern by five principal man with their inferior officer his secretary and four call sabandar with these rest all authoritie^ the king will be their Law for it seem there be no freeman in the land for the life and good of all be at the king pleasure he will make no offender happy by death but cut off their hand and foot and banish they to a i will name polo-wey if he put any to death the elephant tear he to piece or they drive a stake into his fundament and so he die there be jail and many fetter prisoner that go about the town his woman be his chief counsellor he have three wife and very many concubine which be very close keep he have very many galley I think a hundred some that will carry four hundred man make like a wherrie very long and open without deck forecastle chase or any upper building their oar be like shovel of four foot long which they use only with the hand not rest they upon the galley they bear no ordnance with these he keep his neighbour in obedience a woman be his admiral for he will trust no man their weapon be bow arrow javelin sword target they have no defensive arm but fight naked he have great store of brass ordnance which they use without carriage shoot they as they lie upon the ground they be the great that I have ever see and the mettle be report to be rich of Gold the trust of his land force stand upon his elephant these people boast themselves to come of Ishmael and Hagar and can reckon the genealogy of the bible perfect in religion they be mahometist and pray with bead as the papist do they bring up their child in learning and have many school they have a archbishop and spiritual dignity here be a prophet in Achien who they great honour they say that he have the spirit of prophecy as the ancient have have he be disguise from the rest in his apparel and great embrace of the King the people be general very cunning merchant and whole dedicate thereunto of mechanical artesman they have goldsmith gun-founder shipwrights tailor wever hatter pot-maker and aquavitae stiller which be make of Rice for they must drink no wine cutler and smith as touch their burial every generation or kindred have their particular place to bury their dead which be in the field they lay the corpse with the head towards Mecha have a free stone at the head and another at the foot curious wrought thereby signify the worthiness of the person but in the place of the king burial every grave have a piece of gold at the head and another at the foot weigh at the least five hundred poun^ weight cunning emboss and wrought this king have two such piece in make and almost finish which we see that be a thousand pound weight a piece and shall be rich set with stone I do great desire to see the king burial because of the great wealth therein but can not I do almost believe it to be true because this king have make two such costly monument the people that trade in this place be of China Bengala Pegu java coromandel Gusarate the turk be call Rumos in the indies the reason of that name be their metropolitan and imepriall city WILLIAM Adams his voyage by the Magellan straits to * * this voyage though not by the cape of good hope yet because it be to japon I here deliver see before pag. 78. japon write in two letter by himself as follow have so good occasion by hear that certain english merchant lie in the island of java although by name unknown I presume to write these few life desire the worshipful company be unknown to i to pardon my boldness the reason that I write be first for that conscience bind i to love my country and my countryman your worship therefore shall understand to who these present shall come that I be a kentish-man bear in a town call Gillingam two english mile from Rochester one mile from Chattam where the king ship lie and that from the age of twelve year I be bring up in limehouse near London be prentice twelve year to one master Nicholas Diggines and have serve in the place of master and pilot in her majesty ship and about eleven or twelve year serve the worshipful company of the Barbary merchant until the indian traffic from Holland begin in which indian traffic I be desirous to make a little experience of the small knowledge which God have give i so in the year of our lord God 1598. I be hire for chief pilot of a fleet of five sail which be make ready by the chief of the indian company Peter Vanderhag and Hance Vanderuek^ the general of this fleet be a marchatt call jaques Mayhay in which ship be admiral I be Pilot. so it be the three and twenty or four and twenty of june before we set sail * * Adam chief pilot of a fleet of five sail it be somewhat too late ere we come to the line to pass it without contrary wind for it be about the midst of September at which time we find much southerly wind and many of our man be sick so that we be force to go to the coast of gynny to cape Lopo Gonsalues cape Lopo Gonsalues where we set our sick man a land whereof many die and of the sickness few better have little or no refresh and the place be unhealthy therefore to fulfil our voyage we set our course for the coast of Brasill determine to pass the straits of Magellan and by the way come to a island call Nobon at which island we land and take the town which contain about eighty house in which island we refresh ourselves have ox orange the isle of Nobon take and diverse other fruit but the unwholsomenesse of the air be such that as one better another fell sick we spend upon the coast of the cape Gonsalues and of Annobon about two month time till the twelve or thirteen of November at which time we set sail from Annobon find the wind still at the south by east and south southeast till we get four degree by south the line at which time the wind favour we come to the southeast and east southeast and east so that we be up between the island of Annobon and the straits of Magellan about five month one of our five sail spend her main mast by which we be much hinder for with much travel we set a new mast in the Sea then the nine and twenty of march we see the land in the latitude of fifty degree have the wind two or three day contrary so in the end have the wind good we come into the straits of Magellan the six of April 1599 at which time the winter come so that there be much snow April 6. 1599 and our man through cold on the one side and hunger on the other grow weak we have the wind at north-east some five or six day in which time we may have pass through the straits but for refresh of our man we wait water and take in of wood and set up of a pinnace of fifteen or sixteen ton in bigness at length we will have pass through but can not by reason of the southerly wind with wet and also very cold with abundance of snow and ice wherefore we be force to winter and stay in the straits from the six of April until the four and twenty of September they winter in the s^aights of Magellan in which time the most part of our provision be spend in so much that for lack of victual many of our man die through hunger now have pass through the straits and come into the south sea we find many hard stream be drive to the southward in fifty four degree be then very cold at length we find reasonable wind and weather with which we follow our pretend voyage towards the coast of Peru but in long travel we lose our whole fleet be separate the one from the other yet before the disperse of our fleet we have appoint if we lose one another with storm and foul weather that in chili in the latitude of forty six degree many of their man die for want of food they stay in forty six degree and refresh themselves the mouth of Baldivia the isle of Mocha we shall stay one for another the space of thirty day in which height according to agreement I go in six and forty degree and stay eight and twenty day where we refresh ourselves find the people of the country good of nature but by reason of the spaniard they will not have deal with we at the first they bring we sheep and potato for which we give they bell and knife whereof they be very glad but in the end the people go up from their house into the country and come no more unto we we stay there eight and twenty day and set up a pinnace which we have in our ship in four part and in the end depart and come to the mouth of Baldivia yet by reason it blow much wind we enter not but direct our course out of the bay for the island of Mocha unto the which we come the next day find none of our Fleet. so not find they we direct our course for the island of Maria and the next day we come by the cape which be a league and a half from the island and see many people toss about the cape and find good ground anchor in fifteen fathom in a fair sandy Bay a fair sandy Bay we go with our boat hard by the water side to parley with the people of the land but they will not suffer we to come a land shoot great store of arrow at our man nevertheless have no victual in our ship and hope to find refresh we forcible land some seven and twenty or thirty of our man and drive the wild people from the water side have most of our man hurt with their arrow they be on land we make sign of friendship and in the end come to parley with sign and token of friendship which the people understand so we make sign that our desire be to have victual for iron silver and cloth which we show they wherefore they give our folk wine with to eat and other fruit and bid our man by sign and token to go aboard and the next day to come again and then they will bring we victual so be late our man come aboard the most part of they be hurt more or less and yet we be very glad that we have come to a parley with they hope that we shall get refresh the nine of November 1599 the next day be the nine of November 1599 our captain with all our officer prepare to go a land have take counsel to go to the water side but not to land more than two or three man for there be people in abundance and be also unknown our man therefore be w^lled not to trust they this counsel be conclude the captain himself go in one of our boat with all the force that we have and be by the shore side the people of the country make sign that they shall come a land but that do not like our captain well in the end the people come not near unto our boat our captain with the rest resolve to land against that which be conclude in our ship before the go on land at length three and twenty man land with musket and march up towards four or five house and when they be about a musket-shot from the boat more than a thousand indian who lay entrench immediate fall upon our man with such weapon as they have and kill they all to our knowledge so our boat wait long to see if any of they will come again twenty three man slay but see no hope to recover they our boat return with this sorrowful news that all our man that land be slay which be a lamentable thing to hear for we have scarce so many man leave as can wind up our anchor the isle of maria. the next day we wait and go over to the island Maria where we find our admiral who have arrive there four day before we and depart to the isle from Mucha the day before we come from thence have the general master and all his officer wound on land and God have so plague we that all our officer be slay so that the one of we bemoan the other nevertheless be glad that we be come together my good friend Timothy shotten be pilot in that Ship be at the island of Maria Timothy shotten of the emperor call i again he be call the second time demand the reason of our come so far I answer we be a people that seek all friendship with all nation and to have trade of merchandise in all country bring such merchandize as our country have and buy such merchandize in strange country as our country desire through which our country on both side be enrich he ask much concern the war crucify the usual punishment of malefactor in japan the je^uites and portugal accusation nor of the rest of the company in which time I look every day to be cross as the custom of justice be in japan as hang be in our land now in this long time of imprisonment the jesuite and the portugal give many evidence to the emperor against we allege that we be thief and robber of all nation and if we be suffer to live it shall be against the profit of his majesty and the land for than no nation can come there without rob but if justice be execute on we it will terrify the rest of our nation from come there any more and to this intent they sue to his majesty daily to cut we off make all the friend they can to this purpose but God be merciful unto we and will not suffer they to have their will of we at length the emperor give they this answer that as yet we have do no hurt or damage to he nor to any of his land the emperor answer and therefore that it be against reason and justice to put we to death and if our country and they have war one with the other that be no cause that he shall put we to death the emperor answer they in this manner they be quite out of heart that their cruel pretence fail for the which God be praise for ever and ever now in this time that I be in prison the ship be command to be bring so near to the city where the emperor be as she may the which be do so the one and forty day of my imprisonment the emperor call i before he again he be call the three time before the emperor demand of i many question more which be too long to write in conclusion he ask i man to live upon two pound rice a day and yearly so much as be worth eleven or twelve ducat a year myself the captain and mariner all alike so in process of four or five year the emperor call i and as for the emperor say he if it be not good it be no matter wherefore at his command I build he a ship of the burden of eighty ton or there abouts which ship be make in all proportion as our manner be he come aboard to see it like it very well by which mean I come in more favour which he so that I come often in his presence who from time to time give i present and at length a yearly revenue to live upon the emperor bestow a yearly revenue on he of 70. ducat and two pound of Rice a day much about seventy ducat by the year with two pound of Rice a day also now be in such grace and favour by reason I learn he some point of geometry and the mathematics with other thing I please he so that what I say can not be contradict at which my former enemy jesuite and portugal do great wonder and entreat i to be friend they to the emperor in their business and so by my mean both spaniard and portugal have receive friendship from the emperor I recompense their evil unto i with good so to pass my time to get my live it have cost i great labour and travel at the first but God have bless my labour in the end of five year I make supplication to the king to go out of this land desire to see my poor wife and child according to conscience and nature with the which request the emperor be not well please and will not let i go any more for my country but that I must continue in his land etc. yet in process of time be in great favour with the emperor I make supplication again by reason we have news that the hollander be in Ache^ and Patania which rejoice we much with hope that God shall bring we to our country again by one mean or other then I make supplication again and bold speak myself with he at which he give i no answer I tell he if he will permit i to depart I will be a mean that both the english and hollander shall come and traffic there in his land he answer that he be desirous of both those nation company for traffic but will not part with i by any mean but bid i write to that purpose see therefore I can not prevail for myself he obtain liberty for the captain I sue that my captain may depart which suit he present grant i so have get his liberty he embark in a japan junck and sail to Patane but he tarry there a year space wait for Holland ship and see none come he go from Patane to jor where he find a fleet of nine sail of which fleet matleef be general and in this fleet he be make master again which fleet sail to malacca and fight with a armado of portugal in which battle he be shoot and present die so that as yet I think no certain news be know the captain slay at malacca whether I be live or dead therefore my desire be that my wife and two child may hear that I be here in japan so that my wife be in a manner a widow and my child fatherless which thing only be my great grief of heart and conscience etc. I be a man not unknown in Ratcliff and limehouse to my good master m. Nicholas Diggines and m. Thomas best and m. Nicholas Isaac and William Isaac brother with many other also to m William jones and m. give i a live like unto a lordship in England with eighty or ninety husbandman who be as my servant and slave the like precedent be never do to any stranger before thus God have provide for i after my great misery his name have and have the praise for ever amen now whether I shall come out of this land I know not until this present there have be no mean but now through the trade of the hollander there be mean in the year of our lord 1609. two holland ship come to japan their intention be to take the carrack two ship of Holland come to japan in the year 1609. that yearly come from Macao and be some five or six day too late nevertheless they come to Firando and come to the court to the emperor where they be in great friendship receive condition with the emperor yearly to send a ship or two and so they depart with the emperor pass now this year 1611. there be a small ship arrive with cloth another small ship of Holland arrive there 1611. lead elephant tooth damask and black tafficies raw silk pepper and other commodity and they have show cause why they miss the former year 1610. according to promise yearly to come this ship be well receive and with great kindness entertain you shall understand that the hollander have here a indies of money for they need not to bring silver out of Holland in to the east indies for in japan there be much silver and gold in japan commodity vendible for ready money there be much silver and gold to serve their turn in other place where need require in the east indies but the merchandise which be here vendible for ready money be raw silk damask black taffity black and red cloth of the best lead and such like good so now understand by this Holland ship late arrive here that there be a settle trade drive by my countryman in the east indies I presume that among they some either merchant master or mariner must needs know i therefore I have embolden myself to write these few line in short be desirous not to be over-tedious to the reader this island of japan be a great land the length and breadth of japan and lie to the northwards in the latitude of eight and forty degree and the souther-most part of it in five and thirty degree and the length of it east by north and west and by south for so it lie be two hundred and twenty english league the breadth south and north of it thirteen degree twenty league to the degree be two hundred sixty league and be almost square the disposition of people the people of this island of japan be good of nature courteous above measure and valiant in war their justice be severe execute without any partiality upon transgressor of the Law they be govern in great civility I think no land better govern in the world by civil policy the people be very superstitious in their religion and be of diverse opinion many jesuite and franciscan friar in japan there be many jesuite and franciscan friar in this land and they have convert many to be christian and have many church in the island thus in short I be constrain to write hope that by one mean or other in process of time I shall hear of my wife and child and so with patience I wait the good will and pleasure of God almighty desire all those to who this my letter shall come to use the mean to acquaint my good friend with it that so my wife and child may hear of i by which mean there may be hope that I may hear of my wife and child before my death the which the lord grant to his glory and my comfort amen date in japan the two and twenty of October 1611. by your unworthy friend and servant to command in what I can william Adams endorse to my unknown friend and countryman desire this letter by your good mean or the news or copy of this letter may come to the hand of one or many of my acquaintance in limehouse or elsewhere or in Kent in Gillingham by Rochester a letter of WILLIAM Adams to his wife from japan love wife you shall understand how all thing have pass with i from the time of my absence from you we set sail with five ship from the texel in Holland the four and twenty of june 1598. and depart from the coast of England the five of july and the one and twenty of August we come to one of the isle of Capo Verde call Sant' jago the isle of cape Verde where we abide four and twenty day in which time many of our man fall sick through the unwholsomenesse of the air and our general among the rest now the reason that we abide so long at these land be that one of the captain of our fleet make our general believe that at these land we shall find great store of refresh as goat and other thing which be untrue here I and all the pilot of the fleet be call to a council in which we all show our judgement of dislike the place which be by all the captain take so ill that afterward it be agree by they all that the pilot shall be no more in the council the which be execute the fifteen day of September we depart from the isle of Sant' jago and pass the equinoctial line and in the latitude of three degree to the south our general die their general die wherewith many contrary wind and rain the season of the year be very much pass we be force upon the coast of guiney fall upon a head-land call cabo the new general command to bear up with cape de Lopo consalue cabo in guiney Capo de Lopo consalue Nobon take by the hollander there to seek refresh for our man the which we do in which place we land all our sick man where they do not much better for we can find no store of victual the nine and twenty of December we set sail to go on our voyage and in our way we fall with a island call Nobon where we land all our sick man take the island in by force their town contain some eighty house have refresh our man we set sail again at which time our general command that a man for four day shall have but one pound of bread that be a quarter of a pound a day with the like proportion of wine and water which scarcity of victual bring such feebleness that our man fall into so great weakness and sickness for hunger that they do eat the calf skin April 3. 1599 the straight of Magellan wherewith our rope be cover the three of April 1599 we fall with the port of saint julian and the six of April we come into the straight of Magellan to the first narrow and the eight day we pass the second narrow with a good wind where we come to a anchor and land on penguin island where we lade our boat full of penguin which be fowl great than a D^cke wherewith we be great refresh the ten we weigh anchor have much wind which be good for we to go through but our general will water and take in provision of wood for all our fleet in which straight there be enough in every place with anchor ground in al^ place three or four league one from another in the mean time the wind change and come southerly so we seek a good harbour for our ship on the north-side a good harbour four league of Elizabeth Bay all April be out we have wonderful much snow and ice with great wind for in April May june july and August be the winter there be in fifty two degree 1/^ by south the equinoctial many time in the winter we have the wind good to go through the straits but our general will not we abide in the straight till the four another that storm be long we be drive into the latitude of fifty four degree 1/^ by south the equinoctial the weather break up and have good wind again the nine of October we see the admiral of which Mar^a th^y meet with their admiral the general and 27. man slay at Mocha where we find our admiral who when we see our heart be somewhat comfort we go aboard they and find they in as great distress as we have lose their general with seven and twenty of their man slay at the island of Mocha from whence they depart the day before we come by here we take counsel what we shall do to get victual to go on land by force we have no man for the most part be sick there come a Spaniard by composition to see our ship and so the next day he come again and we let he depart quiet the three day come two spaniard aboard we without pawn to see if they can betray we when they have see our ship they will have go on land again but we will not let they show that they come without leave and we will not let they go on land again without our leave whereat they we^e great offend we show they that we have extreme need of victual and that if they will give we so many sheep and so many beef they shall go on land so against their will they make composition with we which within the time appoint they do accomplish have so much refresh as we can get we make all thing well again our man be for the most part recover of their sickness there be a young man one Hudcopee which know nothing but have serve the admiral who be make general and the master of our ship be make vice-admiral who name be jacob Quaternak of Rotterdam so the general and vice-admiral call i and the other pilot be a Englishman call Timothy shotten which have be with m. from the cow in the i will of wight the three and twenty we arrive at teneriffe in the road of Aratana the fourteen of january at night we be trouble with extreme heat lightning thunder and rain all the night the sixteenth we pass under the equinoctial line shape our course for the i will Loronnah the wind be at south southeast our course south south-west and some three degree southward of the line we meet with such multitude of fish as it be incredible to report so that with our hook line and harp iron we take so many dolphines bonito and other fish that our man be so weary with eat of fish that we can not tell what to do with it moreover there be fowl call pasharabove and Alcatrarzes we take many of those pasharabove for it be a foul that delight to come to a ship in the night and if you do but hold up your hand they will light upon it the other foul call Alcatrarzi be a kind of hawk that live by fish for when the bonito or dolphines do chase the fly fish under the water so that he be glad to flee from they out of the water to save his life pasharabove this Alcatrarzi fly after they like a hawk a partridge of these fly fish I have see so many flee together that you will have think they to be a great flock of bird afar off they be but little fish scarce so big as a hear the i will of Fernando de Loronnah the two and twenty we come to a anchor at the i will of Loronnah be four degree to the southward of the line where in go on shore our Skiffe be overset by reason of the violent breach that the sea make at which time be drown a kinsman of our general call master Richard Michelburne and all the rest be save the five and twenty our long boat go to fill some empty cask with water come again within the danger of that unfortunate sea and be overset and two more of our man drown here we be very (@) trouble in get wood and water aboard because the land be so dangerous that (@) be force to pull our cask on shore with rope and so back again when it be fill not six day before we come hither there be a Hollander here which send his boat for water which be break all into piece against the rock and his man brain beat out and their arm and leg cut from their body the six and twenty our general go on shore to see the island and march up and down in the same we find nothing but a wild country inhabit only by six negro which live like slave in this island have be great store of goat and some wild ox but by reason the Portugal carake sometime use to water here when they go into the east indies and that these poor slave be leave there as their servant to kill and dry goat against their come thither they have destroy both goat and ox so that we can find but few in this island be great store of turtle-dove Alcatrarzes and other fowl which we kill with our piece and find they to be very dainty meat also here be good store of Maiz or Guynie wheat here be likewise plenty of rot tree whereon grow the fine bombast and abundance of wild goard and water-melon when we be furnish with wood and water we come aboard the twelve of February we find ourselves to be in seven degree five minute to the southward in which place at night I think I see the strange sea that ever be see which be a strange glitter of the Sea that the burn or glitter light of the sea do show to we as though all the sea over have be burn flame of fire and all the night long the moon be down you may see to read in any book by the light thereof the thirteen day in the morning we descry a island or rather indeed a rock the name be Ascention the height eight degree thirty minute to the southward the first of April towards night we descry land from the main top which bear of we south southeast when according to our reckon and account April we be not near by forty league but yet the variation of the compass do tell we that we be on land thirty league before we see land the second day in the morning we be hard by the shore which be ten or twelve league to the northward of the bay of Saldannah the three day we sail by a little island which captain John davis take to be a island that stand some five or six league from Saldannah whereupon our general sir Edward Michelburne desirous to see the island take his Skiffe accompany with no more than the master mate the purser and myself and four man that do row the boat and so put off from the ship we come on land while we be on shore they in the ship have a storm which drive they out of sight of the island and we be two day and two night before we can recover our Ship upon the say island be abundance of great coney island coney and seal whereupon we call it coney island the eight day we come to a anchor in the road of Saldannah the nine we go on shore find a goodly country they land in the road of Saldannah inhabit by a most savage and beastly people as ever I think God create in this place we have excellent good refresh in so much that I think the like place be not to be find among savage people for we neither want beef mutton nor wildfowl all the time we lay there this country be very full of ox and sheep which they keep in great herd and flock as we do our cattle in England moreover it do abound with store of wild beast and fowl as wild deer in great abundance Antelops babious fox and hare ostrich crane pelican heron goose duck pheasant partridge and diverse other sort of excellent fowl of which fowl we kill great store with our piece it be also most pleasant water with wholesome spring which have their beginning from the top of exceed high mountain exceed high mountain which fall into the valley make they very fruitful also there be a kind of tree not much unlike to bay tree but of a far hard substance that grow close by the sea side the people of the country bring we more bullock and sheep than we can spend all the time we stay there so that we carry fresh beef and mutton to sea with we for a piece of a old iron hoop not worth two penny you may buy a great bullock and for a piece of iron not worth two or three good horse nail you may buy a sheep they go naked save only they wear upon their shoulder a sheep skin and before their privity a little flap of a skin their woman some be well feature some of their man have but one stone copper be now in great request with they a certain kind of root may. the cape Bona esperanza cape Das Agu^lhas which cover as much as though they have none at all before they in the time of our be there they live upon the gut and filth of the meat which we do cast away feed in most beastly manner for they will neither wash nor make clean the raw flesh and a certain kind of root which they have which grow there in great abundance in this place we lie on shore from the nine of April until the three of may. by which good recreation and they find in double of this cape in the extremity of our storm appear to we in the night upon our main topmast head a flame about the bigness of a great candle which the portugal call hold it a most land of the great island of sumatra here we send off our boat to get some fresh water but the sea go with such a violent breach upon the shore that they dare not land the people of this island make
