DAVID MIDLETON to java and Banda extract out of a letter write by himself to the company this be the five voyage set forth by they @. i. their affair at Bantam Botun Bengaia we set sail in the down the four and twenty of April 1609. in the expedition of London April 24. 1609. they arrive at Saldania they arrive at Bantam and get sight of forteventure and the Lansarot the nineteen of May and with such wind as blow some fair some fowl we arrive at Saldania the ten of August and water and make haste and set sail the eighteen of the same we proceed for Bantam and arrive there the seven of December miss captain keeling very narrow that we have not sight of he for he pass we in the night by the alteration of state their debt be almost desperate nor will this governor suffer they as before themselves to imprison debtor and distrain he also exact unreasonable sum for rent whereas the ground have be give and the house build at the company charge else we shall have sure see he as for our business I make all the dispatch that may be both by day and night to get the iron a shore and will not stay to set up my pinnace and leave m. Hensworth in the house and be drive to give a great many of gift more than be requisite if the state of the country have be as in former time and leave Edward neetle and three more of my company with master hemsworth as his desire be be in a strange place and know none in the house so I take such commodity as I think most vendible in those place whereunto I be to go and what hope be of make a voyage I trust captain keeling have long since make manifest yet for all this I must try their courtesy the eighteeth of December I take my leave of master hemsworth who be very loath to stay behind i but I persuade he to be of good courage and doubt nothing see I be to take master spalding with i for his language and have no body to leave in the house but himself and tell he that if the governor send for he m. Augustine spalding go with he to the Maluccas he depart for the Maluccas the straight of Desolam the i will of Botun he must tell he plain that I have leave express order in any hand not to yield to any of his former demand yet he may take what he will for he must deliver he nothing then I set sail that evening for the Maluccas as I suppose and the wind favour we the seven and twenty of the same we pass the straits of Desolam and be through they lay becalm ten day which be no small grief to i in much heat under the line be doubtful of the westerly monson which if it shall fail i will be the overthrow of my voyage the eight of january we come before the town of Botun and send to know some news and there the king be go to the war and very few people in the town so I anchor not but we through the straits the same day the next day we see a great company of Caeracolles which we imagine to be the king of botunes army which prove so indeed the king send a small prow when we draw near unto he to see what we be I send he word who I be and it prove little wind and want water I demand whether there be any near hand so the people show i where there be great store of good water then I stand with the place and the king and all his caricolle come under sail after i and come to a anchor fair by we and send one aboard in his own name to bid i welcome and desire i to send master spalding with the messenger to come and speak with he to hear some news the king desire be that I will ride all night and in the morning he will come and see the ship and i it prove calm so we ride still and the next day the king come aboard and I make he and all his noble a banquet and give the king a gift worthy such a person a banquet make to the king of Botun and all his noble commodity provide by the king of Botun and a gale come fit to be under sail then the king weep and say I may think he but a dissembler see he have no merchandise for i for four month before my come he have his house burn to the ground where he have provide of every thing somewhat both nut and mace and clove and great store of Saunder wood a whole house full and a great Warehouse full of the cloth of his country which be very vendible in most part of the land thereabouts and all the loss which former he receive grieve he not half so much as when I tell he that I come and have cause the ship to be fit of purpose to come and buy his commodity that he shall provide for i he further say that I have keep my promise and swear by the head of Mahomet so will he have do if God have not lay that cross of fire upon he have sundry of his wife and woman burn but now he be abroad at war with his force he can not tell the issue of it and as the case stand with he he can not spare any of his people to make any provision for i and say that if I have not come by the night afore he have be in the field against another king his enemy who town he show i and request to shoot at it as I go by I say I be a stranger and know he not and to procure myself enemy I have no reason but if the other king shall come and offer he or any of his subject wrong while I be there I will do my best to send they away which speech of i give the king great content so the king take his leave and we set sail present the four and twenty of january we arrive at the island of Bangaia the i will of Bangaia the hollander fortify hateful to the people the manner of a Hollander where the king and most of his people be flee for fear of some enemy and certain I can not learn the truth there be a Hollander there that tell i that the king be flee for fear of the king of Makasar who as he think will force the king to turn Moor for he be a gentile but I rather think they flee for fear of the hollander who will have build a For^ there but when they perceive the people be flee they leave it uneffected this one Hollander bear such a sway that never a man leave upon the island dare displease he he have as many woman as he please two house full of the choice of the country daughter and many man and woman slave and be a pleasant companion and will dance and sing all day long near-hand naked as their manner be and win the heart of the people and will be drink two day together among the people of the island and be of himself and have live long in the country and will not be command by any Hollander and dwell over against if the governor of will speak with he he must send two of his merchant to be keep in pawn till his return he take up the king duty of Tarnata in all the land thereabouts and serve his own turn and send the king what he may spare here we have good refresh for my people be I praise God in better estate then when I set sail from England the goo^ health of h^r people and have not have a man sick to that present there I sheathe my long boat which we tow for fear of the worm that will have spoil she and after set sail the nine and twenty of january come to sea we find the wind right as we shall go so strive all we may to get to wind-ward but can not the stream carry we direct south and run so swift that we lose fifteen league in two day then I be fain to alter my detetmination for go for the and bear up the helm to go for Banda and may go with a down sheate @. 2 occurrent at banna contest with the dutch trade at Puloway and many peril the five of February we get sight of the land of Banda and make all the sail we can Banda to get near before night and draw near I send my Skiffe to hear some news of some of the country people who send i word that the hollander will not suffer any sail to come into the road but they will take all he bring if it be such thing as they stand in need of and make payment at their own pleasure but if any juncke come and bring commodity very vendible for the country people injury of hollander they be not permit to have any speech with any of the country but the Hollander will bring they to the backside of the castle within musket shoot of their ordnance that one must not set his foot ashore but they will send a bullet at he they have fifteen great juncke which they keep in that manner what hope be there to make a voyage there see they deal so with all fifteen great juncke detain by the hollander that come into the road and banish captain keeling not permit he to stay to gather in his debt but give he bill to receive his money at Bantam as I hope from his own mouth your worship have hear at large yet for all this I stand into the road with flag and ensign and at each yard arm a pendant in as comely a manner as we can devise there come a small pinnace of thirty ton send from the governor of the castle think it have be one of their country ship but come near we stand into the road before i after they have hale we I can have no other speech with they as soon as I come thwart of lautor I salute the town with ordnance and come to a anchor within shot of their ship then present a dutch boat come aboard we from the governor to have i come into the road and come ashore to he and show he my commission I make answer I be but new come and to show my commission to the governor or to make any man acquaint with those business which belong to the make of my voyage I will not they further ask whether I be a merchant or a man of war I answer I will pay for what I take then they threan i who tell they I be there and will ride there do as they shall please I hope I shall defend myself so they return to the castle in a great rage the hollander no soon go but great store of the man of lautor come aboard i kindness of the bandanese to the English and bid i welcome then I understand the whole estate of the country and the country will be willing to deal with i if I can procure leave of the hollander for they be now friend but pulaway and Polatronu be at warn with they now know well that in trouble water it be good fish there be one of Pulaway among they I have private conference with he and give he money in his purse to certify they of the island that I will give they money or commodity for all their spice and that the hollander and I be like to be enemy and let they not doubt but that I will get their spice aboard one way or other in the mean season there come another boat from the vice-admiral and the same boat from the castle with express commandment from the governor to i to come in be dinner time I cause they to stay dinner and after dinner tell they that I will ride there and stand to the danger of the road for I know full well that our nation be friend in Europe and for we to be enemy among the heathen people it be not good be christian whereupon they tell i plain I must not ride there and if I do they will fetch i in perforce I say I will ride there till I find the inconvenience of the road as by their speech it be foul ground then will I come into the best of the harbour for neither of our prince give any such authority to any of their subject but that every man may ride and go at their own peril they say that the country be they then may I the more bold say I ride here for we be friend so they depart in displeasure this evening I be about to land ordnance upon the side of a hill where we ride and begin to fit the ship to fight with they that shall molest i and send out some to see what ground there be round about the ship and it be all rock so by no mean the ship can ride there so we leave our pretence of land ordnance in the morning I send my Skiffe with master spalding and the principal of the ship with a letter to the governor and bid they say nothing more than I have write and make no long stay but bring a answer present for we ride very bad the copy of which letter hereafter follow may it please you worship with patience to consider that whereas you have diverse enemy and few friend in this place I be a Christian if your worship stand in need of any thing that I have I pray you make bold to demand it and I will be as ready to perform it to my power for whereas there be amity between our prince at home I shall be unwilling that we their subject shall be at enmity here further forasmuch as you command i to come under the command of the castle I hope I have that privilege that both prince allow their subject to come and go at their own pleasure and stand to the danger of the road at their own peril and whereas you demand to see my commission I be a gentleman and willing to show it upon equal term for if you will meet i secure as I will do you appoint our meeting on the water in our boat equal man or in any other convenient place where I may be as near my force as you be to you and whereas it be report that a contract be to be make with the inhabitant of Lantor and your worship my desire be that you will use i as a indian for my money then shall I think myself much behold to your worship and be more willing to deal with you then with they furthermore forasmuch as you be at enmity with the land of Puloway and Polaron my desire be to be resolve whether I may have their spice without your hindrance thus desire your answer to these particular and the same to be return by these bearer I bid you farewell from aboard my ship this seven of February 1609. you in friendship DAVID MIDDLETON all my company come to the castle be bring to the governor where they sit in council so they deliver my letter which be open read they will send i no answer but by word of mouth yet detain my letter they have determine by counsel have three great ship of one thousand ton a piece and three Pinnasses of thirty ton a piece that one of the ship be unserviceable call the great sun shall clap i aboard uncharitable purpose of the dutch. and there set herself a fire and have for the same purpose swear sundry person to come and make she fast with chain and have put into she thirty barrel of powder for the same intent which be man out of the castle with all the ship and boat to take up the man when she shall fire the great horn shall come and ride within musket-shot and batter upon we and the frigate round about we to keep we do on all side my folk see their speed they make to warp out the great sun make small stay but come away and tell i what preparation be make to have we I think it fit to go and speak with the governor myself and before we will try it by battle to see what he will say to myself and so take my commission with i I come to the castle and be meet at my land by the governor and all the principal man that be in the castle and ship and be bring through a guard of small shot of three hundred soldier who give i three volley of shot and the castle seven piece of ordnance for my welcome so we come to the governors chamber where for we two there be chair set the rest have form and after many salutation and compliment of welcome to the castle I begin and say I understand by my company which be with they before my come that they will not be persuade but that I be a pirate and have no commission and that it shall appear to the contrary I come myself and bring my commission with i to manifest that I be no such person but have the king majesty broad seal to my commission and call to my man for it and show it they read the first line unto they and lap it up again then they say that they will see it all I say they shall not while I live the commission be i commission show you all apparent see and the great seal at my commission and myself nominate therein and if they will see more it be not my commission they shall expect it we will have be go aboard but be will to stay awhile so there pass word between we some sharp and some sweet but at the length they begin to be more mild and call for a cup of wine than the company rise all up drink a cup of wine and go to walk and view the castle the office whereof be very neat and very well furnish with armour and great store of munition take my time I put in practice to see what money will do which often make wiseman blind that so I may attain unto my lade by large proffer I offer one thousand pound to be sure to have my lade the might of money and to give my chain from about my neck to one to procure it offer to pay more than they pay for their spice have set this matter abroach know the ship to ride in danger I tell the governor now they apparent see I be no man of war I will bring in my ship he reply with the residue that all the friendship they can do i I shall find they willing to pleasure i therein it draw late I take my leave to go aboard at what time the governor cause all the ordnance in the castle to be shoot off and as I pass by the ship they and the frigate shoot off till I come aboard the next day be the eight of February I bring my ship into the road and rid between their ship and the castle and give they all my ordnance and be answer from the castle and ship and frigate with great store as soon as we come to a anchor the governor with all the chief of the castle and ship come aboard of i so I entreat they to dinner to such as we can provide which they very kind accept and after dinner the main point which be my lade I can not by gift nor any mean I may devise have any grant to buy one pound of spice and have prove sundry mean to induce they to hear reason the governor tell i plain he dare not give i leave to deal for any spice under pain of loss of his head I see no good to be do in ride at a anchor among they determine to take in water and take my fortune but they will not suffer my boat to go ashore for water but they will send a man with we to see that we have no conference with any of the country people after I have water aboard I send master spalding to show the governor that I will be go and that I have send he to acquaint he therewith for myself will not come out of the ship dutch scrupulosity the governor marvel whither I will go the wind be westerly master spalding say he know not so I warp till I can get sea-room to set sail the governor send three Pinnasses to go out with i and one come in a boat aboard we send from the governor to command i that I shall not come near any of those land I send he word I will not be at his command for I be find to Puloway as soon as possible I can and bid he send his ship to send i away for I will quick send the frigate further from i he go aboard one of the frigate and I cause our man to get up their small shot and fit themselves to fight with their ship which be fit and their sail bring to the yard of purpose I call all my company to know their mind and tell they plain that if they will stand by i I mean to set up my rest his purpose for Puloway to make my voyage at those land let the Hollander do what he can and promise they if any man be maim he shall have maintenance during his life which if it please God I will have perform and further promise that if they will fight it out to give frank among they those thing that be i own which be in the ship so with one consent we be all willing to try what force the Hollander will send out to drive we away the Pinnasses see my folk to bring up their small shot think it will be small to their ease to guard i any long and therefore bear up for the harbour while we be a warp out the admiral have be twice aboard the Pinnasses and the vice-admiral and the lieutenant governor of the castle also what they do there I know not english resolution it fall calm and the wind westerly and a great stream set to the east north-east and we drive a great pace so I man my boat and send master spalding away with money and my pursers mate and five more to go and certify they of the land of pulaway that we have part enemy with the hollander and that I have send he to know their mind whether they will sell i their spice and I will give they money for it and will have come myself but will fain see the ship in some place where she may ride and then I will come either in the ship or in a pinnace that I have within board to set up while my boat be absent there come two prawe from Lantor to know why I go away I tell they the stream set the ship away I will fain have go to Pulaway if the stream have not hinder i and have send a factor thither to buy spice they say they be glad that I go not away for altogether then I pray they to tell they of Lantor that I will give they money or commodity for all their spice which they have if they will sell it i before the Hollander that come to take their country from they one of they say that he will go to the island and see my people and then he will show they of Lantor at master spaldings come ashore the country flock about he and bid he welcome but will make no price with he till I come myself m. spaldings welcome but will deliver spice upon a account till God shall send i thither to go through with they myself I bid master spalding hire i a pilot if he can to harbour my ship near hand who speak to the country for one and they hire he a co^ple to who the country give twenty rial and I must give they as much so master spalding send they aboard and write to i to send he more money and cloth the i will of ceran which I do the same night and bear up the helm for ceran and come to a place call Gelagula be thirty league from Banda a reasonable good road and as soon as possible we can we take a house and bring our pinnace ashore to set up have have she within board thus long and can never have time to set she up because the time of the year do so fast slip away and the monson be at a end labour all that night to get she dispatch be fit I name she the hope-well the seven and twenty of march we make all thing ready to set sail to the island of Pulaway the hope-well and arrive there the one and thiti of the same in the night and can not lade any spice till I have agree with the country people the country ask many duty and great gift but in fine I agree to pay as captain keeling pay after the chief have what they look for for every one must have somewhat that all must not know and a man must ever be give for they never cease beg and it be not for a man ease to deny they any reasonable matter especial as the case stand with i after we have agree we lade the hope-well with mace and send she away she be but nine tun can carry but little of such commodity which fill present wherefore I be drive to look out for more help to get over the spice so I hire a great praw and be to build she they lade spice which we lade with nut and send to the ship and there build she high and make she one of five and twenty tun but she make but one voyage and then we hear no news of she in three month still expect her come to Pulaway a long time the hope-well make two voyage can bring i no news of she so that I very think she have be sink for I come in company with she in the hope-well myself and have a great storm be perfect persuade that the sea have eat she up and give she for lose have twelve of the lusty man in the ship in she it be no small grief to i to see the time of the year to wear away and can not get my lade over to the ship nor dare bring the ship over for there be no ride for she and she pass the island oft all hope be pass for six month I make enquitie for other vessel and hear of a junck that belong to Lantor but she be old and lay near the hollander ship I go and buy she and get such help as I can to trim she the want of my twelve man put i to much trouble if I have have they with i all the while it have be a great shorten to our voyage for most of our man be down upon sore leg and as soon as one be any thing well he must into the hope-well and another poor lame man take his room have some three time well and down again thus I be drive to my wit end not know which way to turn i be every hour in danger of the Hollander to come and take the island who as by intelligence from time to time we hear seek sundry mean to make i away by offer large money for rogue to effect it either by poison or otherwise but I praise God I have some friend upon the island who give i secret warning of such man or to be aware of such men-slave for they will do i some mischief and come for the purpose whereupon I be fain to get all the land to draw to a head sore leg and fit their caracol and keep the hollander Pinnasses from come aboard so the Pinnasses dare not stir and the islander land secret upon Nero and cut off sundry of the hollander that they dare not stir out of the castle except they be many and well fit these islander build a fort upon the side of a hill from whence they shoot into the castle treacherous offer which trouble the Hollander much so we be sure that the Pinnasses can not come out as in former time to cut we off as oftentimes they have attempt make nine voyage in she myself and never can spare above seven man to go in she and but five at Puloway the rest in a manner lame and sick in a most villainous country where all thing be so dear that one shall eat and not to be have but at some time which be a great grief unto we all with such foul weather of reins continual which be like to have make a end of we all the junke which I have buy at Lantor I be fain to get away untrimmed for the hollander send i one of their ship see man at work upon she when they have fit she to batter she to piece so that night she weigh I get the help of two town to launch she and be to carry she a great way upon ruler this we do by night and get she out of sight by day and bring she to Puloway and be fain to buy sail for she and all thing else for she have nothing belong unto she but the bare Hull I set the country carpenter a-work which do her little good as prove afterward and have send to the ship by the hope-well that they shall bring over some rig for the junke and that master davis shall come and carry she over fit she as well as I can with those silly carpenter which the place afford the hope-well stay three week and we never hear any word what be become of she be doubtful whether any mischance have befall she and we may stay long before they aboard can hire any to come over the hollander have so seize they that they have take carry of victual to the bandaness be reasonable fair weather have the ship Skiffe at Puloway I determine to go over myself and make some shift m. John davis and not to let the time pass do nothing for I can not hire man to carry over the juncke if I will have lade she with silver so I put it in practice see the hope-well come not and not have a sound man with i that can stand on his leg I hire three black and put to sea be out of sight of land there arise a grievous storm that I be fain to spoon afore the sea to save our life yet God be praise we get sight of the land of ceran and keep she right afore the sea clean from our ship and come near the shore the sea aloft do break the i will of ceran sea-perill and take away all hope of come safe ashore night be at hand we strive all we may to keep she upon the sea till day the storm increase that no remedy but we must hazard all to put into the breach over a ledge of rock which we do and no man dare forsake the boat for be beat to piece against the rock so the next day we set she ashore be brimful and have all thing that we have wash overboard we lay hand on the boat and get she out of the suff of the sea and give God thanks for preserve we from so apparent danger be extreme foul weather with much rain we can not tell what to do the black come and tell we that we must go to sea present the country of the cannibal or man-eater if we mean to save our life I ask one of they the reason who say it be the cannibal country and if they get sight of we they will kill we and eat we and nothing will ransom a man if they take he and all christian that they get they roast they alive for wrong that the portugal have do they and therefore if we will not go to sea they will go hide themselves for the canbal will be at the water side as soon as they can look about to descry if they can discover any fisherman or passenger that by stealth pass by in the night we hear this and the moon begin to show the wind to dull and a tide of flood with we we get a head a good reasonable pace and by day we be clear of their watch and keep the shore close aboard we espy a hul of a bark come and row near it and know it to be the diligence so we come and hail she the diligence and there be a couple of englishman in she who tell i that the same night that we have the storm in the Skiffe she chap to a anchor there and the cable burst and she drive ashore and that m. Herniman be go to the town to get man to have she up and save she I land myself to go to the governor of the town to come and bring some help to save she the sand be full of people which come of purpose to have pillage she and I will they to make a shot now and then which stay they from come near they and come to the town m. Herniman be go by land to the ship I offer the governor money to have help to save she who say he will gather the country together within two or three day but I tell he that if it blow she will be lose within a hour inhumanity of the islander one of Puloway be there who know the bark and be earnest with the governor to save she plain tell i that he gape only to have she bulge that he may have the plank to build he a praw then perceive there be no help but must come from the ship I hire guide to follow master Herniman and take one of my own man to keep i company and so proceed by land be twelve mile from the ship be half way we come to a great water which we must swim over my man can not swim so I send my clothes back all but a scarlet Mandilian which these black must carry over for i who tell i the river be full of aligatd and if I see any I must fight with he else he will kill i and for that purpose do carry a great knife in his mouth danger of crododile I be weary not have sleep in two night take the water before the indian know they will be over before i the river be broad and a swift current which the great rain that have fall have make the indian will have have i turn back but be the better half way I be very unwilling be in the water one of the indian that carry my mandilion have get a great cane which I know not of and strike i on the side perilous mistake who feel the stroke suspect it have be a dive under water where the current get such hold on i that before I can come up I be in the sea and there the sea throw i against the beech and bruise my back and shoulder till the time that he come and give i the end of the cane whereof I get hold and he pull i out near hand drown be toss with the sea that every suff wash i into the sea again I praise God I escape this danger and get aboard after I have rest myself a reasonable space to the amazement of all my company so that night I send all that be able to crawl to save the bark which God be praise they do with much toil of so small help the country will not let any man lay his hand to save she expect we will forsake she that they may enjoy she the next day after my come aboard the Hopewell devilish determmation at my come a shore m. spalding tell i of their hard usage of they and what fear they be in the chief of all the land sit before our door to stay my come I go unto they and ask the reason why they deal so with my people in my absence they tell i plain that if I have not come myself they will have take the good and keep the man safe so I tell they the reason of the remove of the ship and say further no marvel that the holander build a castle to defend themselves when I be in friendship with they and leave man among they with commodity that the country stand in need of and make the holander my enemy which be their enemy and seek all the mean that in i lay to do all the land good as they all very well know shall receive such hard measure at their hand they say plain I must not blame they to be jealous of christian for many year portugal and hollander distasteful the portugal and holander have do as I have do but in the end they see apparent they will have their country from they yet now I be come myself they hope I will not think the worse of they so we become good friend and buy spice apace and have buy my whole ship lade have a overplus of stock leave I a ground upon a bank of sand the wind blow hard and the sea somewhat high which make we all doubt her come off this night come a boat aboard of we from the town with a Turk in she a proper man send by of that we look for for Alexander Sharpeigh have sell all his good there Alexander sharpeigh and we may do the like and for the ground of the ship he make nothing of it say it be ordinary for great ship of India to come a ground and yet never hear that any of they sustain any harm thereby he make haste to go ashore to certify the aga what we be with promise in the morning to return with boat to Middleton strike down dead be desirous to know what be the matter which we tell he he present rise up and will my man to show he where they be diverse of my company run after they to see what be the matter and I myself run after they call upon they as loud as I can to return back and make good our house but while I be thus speak I be strike upon the head down to the ground by one which come behind i I remain as dead till such time as they have find my hand behind i and so straight that the extreme pain thereof bring i to my memory assoon as they see i stir they lift i upon my foot and lead i between two of they to the where I find diverse of my company in like take as I be myself by the way the soldier pillage i and take from i such money as I have about i and three gold ring whereof one be my seal the other have seven diamond which be of good worth and the three a gimmal ring when all of we that escape with life in this bloody massacre be bring together then begin they to put we in iron sir h. Middleton and seven more chain by the neck myself with seven more be chain by the neck all together other some their foot other their hand this be do they leave two soldier to guard we the rest depart these soldier have compassion of we and ease we of our band for the most of we have our hand so straight find behind we that the blood be ready to burst out at our finger end with pain unsufferable but we be find to endure it after I have receive this ease of my hand and arm though still overcharge with grief of heart not only for my own necessity and these with i but also for the safety of the we be moor in the road where we find three hollander one whereof be find for Bantam and in her Peter but general of thirteen sail outward find who have spend his main mast and lose company of his fleet put into the road for to refresh his sick man the other two have make train of seal at Pengwin island find home Saldania be a bay some fourteen league north north-east from the cape Bona Speranza bay of Saldania and north by west ten league from cape Falso which be eastward of the former and may both be see in the say bay these two cape be also divide by another great bay the distance between these two bay be some three league be low marshy ground extend south and north which on either side be environ with mountain in this bay of Saldania when you have bring the norther point thereof west northwest northwest and by west for a small ship northwest thwart of the ledge of rock or water place near the shore which will be lay as it be in the swampe between the high mountain call the table and the sugarloaf in six five or four fathom according to the draught of your ship in clean ground and good anchorhold you may safe ride Pengwin island with his ledge distant three league off bear north northwest half west and stretch to the north and by west of you in the road the main land also though it be thirteen league distant trend a way to the west and by west so that there be little above three point open to let in the northwest sea which be the great storm Saldania have in former time be comfortable to all our nation travel this way both outward and home-ward provision more scarce at Saldania then in time past and why yield they abundance of flesh as sheep and beef bring down by the savage inhabitant and sell for trifle as a Beife for a piece of a iron hoop of fourteen inch long and a sheep for a lesser piece whereby weak sick man in former voyage have be easy recover and make strong now contrariwise whether our trade here be spoil by the dutchman we here find who use to spoil all place where they come only respect their own present occasion by their overmuch liberality or whether the cattle in former time so abundant bring down be prey take by war from one another or other difference which may make they greedy of iron to make head for their lance or dart which now by peace or reconciliation they have little need of the true cause for want of understanding in their language I know not but well I find that all the device we can use by bribe or otherwise to they which daily come down to our tent in fair weather will procure nothing from they for our sick man relief but four cow and those four cow which we do buy be so old and lean that there be but little goodness in the flesh for which they will take no iron but thin piece of copper of six inch square and some seven sheep at piece three inch square of copper cut out of a kettle whereof they make ring by six or eight together which they wear on their arm which be bright and smooth at one rial and a half of eight before this town of aden I make my unprofitable abode until the sixteenth of December live in continual danger if any storm have happen which be there ever very doubtful on this monson or time of the year by rummage I omit no mean for bring our good in readiness if so it shall happen that in the end we find sale or trade with they for notwithstanding by the variety of trick whereby from day to day they false delude our people in their hand as to send messenger after messenger to my general to Moha to obtain licence to bring our good into their town and then the merchant will resort out of all place in the country near-hand to buy the same which may be say lest we have discover the unlikelihood of any merchant in that town likely to do the same yet can I never conceit hope of trade or honest deal among they all the time I lay there for the most part I send my pinnace every two or three day to land to know how my factor do with some one or two man beside the cock ging which whatsoever they have to do they be courteous deal withal the soldier frequent their company cunning treachery give they drink and if any man jew or bannian have over reckon they in the price of any thing they will ever be ready to do they right all which I make account be do by the governors direction the better to abuse we by draw our people to conceit well of they and trust their flattery and lie wherein they excel and on the resort of any extraordinary people into the town they will tell our man that they be merchant come to see if we have land any of our good for they to buy when they be soldier call in out of some other near adjoin inland town upon some plot in their head new devise and likewise our factor in person be most time kind use and be tell i the truth to his disadvantage by my people in the pinnace I send of purpose to discover by who I be inform this city in time past have be great and populous but at this time the house both great and small be great ruinate and sink in every part of the town aden decay the present state thereof shop of merchandise there be none of any account merchant none to be discern worthy of that call for money seem to be very scant among they which appear when our man offer to change a piece of eight for asper they use to take it from hand to hand gaze as at a strange thing a ill sign in a place where a ship lade of merchandise be bring to sell. this present governor time grow near out that he must be go and therefore before his departure will have be glad to have see we so foolish as to land some of our good by any devise will often commend captain sharpeigh confidence in they who be here in the ascension sixteen month before we and how at first he bring good on land without mistrust and sell it and his man come bold on land like merchant man of which since we do not the like he make doubt whether we be so or not and that he take delight to hear his trumpet sound on his wall all which I take to be no other than hook device and untrue delusion for I can think but that if at the first like harmless man they trust much they repent it before they go away capt. sharpeigh the first of our nation at aden captain Sharpeigh be the first of our nation that come here and perchance may pass away in some reasonable sort but since then they have have time to advise themselves how to do more villainy which they have nothing else to plead my conceit be that at our first come they make account to buy our good without money and that their plot in desire first one ship to stay the messenger which be send to know what we be and our business though they before do imagine who we be partly by our acquaintance with they at Moha as also their hear of our be at surat the message according to the indian manner be deliver with many compliment and promise of all friendship and further that they will buy our good for money and give we indigo cloth and pepper for the same which be more than we can expect or they have order to grant for what indigo they have with cloth and pepper be present to be employ in their own ship now find for the red sea upon these kind promise the general send merchant ashore both with a present to the governor and with mustre of english clothes and other of our commodity but of all except some little broadcloth and kersey of our best colour as stanimels poppiniay green and other light colour and lead in bar we can sell none for our red lead Dabull double deal the governor buy and send it aboard again and somewhat after the manner we find at surat the governor deal double with we grant free leave to sell yet underhand have man in wait to restrain or beat away such as come to buy so that no man buy make his own price for what he desire to buy for corn and other provision and water to be bring aboard for money we have with all favour and at last we have a cable of eighteen inch and ninety six fathom of the country stuff worth eight pound sterling for one of the darling anchor now whether such kindness as we receive be out of their good disposition to stranger or not it be hard to judge they have present blow abroad and inform at Moha that we endeavour to right what wrong any shall impose upon we and therefore may seem to make the best show unto we the six and twenty in the afternoon beside diverse Mallaber merchant ship which anchor by we we see also in the off a great ship and frigate to who Portugal ship two hour before night the general send off the darling to bring in the say ship but doubt the miss of she by night as also the smallness of his force to command she when night come send of i also in the peppercorn with his frigate well man to attend upon i in regard of the frigate in her company about midnight though very dark I get sight of she ride at anchor send our frigate to the other run away and the great ship get sight of we be come to sail but be command to strike sail do it also their captain and principal to come aboard i he send a soldier and two more in a canon who excuse the captain to be age and unwieldy and that their great boat be so pester with lade that they can not row she wherefore though unwilling I be force to send my own pinnace for some of the principal merchant and soldier but with such straight direction to my cock-swaine that upon pain of great punishment he shall permit none to go into she to the end to prevent spoil I intend sir Henry Middleton shall be the first Englishman shall enter she meanwhile our frigate with the other which they have take return to we and to my grief give knowledge that they kill one of the portugal in fly now have diverse of their man aboard i I give direction to stand in for Dabull but by reason of their ill steerage which we impute to be do of purpose and for that with all our sail we can not fetch they up be get a little a-head we and fear they may mend their sail and get from we I cause they to be call unto to take in their sail and anchor till day which direction give and our anchor ready to let fall I depart into my cabin to examine some of the portugal what their ship be lade withal meanwhile my master pretend to doubt whether the ship be anchor or no without any order or knowledge send my pinnace aboard wherein go one of his mate more greedy of pray then careful of credit who do not only go into the ship but there fell to rifle who though often call make no haste away till his own pleasure be fulfil against who come aboard I cause Thomas Glenham John Staughten George Cockam and Robert mico the purser to be ready at the ladder with a lantern and candle to search they one by one in the portugal sight aboard our ship and turn they out of the boat which be do and the thing throw into the boat stern by Thomas Glenham John Staughten and Robert mico I send again aboard the Portugal ship will the purser to tell they aboard if there be any thing else want they that have be aboard without my direction breed in i much trouble and present discontent yet I use the best mean I have leave to cure the same unruliness in mariner when prey be present which be I desire William pemberton who with the darling I will not permit they April cause they to be put in mind of their behaviour former towards our people in their hand and when without any evil speech give they I think they sufficient by their own mind terrify I cause to be tell they that they shall see how far our nation differ from the rigour of injurious turk which most cruel handle our man without offence who by all fair promise they betray and that I yet know they to have exercise their force in abuse my man yet notwithstanding I will without discourtesy or harm dismiss or send they away who present depart with many promise the next day Maharim Aga of aden send i a present of henne-egge limb and which I will not look at as to receive as a present but by the messenger I send the Aga word that the variety of injury do unto my friend Henry Middleton as often time before relate unto they the wrong and damage sustain from the turk with who till he receive satisfaction from they for the same he can in no wise permit they to trade but notwithstanding he have already quite himself for the injury sustain in India yet must also now be force to carry out of this sea with he all the indian ship that this year by they the turk may receive no benefit but the indian see that by reason of the turk abuse and delay it be likely to prove unto they a unprofitable monson though their departure will be much prejudicial to the turk without trade with they by reason of the loss of their custom yet rather than to carry back again their indian commodity they desire to make a composition with sir Henry Middleton and captain Saris every ship several to pay a certain sum of money and we to forbear to hinder their quiet trade upon this proffer make by the indian sir Henry Middleton after good consideration have no mean to force satisfaction from the turk without further prejudice of the indian and therefore at present determine to accept of their offer still leave the satisfaction due from the turk till future time and to like she shee have in company her sister which be next heir and her young sister little daughter which have be marry to Raia siack brother to the king of joor this her sister common call the young queen they have speech with she be yet a unmarried virgin about six and forty year of age after we have have some conference with she she let fall the curtain intimate thereby that we shall depart signify that next day we shall come again which we do and be well entertain there be twelve woman and child to dance which I have not see better perform in the indies then be all the gentility command to dance or at least make show thereof which cause no small laughter we and the hollander must do likewise and the queen thereat rejoice she have not be out of her house in seven year before till this go to hunt wild buff and bull whereof there be great abundance as she pass along with her train betwixt our house and the ship we salute she with some piece from the ship and musket shoot on shore in this winter of November and December the water by continual rain great water be high than have be in the memery of man so that many beast die many house be drive away and much harm do the five and who dignity and function let it continue for ever also unto you my laudable great and most worthy captain and reyse of all our navy and ship that swim upon the face of the Sea unto you my laudable captain of the castle city and town and unto you worthy and laudable customer dwell upon the sea-coast upon river Bridges and all other part of our dominion and thereunto adjacent upon sight of this my most high and imperial commandment in conformity of your most find duty you shall arise and do obeisance and reverence thereunto hereby you shall understand that the ambassador of the king of great Brittany that reside in our happy and most high port have give we to understand by his supplication that forasmuch as some of his master the king of great Britain his subject have with great charge and labour discover a trade in the east-indies and withal understand of wealth and likelihood of trade in some part of our dominion by the way to be have in their passage to the say indies be therefore desirous to visit those place for the better enlarge of their say trade to the end that such man may in so good and laudable enterprise have all favour aid and help so far as lawful and convenient may be grant have request we in the name of his say master the king of great Britain to vouchsafe they our safe-conduct and recommendation in conformity of who request as also in regard we and our predecessor be and have be for the space of many year in strict league and amity with the aforementioned king of great Britain and the subject of that kingdom who long have have and at this present have free traffic and trade in merchandize in our dominion and province through the mediterranean sea we therefore do command and express charge you all and every of you our above mention subject and officer that you will not only kind and love entertain and receive the say merchant and subject of great Britain come or pass through or by any of our dominion especial intend to trade to the dominion of Yemen aden and Moha and the part adjoin thereunto assist and relieve they with all thing needful for themselves their man and ship but also free to permit they by land or by sea to go or sail outward and return even as their occasion shall require and to remain in any of our Dominons country or city grant they such liberty of traffic and privilege as shall be reasonable without give or suffer any let or hindrance injury or molestation to be offer or do unto they yea you shall yield unto they such office of benevolence and humanity as shall be meet and convenient to be yield unto honest man and stranger undertake so long and laborious a voyage and if so be that we shall understand that contrary to the capitulation the amity and league which be between we and the king of great Britain you do offer they the least wrong and any way molest and trouble the say merchant in their traffic and aught else know you for certain that you shall not only incur our high displeasure but you shall be punish for example unto other and therefore carry yourselves conformable to this my imperial commandment and give credit to this my imperial ensign write at our mansion guard at Constantinople on the fifteen day of the moon call Zil^^gie anno. 1019. the governor afterward take a copy thereof and return it again he tell our general that he be welcome desire that what have former be past touch Sir Henry Middleton may not be remember for that the quarrel grow by two drunken man and be by the then governor rash follow for which he be displace five month since and as concern trade he can not permit any great matter till he have direction from his master jafar bassa of Sinan who he have write unto and will within ten or twelve day return a answer earnest entreat that he will permit his people to come on shore to buy what they want and to sell small matter to the end that the natural may see that we be in peace and amity together and that what be pass be forget these his speech make good what the general have former conceive touch the doubt that the east-indian ship will make of their come in here unless they understand that we be all friend and their not come in here will be a great hindrance to every officer of this port. beside we ride so near the shore as we do of purpose as that no laden ship can come in but that she mu^t p^rforce ride within call of we which do put they in the great fear whereby he reckone^ himself sure of trade either a shore or aboard the ship and that keep the town in this awe he may the more bold adventure his skiff and people to the shore to fetch what our ship want the governor feast they very royal at a dinner with all sort of wild fowl hen goat mutton cream custard diverse make dish and confection all serve in vessel of tin different from our pewter and make goblet-fashion with foot the dish so place the one upon the other that they do reach a yard high as we sit and yet each dish fit to be deal upon without remove the meat be all serve up at once and that before we sit down our drink be water simple or else water boil with a herb call Canhaw therein which be in taste somewhat bitter we do sit crosslegged upon carpet lay upon the floor for there they use neither table nor stool dinner end he lead the general into a inner chamber where he have four little boy that attend he be his bugger boy there they two be set upon a crimson velvet carpet the rest of the chamber floor be spread with very rich carpet one of the boy bear a linen napkin in his hand do usher in two of the other whereof the first have a silver chaffingdish with coal the other bring a dish wherein be diverse rich perfume viz. ambergris aloe and other the governor request the general to let the boy cover his head close with the napkin which do the other boy hold the chaffingdish with the perfume put therein under his head that he may receive the fume which be very pleasant after he have finish the governor and two other chief man about he do the like be as it seem a ceremony much use among they have confer a while together there come in three of the boy again the one bring a vest or gown of cloth of gold wrap up in a case of taffeta die in saffron to preserve the colour of the Gold the other boy have a Shash or turban stripe all with gold and in length twenty two yard the three a Damaskeen or turkish sword rich garnish with silver and gild both hilt and scabbard the governor himself do put the vest upon the general and do gird the Damaskeen unto his side tell he that they be not present from himself but command by the grand signior who as he say do bestow they and entreat he to ride with the cady who be chief justice there and the captain of the galley about the town that the people may take notice of the amity and friendship that be betwixt we they bring a horse rich trap the mettle work of the bridle all of silver but he rather choose to go on foot that he may the better view the town whereto they give consent and so we walk together about the town and have view a house wherein to have settle our factory I be bring to the house of the captain of the galley where he have a costly banquet and thus return by the governors house he meet he upon the stair where again earnest entreat that the discourtesy offer sir Henry may be forget and that it may appear by his often come or send his people a shore they take their leaf one of another and so accompany with a great train of the best of the town he return aboard where the ship discharge fifteen piece of ordnance the turk that remain pledge have diverse present give they be send friendly on shore and have fifteen piece shoot off at their part the one and twenty the general send m. cock and other a shore with a present to the governor a case of bottle fill with which he do earnest desire the general to give he and to send it so wrap up as that it may not be know what it be likewise be send two vest of violet broad cloth to his eunuch they have further direction give they to inquire a shore what custom be due in and out the weight measure valuation of coin prize of Indicos calico cotton-yearne and other commodity fit for we to lade also to procure the Jew to come aboard who be in the ascension at her cast away near the bar of surat and can give we certain intelligence of sir Henry success note of Moha roade note that this road of Moha be very open and dangerous with very shall water a mile of the town low land even with the Sea at this present the wind south south-west a great storm which cause such a sea as that we do send not less than seven foot ride in five fathom and the wind at west you have no succour but the country people say that in the time of those wind extremity of herb begin in the fine of may. which begin in the fine of May the extremity of heat be such as that it dead the wind which make that season very contagious the thirty one the general understand from the captain of the town that yesternight late arrive the messenger from the grand bassa with letter to the governor to this effect that he shall yield we peaceable trade both on shore and with the indian ship as he will answer the contrary at his peril and to let we furnish ourselves with what we want he be doubtful of the certainty of this please news for that not half a hour before m. cock have speech with the governor who speak of no such matter the captain say that the reason of the governor not speak thereof be because here be a jelba find for Mecca and ready to depart which he will not have to know that the bassa have grant we trade fear lest they shall acquaint the sheriff at Mecca therewith who by his letter to the grand signior may cause the grant to be revoke but we rather think the bassa have return some harsh answer with direction to do that unto we which as yet he can effect we be so watchful and wary over he and therefore will not be know to have receive answer from Sinan till better bethink note that hosoroofe one that close have send a letter of m. femell testify their treacherous usage here do now send word by our linguist that the general shall beware of come a shore himself unless he have good pledge as former and then he may bold come but otherwise not to trust they though the governor shall swear upon his Koran for they be soldier and do not much respect oath and as he hear the news that be come from the bassa do not tend to our benefit for that the copy of the grand signior pass be not as then come to the bashaes hand but than shall be full see what will be do which will be within six day the second of April 1612. the caravan from in Egypt arrive here in Moha April Caravan of Cayro indian ship the three come into the road two indian ship one of Chau the other of Cananor their lade indico and pintado ambergris and cotten-yarne with at least four hundred passenger who carry much wealth about they we salute they with nine piece of ordnance out of our Fleet. they answer with three chamber a piece be all they have the general send the Skiffe to inquire what news upon the coast of surat the captain send word that there be three english ship trade there but further can not tell the captain of the town with five chief janissary come aboard be send by the governor to let our general understand that the bassa have write unto he to entreat and use we kind and to permit we peaceable trade desire the general that he will in person come a shore the next morning and he shall further understand he crave pardon not forget hosoroofe admonition but captain Towerson be desirous to go a shore the captain be request to tell the governor that the general upon good pledge will the next morning send his brother unto he which be well like of so have feast the captain and his retinue and give they diverse present they be send a shore with twenty one piece of ordnance at part which he send word that he take so well as that we shall not want the best assistance he can do we the four in the morning though the pledge be not yet come yet desirous to see what the bassa have order captain Towerson be send a shore for we hold the two indian ship which rid hard by we for sufficient pledge if on shore any injury shall be offer the governor use he friendly and vest he to content but nothing be effect of that he go about the turk not perform their promise the governor send word that it will be fit to send two of our man of good fashion up to the bassa to Sinan with the king letter and present and then speedy dispatch will be have to our like whereof the general approve intend the next day to lay out a present for he the five the captain of the galley send aboard three letter which the last night come to the governors hand from s. Henry Middleton and captain Sharpeigh three letter from sir Henry Middleton and capt. sharpeigh who ride then at a anchor at Babmandel the effect whereof be that he be come from surat and have little or no trade there that captain Hawkins upon distaste be come from agra and with his wife be aboard his ship that he have bring all away from thence except one man of captain Hawkins which go over land for England and that he be come back to be revenge of the turk wish our general to get his good and people aboard with all speed hereupon he alter what yesternight be agree upon and forthwith send one of the merchant away to sir Henry with a letter of the proceed of his voyage and of the manner of our entertainment here hitherto that if he have not thus come in he have on Monday send two man of fashion up to Sinan note the two indian ship aforesaid do discharge here these good follow indian merchandise aloe sixty kintal indigo six hundred churl out of both ship sash of all sort great store cinnamon of Celon one hundred and fifty bahar each Bahar three churl and a half osfar which be a red dye great quantity clove great store Bastas or white from twenty to forty royal the courge a Corge be twenty piece a great quantity the price of indigo be from thirty to thirty five forty and fifty rial the churl the seven the general write to the captain of the town that he shall procure the indian merchant to barter with he at reasonable rate for such of their commodity as he shall desire and as may serve to lade one of our ship which do will satisfy s. Henry of their now friendly meaning towards we and cause he to forbear all hostile attempt at this present there be a great rumour spread in the town of a jelba or two which sir Henry have take come we into the harbour I doubt what the cause of their come may be and be send off the Skiffe to command they not to come near the ship but the king be the head-most weave with his handkerchief and will the rest to attend and himself come aboard tell i that he have command they to come to tow our ship in about a point somewhat dangerous by reason of the force of the tide which be such a strong tide that have a stiff gale of wind yet we can not stem it and come into the eddy we shall have be set upon the rock so we send hawser aboard they and they fall to work in the mean while the king do break his fast with i be at a anchor I will have requite the people for their pain but the king will not suffer they to take any thing we anchor before the town we anchor before the town in five fathom so Fuccate a large and fair town which do and remembrance leave with the master and cape merchant for the well govern of the ship and house ashore during my absence take with i ten english and nine other beside the former sixty which be only to attend the galley I depart from Firando towards the emperor Court we be row through and among diverse land all which or the most part of they be well inhabit and diverse proper town build upon they whereof one call Fuccate have a very strong castle build of fre^ stone but no ordnance nor soldier therein it have a ditch about five fathom deep and twice as broad round about it with a draw bridge keep all in very good repair I do land and dine there in the town the tide and wind so strong against we as that we can not pass the town seem to be as great as London be within the wall very well build and even so as you may see from the one end of the street to the other the place exceed people very civil and courteous only that at our land and be here in Fuccate and so through the whole country whithersoever we come the boy child and worse sort of idle people will gather about and follow along after we cry that be to say you coreans with false heart wonder hoop hollow and make such a noise about we that we can scarce hear one a other speak sometime throw stone at we but that not in many town yet the clamour and cry after we be every where alike none reprove they for it the best advice that I can give those who hereafter shall arrive there be that they pass on without regard those idle rablement and in so do they shall find their ear only trouble with the noise all alongst this coast and so up to Ozaca we find woman diverse that live with their household and family in boat upon the water woman with their household that live in boat upon the water women-divers as in Holland they do the like these woman will catch fish by dive which by net and line they miss and that in eight fathom depth their eye by continual dive do grow as red as blood whereby you may know a dive woman from all other woman we be two day row from Firando to Fuccate about eight or ten league on this side the straits of xeminaseque we find a great town where there lie in a dock Straigh^s of a strange juncke a juncke of eight hundred or a thousand ton of burden sheathe all with iron with a guard appoint to keep she from fire and treachery she be build in a very homely fashion much like that which describe Noah ark unto we the natural tell we that she serve to transport soldier into any of the land if rebellion or war shall happen we find nothing extraordinary after we have pass the straits of xeminaseque until we come unto Osaca where we arrive the twenty seven day of August our gailey can not come near the town by six mile where another we find here a garrison of three thousand soldier maintain by the emperor to keep Miaco and Osaca in subjection garrison change every three year their march and weapon the garrison be shift every three year which change happen to be at our be there so that we see the old band march away and the new enter in most soldierlike manner march five a breast and to every ten file a officer which be call a captain of fifty who keep they continual in very good order first their shot viz. Calievers for musket they have none neither will they use any then follow pike next sword or cattan and target than bow and arrow next those weapon resemble a welch-hooke call waggadash then caliever pay for what they take as all other man do every town and village upon the way be well fit with cook and victual house where they may at a instant have what they need and diet themselves from a penny English a meal to two shilling a meal the diet in japan the diet use general through the country be rice of diverse sort one better than other as of our wheat and corn here the white account the best which they use in stead of bread fish fresh and salt some pickle herb bean radish and other root salt and pickle store of provision wild-fowl duck mallard teal goose pheasant partridge quail and diverse other which they do powder and put up in pickle of hen they have great store as likewise of dear both red and fallow wild boar hare goat kine etc. of cheese they have plenty no butter nor milk eat butter they make none neither will they eat any milk because they hold it to be as blood nor tame beast of tame swine and pig they have great abundance wheat they have as good as any of we be red great Britain your majesty kind letter send i by your servant captain John Saris who be the first that I have know to arrive in any part of my dominion I hearty embrace be not a little glad to understand of your great wisdom and power as have three plentiful and mighty kingdom under your powerful command I acknowledge your majesty great bounty in send i so undeserved a present of many rare thing such as my land afford not neither have I ever before scene which I receive not as from a stranger but as from your majesty who I esteem as myself desire the continuance of friendship with your highness and that it may stand with your good like to send your subject to any part or port of my dominion where they shall be most hearty welcome applaud much their worthiness in the admirable knowledge of navigation have with much facility discover a country so remote be no whit amaze with the distance of so mighty a gulf nor greatness of such infinite cloud and storm from prosecute honourable enterprise of discovery and merchandize wherein they shall find i to further they according to their desire I return unto your majesty a small token of my love by your say subject desire you to accept thereof as from he that much rejoice in your friendship and whereas your majesty subject have desire certain privilege for trade and settle of a factory in my dominion I have not only grant what they demand but have confirm the same unto they under my broad-seale for better establish thereof from my castle in Surunga this four day of the nine month in the eighteen year of our Dary indies 1 we give free licence to the subject of the king of great Britain viz. sir Thomas Smith governor and company of the east indian merchant and adventurer for ever safe to come into any of our port of our empire of japan with their ship and merchandize without any hindrance to they or their good and to abide buy sell and barter according to their own manner with all nation to tarry here as long as they think good and to depart at their pleasure 2 item we grant unto they freedom of custom for all such merchandize as either now they have bring or hereafter shall bring into our kingdom or shall from hence transport to any foreign part and do authorise those ship that hereafter shall arrive and come from England to proceed to present sale of their commodity without further come or send up to our court. 3 item if any of their ship shall happen to be in danger of shipwreck we will our subject not only to assist they but that such part of ship and good as shall be save be return to their captain or cape merchant or their assign and that they shall or may build one house or more for themselves in any part of our empire where they shall think fit and at their departure to make sale thereof at their pleasure 4 item if any of the english merchant or other shall depart this life within our dominion the good of the decease shall remain at the dispose of the cape merchant and that all offence commit by they shall be punish by the say cape merchant according to his discretion and our law to take no hold of their person or good 5 item we will that you our subject trade with they for any of their commodity pay they for the same according to agreement without delay or return of their ware again unto they 6 item for such commodity as they have now bring or shall hereafter bring fit for our service and proper use we will that no arrest be make thereof but that the price be make with the cape merchant according as they may sell to other and present payment upon the delivery of the good 7 item if in discovery of other country for trade and return of their ship they shall need man or victual we will that you our subject furnish they for their money as their need shall require the discovery of Yeadzo to the northward 8 and that without other passport they shall and may set out upon the discovery of Yeadzo or any other part in or about our empire from our castle in Surunga this first day of the nine month and in the eighteen year of our * * or reign Dary according to our computation seal with our broad-seale etc. underwritten minna Mottono you yea note 9 intelligence concern Yedzo deliver in the city of Edoo in japan by a japanner who have be there twice that Yedzo be a island and lie on the northwest side of japan and distant from thence ten league Yedzo be a island hairy people that the people be white and of good condition but very hairy all their body over like monkey their weapon be bow and arrow poison the people in the southermost part thereof do understand weight and measure whereof within the land thirty day journey they be ignorant they have much silver and sand-gold whereof they make payment to the japanner for Rice etc. Rice and Cotton cloth of japan be here well request iron and lead be bring to they from japan necessary for the belly and back be most vendible to they Rice transport from japan to Yedzo have yield four for one the town where the japanner have their chief residence and mart be call matchma matchma therein be five hundred household of japanner who likewise have a fort there the governor whereof be call matchmadonna this town of matchma be the principal mart town of all Yedzo whither the natives most resort to buy and sell especial in September for their provision for winter in march they bring down salmon and dry fish of sundry sort and other ware for which the japanner barter which the japanner rather desire then silver people of low stature far to the northward a current to the east north-east the japanner have no settle be or trade in any other town than matchma that further to the northward upon the same land be people of very low stature like dwarf that the yedzo be people of the stature of the japanner and have no apparel but what be bring they from japan that there set a very violent current between Yedzo and japan which come from corea and set to the east north-east
