we injury as former they have do at Polaway Cambella and other place and how they have turn the glass for master ball have he in their possession and threaten to hang he present if he cause not the english to come from land forthwith the hollander can make no claim to polaroone also we then show they the surrender of polaroone and our right and possession there for his majesty of England which we will hold and maintain to our utmost power and wish they to be well advise what they do and that they will be short call to a account for their disgraceful word and ab^ses do to the english demand also of they the island of Polaway as in right due to his majesty by lawful surrender further demand of they if they have any surrender of the island of polaroone but they can not say of any they have and when we show the surrender we have unto they the predicant have the same in his hand aboard the swan peruse it say with these word this be a true surrender all this time the glass run in the great cabin before their face put they in mind of be go we also tell they that their come be only to betray we and to put we from the island by their treachery which our nation have diverse time have experience of wherefore we neither can nor will trust they any more and so put they in mind of be go for the glass six time run they must expect shoot from the shore and if in case they do reply and do shoot unto the land or show any discourtesy or wrong unto the people of polaroone we will take it as do to we and will defend they be now becomne our king subject they will have stay until the next day but we will not grant it doubt that more of their ship may have come over they then desire till midnight which we grant if we may see they about to way their anchor and that we will send unto the shore and persuade the bandaneses to forbear also I demand of dedall the cause of their come to molest we who answer it have be former a custom in pass by the island I tell he that be untruth the english be the first christian that ever come into the road of polaroone for that the people of the island have report unto we that there be never any christian ship in the road till we come and that we be the first so he be silent and will not maintain his report they come into the road about three of the clock in the afternoon and depart thence about eleven at night we have be since inform that they come purposely to betray we and to have beat we out of the road or to have take our ship and have give the attempt but that they perceive we be fortify on the land if they have then begin the hollander come to beat we out of the Road. we doubt not but to have make our party good with they for we have both fort ready and our gunner ready to give fire upon our watchword or sign from the ship the ten of januarie a holland ship and pinnace come forth from Nero the pinnace come edge near the small island or high sand adjoin to polaroone call belong unto polaroone and consequent to the English there be no inhabitant upon the say island or sand but it be full of tree and bush and polaroone man resort thither daily to fish about the say small island the hollander send a pinnace to sound the depth by polaroone and to invade we now the say pinnace come near the say island and do sound the depth as she go which we perceive make four shot at she from the defence fort not intend to strike she but shoot wide give they notice to forbear and be go the pinnace at every shot reply with a base or some such like piece unto the small island among the tree where there be some english and some bandaneses of polaroone which be in danger of their shot and see they brave we in such manner the gunner be bid to do his best who then make a shot which fall close over they at the stern of their pinnace or frigate which make they cry out and present get off they be hollanders and seem man which come to sound the depth and where to land purpose to come with their force and there to fortify and so to put we from the great island John Davies in the swan will go out of the road to fetch water januarie the thirteen master davey complain he want water and purpose to go over for wayre upon Lantore side and there to water we acquaint the people o^ polaroone herewith who will by no mean consent he shall go out of the road neither will we doubt some injury from the hollander and the people of polaroone tell we that they will rather fetch they water over upon Lantore with their prawe I go present aboard and acquaint master davey herewith but he and the company will not yield hereunto but speak all in general against it and say that the bandaneses wo^ld bring they rain water or such as may be unwholesome for his man to drink say it be but six or eight day time the same time there come over unto we from wayre a free town upon Lantore also from the i will of rosinging a island of itself the principal of both those place to have parley with we to surrender both the say wayre and rosinging unto his majesty as the people of polaroone have late do now the surrender of both those place be draw and all conclude upon at polaroone the i will of rosinging and town of wayre desire to surrender themselves and to have some go to take the same surrender the swan and four merchant go to Rosing and take the surrender the people of rosinging and wayre go with good to the swan the star take the swan slay five man use cruel violence and proud insultation they desire that some english may go over to receive the same from all their hand and to see all right thereunto perform now master davey resolution be to go over to water we conclude that master Sophonie Cozock George Muschamp Robert Fuller and Thomas Hodges shall go over for wayre and rosinging in the swan to perform the say business or see it do and the swan there to water after which dispatch it be order that master Sophonie shall return again in the swan and the other three shall remain upon the island of rosinging for possession till further order all business be there end according to our expectation diverse man of wayre and rosinging desire to lade nut and mace in the swan and passage for polaroone there to sell their spice to we for Rice and Cloth all be grant they ship twelve of themselves with nut and mace a great quantity the swan set sail and go for Geulegola be but a little way from wayre as I understand and there water after which they set sail and eight league of land a holland ship or two give they chase which they in the swan perceive ask the master what he mean to do think that he purpose to fight with they master davey answer they see my colour and I see they I know he to be a Hollander they i to be a Englishman I know no hurt I have do they and I stand for my port of polaroone and in short time the holland ship the star be come within shot never hale the swan nor say word of their intent but let fly great shot and small in most violent manner the swan have receive two or three great shot through and thorough before she ever reply and some of the man kill the fight continue as master davey write one hour and half wherein five man of the swan be kill viz. Sophonie Cozock merchant beat in piece with a great shot Robert Morten quater-master and drummer Christoper droop Edward Murtkin and a bandanese of wayre a passenger three other be main have lose leg and arm and almost all hope of life if not dead already more eight man wound most of their wound deadly and in this their cruelty a villain of the star stand upon the poop with a draw sword brave with these word english villain and rogue we will kill you all thus he speak in dutch. it seem that the swan man be much discourage see many of their man lie dead wound lament insomuch that none will stand by the sail to trim the ship for their best advantage so that the holland ship lie still in her quarter pour in small shot and great and so take she board she both soldier and other break up cabin and pillage they and the man also in most base manner both of clothes and all thing else throw over board what they like not the Spaniard never use more cruelty in their profess war the star have in she one hundred and three score man most soldier take from Nero and Polaway castle the swan have not above thirty able man to fight the rest sick and lame and the man somewhat weary out in toilsome labour at polaroone in land the ordnance and make two fort ten also of their company be leave in polaroone to defend the fort two of which be gunner viz. Harman Hammon and John day the swan be take they carry she present under Nero castle and all the man the surrender of polaroone be take in the swan so we procure another verbatim from the polaroone man which I have bring with the surrender of rosinging and deliver bo^h at Bantam etc. she be much batter and tear they much glory in their victory and show the bandaneses their exploit in the great disgrace of the english what they can say that the king of England may not compare with their great king of Holland and that one Holland ship will take ten of the english ship and that saint George be now turn child and that they care not for the king of England the swan be bring to Nero they present send our man on shore and keep they all prisoner many of they in iron neither man nor boy have liberty the swan set sail from polaroone the sixteenth of januarie 1616. we expect her return in eight or ten day at further but never hear of she till the five and twenty of February by Robert Fuller who be at rosinging and wayre hear of a english ship under Nero castle and come over to polaroone to acquaint we herewith present we dispee away Robert hayes Purser of the defence with some principal man of polaroone to land upon Lantore side be our friend so to go as near as may be to the holland ship and to make sign to they by a white flag of truce our messenger stay almost two hour at last they come with their boat to fetch he a messenger send to know why they take our ship their boorish usage of he but make he wade to the middle and so carry he aboard one of the holland ship the principal and assistant of Nero meet he aboard our messenger demand why they have take the swan and what be becomne of the man the reason of detain the ship man and good they answer that time shall bring to light our messenger still urge to know and therefore he be send they use many disgraceful word of the english their vaunt and threat and that they will come over to polaroone with their force and drive we from the island and other place hay reply they have already do more than they can answer and return without sight of any man of the swan company the poor ship there lay rend and tear in view of the country people in short time after they send over unto we a messenger with a letter which we answer as we do other after send their messenger still come with a flag of truce all which say letter and surrenders I bring with i to Bantam and deliver to captain ball. now we be still threaten by their letter as also by word of mouth from their messenger report that the hollander be prepare ship against Polaroon that as they have the swan so will they also come to fetch the defence and drive we from the island we still answer that we expect their come in regard they have so often threaten we and that we will defend it as long as life last many brauado they make daily shoot at Nero and Polaway forty fifty and sixty piece of ordnance think to affright we therewith also the people of Lantore bring we word that they be fit their ship and ship plank and earth which we imagine be for land service have then seven ship four galley and frigate and many man and that they pretend to come over to fight with we hollander practise to fire the ship defence and that they have instigate their black which be slave that if they can by any mean go over to polaroone and there set on fire the defence they shall be freeman as also some other reward they shall have also the hollander report that we shall carry no spice from the island hollander threaten that we shall have no spice from those land or any the land of Banda hereupon we consider that have make a contract with the people of polaroone wayre and rosinging and have trust our good unto they also a good quantity of nut and mace be ready to dispatch away lie ready upon polaroone the hollander threaten to come over and force we from the say island of polaroone and to take the defence hereupon we resolve to maintain the honour of our king and good of the honourable company our employer to land all the gun out of the defence our people fortify polaroone and all provision else and to fortify upon the small island adjoin unto polaroone there be no people on the small island but full of tree and bush and there the hollander purpose to have land and to have fortify which have they perform they will have command the road and do we much injury for that the people also of the island polaroone can not have fish as they be acuustome neither can the english have come into the road but that they on the small island will have beat they off and to prevent all danger we land all the defence ordnance only four great piece and some bread and two butt of cider also a terce of wine and be all fortify upon the say small island with the help of the bandanese the master of the defence master Hynsley be also on the small island and all man else at work and land thing some man be leave aboard the say defence to keep the ship a conspiracy be plot nine man go away in the defence unto the hollander John Christmas Boatsons mate John Owers William Carter Richard Taylor Edward Bridges John Harris Will rockwell Hugh woodlock and the same night the twenty of march 1616. either they let the ship drive or cut the cable and so drive off in the night which we perceive from the small island present send a boat after they advise they to return with the say ship but those villain will not hear they neither suffer the boat to come near they but bend their piece against they and discharge a musket shoot at they they be not able to overcome they forsake the say ship and come back unto we at the small island acquaint we what have pass the next day we perceive they run into Nero road under sail and under the command of Nero castle some of the man go present as we understand on shore and mee^ing with the hollander report unto they of their exploit and contend among themselves who shall be the best pilot in conduct the ship thither one report it be I and another it be I and as the hollander messenger report unto we afterward come over unto we that they bring a can of wine ashore and drink unto the hollander as soon as they come on shore present the hollander take possession of the say ship the defence and have all the villain into their castle and examine they of all our proceed at polaroone and they discover all how we be fortify and what pass among we these villain take the course to cut all our throat upon polaroone the hollander encourage by the villain that run away for the go away of the ship breed a jealousy in the bandaneses that it be a pretend plot among we to join with the hollander and so to betray they also their discover our weakness upon polaroone may have encourage the hollander to have attempt that in which else they perchance will have doubt of victory and indeed many sharp threat we have after the run away of these fellow and expect daily their come over which have they come it will have cost many man life for their have take the swan and kill our man abuse they with imprisonment and fetter and all the disgrace that may be have much harden the heart of the english against they the three and twenty of march 1616. we dispee away a letter unto the hollander at Nero by Robert Fuller who be land upon Lantore the people of Lantore be then in parley with the hollander about a factory that the hollander desire upon Lantore and also will build a fort there the people of Lantore will not accord with the hollander but the people of Lantore will not grant it this time our messenger can not pass but desire to stay three or four day with kind word from the Lantore people so our messenger return the effect to demand the defence man and good the five and twenty a messenger come over unto we from Laurence Ryall principal general be new come to Nero from the Moluccas understand what have pass desire to have parley with we and will have master Corthop and myself to come in a praw offer of parley betw^ene the hollander agent and factor of polaroone and two of his principal merchant shall do the like and so to meet each other half way betwixt polaway and polaroone to parley but we refuse their demand doubt the treachery for they may have man lie secret and so carry we away perforce also the same time and by the hollander messenger we receive a letter from master davey be prisoner at nero. the effect dislike of what we have do and still do maintain John davis his judgement by information of the hollander in keep the say island of polaroone and that our commission can not warrant what we have do and advise we to have parley with the general Laurence Ryall and to come to some agreement that no more blood may be spill all which he have write I conceive be by the instigation of the hollander possess he with many untruth as hereafter it plain appear the first and principal they have so wrought he in humour he and make he believe that they have our king majesty letter to take any english ship if they find they to the eastward of the selebe which news make we much to marvel and that if any such thing be we must obey it hereupon we do write a letter unto Laurence Ryall general by his messenger that if he will send over unto we two of his principal merchant viz. Henrick de Watterfoord and Peter young and to land they upon the small island and have receive they into our charge master Corthop and one more to attend upon he will present go over so their m^ssenger depart and two day after viz. the three of April return with this answer the two merchant before name which we desire for pledge can not come the one go to sea in the horn the other his business such be principal book keeper can not be spare the say Laurence Ryall propound two other late come over and principal merchant call Cornelius neep and Hans Rogers we return the say messenger accept they and the six of April their galley come over unto we and bring these two man present receive they into our charge and a tent be set up near the place where they land there lodge they because they shall not come near our fort to take any view how we be fortify and place a guard always about the tent twelve english man with small shot and that they may receive no wrong of the bandanese nath. Corthop upon pledge go to parley with the hollander at Nero present master Corthop go into their galley and go over to Nero and arrive there near night and be receive no word pass that night but refer until next day so the next day do discourse many opposition on both side which I leave to relate because of the letter of master Corthop which I bring from Banda and deliver unto captain ball will certify your worship at large only a little I will touch many threaten word they use and speak of many abuse they have receive by the English the hollander accuse our people of untruth that sir Henry Middleton do wear the holland colour in the red sea in the trade and give out they be hollanders master Corthop reply that be a untruth for that he come forth in the say ship and continue in she as long as she reign and never know she to wear Holland colour and reply that sir Henry be a gentleman that much scorn to wear the holland colour also report the hollander report ^hat they have our king ^ for take of ship etc. all untruth that they have the king of England letter to take any english to the eastward of the selebe so master Corthop urge they that he may see the same and that if they can show he that we will obey it and begone but they can show no such letter diverse other thing they allege but no truth and many persuasion to leave the island of Polarcone persuade he the great error we be run into in hold the same all this while master davey neither any the english be permit to come near master Corthop the general Laurence Ryall see he can not pervaile and to have his desire grow much discontent and throw his hat on the ground and pull his beard for anger master Corthop answer he that he can do nothing of himself but be join to a counsel be assistant and will relate what have pass when he come to polaroone and that we will consider of it and so write our direct answer thus I advise he to say that he may get the more free away the Hollande^ deny to restore our ship but upon condition to render polaroone also master Corthop demand the defence man and good in their possession but they will deliver neither ship nor man except upon composition thus be Laurence ryalls demand that we will permit he to come with his ship and galley unto the small island adjoin to polaroone where our castle be and twelve piece of ordnance and there to land his man and his ordnance and be possess will deliver unto we the swan and defence and all our man and for the good he will make restitution to all to a penny all this will not do then to conclude desire master Corthop to set his hand unto a note which he have draw the effect that the say Laurence Ryall have make these proffer unto we master Corthop likewise refuse and will not put his hand hereunto now they have so wrought with master Davie that they be persuade that he will persuade somewhat he be send for by the general and admit into the room with master Corthop so master Corthop and he have much discourse speak of the letter which they shall have and be persuade that it be true and that we continue in a great error then master Corthop acquaint he what have pass in discourse with Laurence Ryall Laurence ly-all and what proffer we have make he if he will show we the say letter which master Davie perceive so reasonable a proffer the man of the swan do complain of want of food and clothing in their imprisonment in the hollander hand and that they have sit in judgement upon they and give sentence upon they a praw send towards Bantam from Polaroon which they can not according as they have verify unto he make good master Davie present in great fury rail against they all say they have do he great injury in tell he and possess he with so many falsehood and further say that they promise he and his man good quarter but his man complain much of want of food and clothing and hard usage and that they have sit in judgement upon he and his company and have give they all condemnation there to remain until they hear out of Holland and can be content to remain so as we can keep they from the island of polaroone etc. so master Corthop take his leave and be bring over again unto we and be land we present release their hostage and so depart for nero. now the easterly monson be come we fit a Bandan praw to dispeed away from Bantam to give advice what have pass it be conclude myself Mr Hynsley master of the defence and other to the number of four english and fourteen bandanese of polaroone shall go we have the great number of man doubt of the hollander lay wait for we whereby we may by row free ourselves and indeed the principal of polaroone desire it these which we bring five of they be principal man one be the sabandors son the principal of the island his father be the other four be Orencayas and the rest their servant these also come to deliver the nutmeg tree and earth of the say island and to manifest their love unto the English we set sail from polaroone the seventeen of April 1617. and as we fall with Bottone stand our course for moccasor a Holland ship and pinnace give chase we discover a great ship and pinnace they see we give we chase bearing a press sail so that we have no way to escape they only we must perforce stand in for Bottone and do half a day they give we chase and have fetch we up have we not row hard so we be near the town of Bottone by night think they will not have come so far into the river next morning we perceive this ship and pinnace almost within musket shoot of we present we land most of what we have in our praw and carry it into the wood and go present unto the king and give he a present such thing as we have to the value of thirty rial desire his protection which he promise we in all kind manner and send his servant to put all our thing in house and put we into two several house to lodge and to keep in heathen kind than hollander to the English that we be not see abroad so we take our leave we be no soon go but present come the hollander and give a present three time the value of what we give inquire what we be that be land but the king reply that he do not know the king demand they how long they mean to stay they say six day hereupon the king advise we to stay so long time to see if they will go or not that we may go with the more security the six day be expire they will stay six day long to mend their mast as they report so see their intent and our praw lie in view of their ship and pinnace that we can not go about to fit our praw but they will have take notice thereof wherefore I buy a praw and the king command all our thing to be carry by his slave into the same we by the help of the king of Bottone get another praw and come to Bantam lie out of sight of the ship and all thing be fit send his man out of the river pass near the holland ship with the praw and to carry she about on the backside of the island and send fifty man with we and convey we over land unto the say praw where we go present aboard and keep under the island until near night and so stand our course for moccasor hear no more of they we be inform that the hollander keep watch every night upon the water near our Bandan praw at Bottone we arrive at moccasor the seven of May 1617. and there we find the attendance pretend for Banda but can not beat it up the easterly monson be come so we ship in the attendance a hundred and eighty sucket of mace which be buy at moccasor and sedt the praw for Beniarmasin and Suckadania for advice and that a supply of good be not yet come to furnish those part as be pretend for that the Solomon be not arrive yet at Bantam be long expect the three of june we arrive with the attendance at Bantam understand of the death of captain George Barkley the surrendry of the i will of Banda bring to Bantam and deliver to master ball. and master Ball succeed he captain of the house unto he I deliver all thing viz. two surrenders the hollander letter and other copy of letter to they write by we and all thing else of our proceed in Banda all which I doubt not but your worship shall receive by the first conveyance also may it please your worship to understand the messenger that come over first unto we from the hollander have be with we two several time with letter from the principal of the hollander at Banda this fellow call Christopher Vande loare as he report come over unto we in a praw and three black with he say that he be run from the hollander upon discontent the captain of Nero have abuse he and that he love the english and will serve we also be exceed earnest with we present upon his come over and importune we extraordinary that we shall go that night upon the island of Polaway with fifty man and he will warrant we the island of Polaway and will bring we so that we shall take the castle discover unto we his plot I can not believe he but tell he that he be send to betray we this fellow hereupon protest and swear most deep to the contrary and that the hollander will present hang he if ever they do take he we tell he we will not seek it by force of arm for we have no commission so to do not doubt but they will be make to deliver the say island by right of law and justice the i will of Polaway take from we by force of Arms. a counterfeit messenger or dissemble runaway the english have the first possession and surrender of the say island and be by force of arm put from it upon his protestation master Corthop accept of he and give he liberty and go with he wheresoever he go upon the island so that he see all our fortification and occurrence of business which much grieve i for I counsel he many time to lay he fast at the first place where he be receive which be upon the defence-fort and tell he often my opinion that he be a villain and be send to betray we also it be the opinion of the bandanese yet all will not persuade master Corthop so I think good to have he with i to Bantam and that he may be send for England for that he know of all wrong the hollander have do unto we and he have say unto i and other that the three ship that be with we at polaroone which before I note come purposely to fight with we and to have beat we from the island and that the horn have plank brick and lime and other provision to fortify upon polaroone or the small island but that we be before hand also he do manifest unto we of four other great ship that be send from Nero which ship we see come forth and ply for polaroone but they be by the strong currant put to leeward and so force for Amboyna also he tell we the hollander suborn their slave to set fire upon the ship defence that their condemn slave be set to work to fire the defence at polaroone and if they can perform it they shall have their liberty and be freeman all this he manifest and aver to be true within three day after our arrival at moccasor this fellow publish that the swan be take by one of their Pinnasses and other disgraceful word tend to the disgrace of the english which as soon as I hear thereof I present charge the master of the attendance with he and so send he aboard hereupon he vow to have my life short after we set sail for Bantam and come near put he in the bilbo and search he and his chest for letter which he may have of advice to convey unto the hollander and find a draught which he say be of Polaway castle also a letter pretend unto the principal of the hollander or english at Bantam all which I deliver unto captain ball. captain ball. this fellow report he be a director in the build of the fort at Polaway and that he have experience therein and when he come over to we bring two hundred rial of eight so at my arrival at Bantam I do acquaint captain ball of business and advise that the fellow may be careful look to and keep prisoner that he run not away to do we hurt he will to have he bring ashore myself and other go and fetch he and deliver he prisoner in the house the counterfeit Hollander suffer to escape by the toleration of g. ball. captain ball have some discourse with he who it be likely give he good word as former he have do with many protestation of his loyalty and have his liberty in the house never make fast with iron nor in any room and many time I speak to captain ball to make he sure and tell he he will watch his time to run away who answer be he shall run if he will little regard it it much grieve i to harbour a traitor in our bosom he have be two month in the house the second of August 1617. get out and run into the dutch house whereas I have advise to keep he sure and send he in the first ship for England so to have witness against the hollander as he must have acknowledge and speak truth upon oath which will much have advantage your worship in the prosecution in law touch the main business the four and twenty of August hollander send ten english man from Bantam to Holland 1617. depart from Bantam a Holland ship of advice direct for Holland and two day after her departure they report here that ten englishman be send in the say ship for Holland what they be we can learn but imagine they the man that run away in the defence the hollander think to make they say any thing by their instigation which may make for they and it may be they will say that the defence be leave as a wrack which be not so the master and company will have go away for Bantam but we hold it not good for that the people of Polaway understand thereof be discontent and say that we have build a fort for the hollander the master write a note that he will set sail that night have no good at all in the ship master Corthop be go aboard to persuade the master and company to the contrary which the polaroone man understand call present a council and show many reason that it be not fit the ship shall go away and will not let master Corthop go aboard by any mean doubt of his go away it be propound that I may go aboard to persuade the master or to command he and the rest to stay and to charge they that if they go if we lose life and good it shall be lay to their charge long it be before the bandaneses will permit i so jealous be they but at last through o^r earnest request grant it and send six man with i of polaroone i acquaint master Hinsley the master and the company of the many inconvenience and danger both of loss of go^ds and life and scandal to our nation and that if we shall have go about to have lade spi^es the hollander will present have have notice thereof and lay wait to have take the ship and bring all into their hand the mariner be keep at polaroone with much difficulty neither have we man munition or victual to maintain the island of polaroone nor the small island Nelaro adjoin all the ship company will have go away be unruly and perverse say they come not to be soldier nor will they stay so that we be fain to give way and entreat they by fair mean like child so little in their resolution regard they what may ensue care for nothing so they may get free the people of polaroone perceive a difference among we do murmur tax we with our promise before mention and that if the defence and man go away we can not resist the hollander our mortal enemy who we expect daily and if they come and have the victory we that shall there remain must expect none other but rigour on both side the people of polaroone will have conceit that we betray they and the hollander will have have no remorse set their slave a work to murder wherein themselves will not have be see and shall they have gain either the great island or the small as they may and will have do have not the ship stay we have lose all good debt credit of our nation without hope ever to be there respect the runaway in the defence in many respect worthy of death all thing consider we resolve the defence to stay and land all thing and to let she ride it out until further opportunity but in the mean time these villain run away with the say defence endanger all and therefore worthy of death at my come from polaroone it be conclude by we that another praw shall be send for Bantam for advice twenty day after our departure doubt the hollander may have pursue and take we as they do their best and so all our proceed have be obscure according a praw be send 170. suckle of mace ship in a junk w^th eight English which be lose by the negligence of one Stacie who reply that they can make as good friend in the court of England as you the honourable company our employer can and that this which they have do hollander brag that they can make friend in court etc. will cause you the honourable company and they to join and that a chain of gold will recompense all and that they have rial enough in holland to pay for a ship or two so as they may hinder we from the he away by poison he that he shall never see England again now for advice as touch the trade at Banda the island of polaroone be report to be the worst island and be about eight english mile compass and the small island adjoin call Neluco about one english mile compass there be pretty store of mace and nut grow upon polaroone and more will be if it be well husband Lantore and rosinging yield great store rosinging be a fine island and yield the large nut and Mace now if we hold polaroone description of polaroone etc. we can want spice for the people of Lantore rosinging and other place thereabouts will come over to we and bring their spice if we bring rice cloth salt pepper mellase and other necessary for food and some moccasor gold which will pass at Banda as currant as rial of eight and at the same rate be worth at Bantam but two shilling four penny the profitable trade or two shilling six penny the piece call mass our Cargason which we have be but small have but one hundred quoyne of rice our cloth at moccasor much decay lie there two or three year if we have have three time as much cloth and spice we can have sell it all for nut and mace at polaroone and be entreat for Rice and cloth by Lantore and rosinging man and other but have it not for they and some return with part of their spice home again they come over to polaroone with prawe and correcorry in the night the mace and nut be very good but lie so long must needs decay by the many molestation of the hollander we have no time nor lime to make wherewith to preserve the nut the trade will prove profitable if we may quiet enjoy the island and we must buy rice at a low rate than at moccasor it be by report at jap^n about half the price may it please your worship to understand that after my arrival at Bantam a land quarrel at Bantam with the hollander the steward of the house be at the market to buy provision the hollander steward there present quarrel with he whereof while they contend notice be give at the dutch house and present Timon the second merchant run forth with twenty japon and hollander a very Timon and black to the Basar or market run upon our steward with their draw weapon he have but two english all disarm enforce they to shift and give way mean while Richard hunt chance to come by and draw his sword who present they assault and give he three wound whereof he die within fifteen day after on the four and twenty of july 1617. notice hereof be bring to the english house we with our japon run forth and meet with they before they can recover their house and wound two hollander whereof both die short after also one of their black then kill outright and one or two more of they be hurt and so drive they home to their house they give after that great word that they will put we all to the sword and do lie in wait for our people with their pistol and piece whereof we have notice by the javan and stand upon our guard night and day to receive they if they have give any attempt on the house or abroad now concern the land of Banda and especial polaway captain castleton may have make it sure unto the english as I have hear report by diverse our right by law and equity unto Polaway and the english have still more right on that island both by law and justice than the Hollander although by force of arm they put the english from it the easy obtain and captain castleton deny the right and possession the english have there as it be report embolden the hollander to use the violence at polaroone and except it be supply this year and the possession maintain the name of English be utter disgrace and little hope of be receive there again which if we hold until your worship have resolve what to do herein we shall in short time procure as much nut and mace as they which may in time prove a entrance into the Moluccas for clove the hollander pretend they have right unto the Moluccas and Banda by the king of Ternates * * in the quarrel first move betwixt capt. keeling and they 1609 they never make such title but pretend agreement and intend and extend force see above pag. 202. their own article of their right son have he prisoner but the bandaneses deny any right the king of ternate have in their land every island be free of itself and govern by sabandor and Orencayas general appoint now it be meet that a supply be send the bandaneses and English for rice victual and cloth and other necessary to hold the possession and bring away the nut and mace there in readiness in godowne the hollander give out that they will take your ship that shall go into those part and cut they off so to famish both english and Bandaneses so your worship may charge they of all damage already do and may expect to hear of further abuse from they wherefore it require a earnest and speedy prosecution that we may quiet trade without molestation unto those part that have surrender and desire trade with we viz. polaway a paradise by report the hollander report it to be as good unto they as Scotland to his majesty polaroone rosinging and wayre wayre be a town upon Lantore and if in case of necessity your worship can agree for Polaway yet if you may enjoy the three last we shall procure nut and mace enough for England as also to transport both thence and hence for surat and other place in the indies now be the time or never upon the vile abuse of bloodshed and murder commit by the hollander and for the trade there it will prove very profitable I make no doubt what have pass former I doubt not but captain jordan have certify at large what since myself it be requisite that I shall relate the particular of all occurrence in respect the business be of so great importance here be find home for England the Charles and hope I pray God send they well at London I have send your worship a brief abstract of our Cargason for Banda and sale there make if I seem tedious I humble crave pardon with my humble duty I end beseech the almighty to prosper and give good success to all your design humble take leave your worship most humble servant in all duty THOMAS SPURWAY endorse to the honourable and right worshipful company of the merchant cause of our come he than rise up and bid we welcome they still suspect our ship a man of war by reason of some excess of some of our countryman in those sea applaud our design and demand why we be so fearful to come on shore without pledge we answer that about six year since some of our countryman be here with kind show and promise entice ashore and by the then governor betray imprison and many murder who harm make we cautelous for our own safety but that we be no otherwise then we profess they shall short know by the testimony of two guzerat junck one of which have not come this year but for the pass and promise of the say ambassador that our ship shall defend they homeward find from man of war in these sea have escape rifle last year by man of our nation through our opportune come to our rescue who deliver her safe at her port and send their chief commander into England to answer those wrong to our king friend he acknowledge our nation good and friendly promise that we shall live on shore and negotiate as secure as in our own country that he will also procure the bassa to confirm the same and will give we any content that for the ill usage former the governor than be a ill man long since remove and now live in disgrace at Stambola and swear by his Mahomet and by his beard that not one hair of we shall be diminish nor any wrong offer Constantinople that he will therefore proclaim our liberty that none may pretend ignorance to discourtesy he wish we also to look out a house in town fit for our person and good command two of his principal chanse to attend we and till we can fit ourselves better recommend we to the jew-merchant his entertainment desire he to assist we in all thing thus after our present deliver as from our captain and many kind thanks the visit the Scrivano we go by the jew persuasion to visit the Scrivano who be likewise chief customer who servant himself not be then at home entertain we with much civility and bring we into a fair room not much inferior in building or furniture to that of the governor where we have leave he and whence he soon return and welcome we with much courtesy assure we of whatsoever the governor have promise and that he himself will see all execute who have power also to right we we be inform that this man authority be no less in the town than the governor who be by he direct in matter of weight he seem a hearty old man after he have make we drink Coho and Sherbet we take our leave and rest that night with our jew. the next morning we spend a hour to view the town and observe the countenance of the people towards we who we find gentle and courteous they view the town the description thereof especial the banians and guzerats of which here live continual great store as merchant shopkeeper and mechanike trade their shop neat build and clean keep their market or Bazar appear well furnish with all necessary beside fruit daily bring out of the country the town for the most part build with brick and stone fair plaster over with plaster of Paris the building flat-roofed some two story high with Tarrises on the top whereon they build summer house of cane and mat in which they rest in the night and pass the first quarter of the day have at that time a fresh breeze from the sea all the rest of the day so hot heat at Mocha their neatness that man can well endure any clothes not so much as a shirt it lie level alongst the seaside be about two mile from north to south there be many fair house and three principal mosque the street keep clean each man door every morning and evening water and sweep seem like sandy bowl ally than street no filth suffer to be cast abroad but carry to a place appoint scour by the sea in fine I have not light see a sweet clean better govern town then this of Mocha betwixt the governor and scrivanoe be the wharfe about twelve score square near which adjoin to the governors house be a platform raise build with hew stone with battlement towards the sea about forty pace square in which be mount thirteen or fourteen small piece of little force against the landing-place be two fair brass piece about five foot in length on the other end be the Alfandica and a brass piece of six foot which carry a bullet as big as a canon this be their strength for defence of the town yet at the north end be a stone house in manner of a fort and in it some few piece but they put small trust in their ordnance rely most on their soldier of which two hundred reside continual in the town the rest be in all to the number of five hundred live within a day or two day journey and be in readiness upon any occasion Hoia nassans son the principal India merchant of the town profess and promise all kindness for we go to his house and after a cup of Coho and tobacco which be usual among these people we go again to visit the governor before we go aboard who rose and meet we cause we to sit by he welcome we promise as free trade here as in any other place of the grand signior dominion another governor expect nor will deny we any thing reasonable say that another governor shall short succeed he but one as his brother honest than himself who shall perform all the promise which he have now make at our request command the water-bayliffe to furnish we with boat at all time to carry we or water from shore for the ship aboard after this we visit the Scrivano and find he very courteous promise to come aboard to see our ship and bid our captain welcome and after a health of Coho dismiss we to return to the ship where our two pledge approve their kind usage who departure be honour with five piece feast on shipboard on the seventeen the Scrivano our pledge the jew and twenty person attend come aboard bring a bullock bread quince and other fruit and a cake of great roundness and thickness like puff-paste wherein be bake hen and chicken very well dress and please enough to a dainty palate we also with a quince Pie crab sack and strong-water add our best welcome he will needs be swear brother to the captain which be solemnize with a cup of sack and after much mirth and view of our ship he depart with great content we have water bring by poor people at reasonable rate we also have give good reason to the governor and Scrivano who approve it to make every juncke that shall arrive to anchor by we and there to ride till they have discharge their good the governor be willing we shall examine and compel they hereto because some juncke pass by their town to other port for trade to the loss of this storm and heat the one and twenty six at night we have a storm of wind off the shore with thunder and lightning very vehement but no rain which continue half a hour the rest of the night extreme hot this storm bring sand and dust aboard in abundance notwithstanding we ride a good league from shore the five and twenty we have a message from the Scrivano that the governor and himself have receive letter from the bassa of Sinan command they to receive and entertain we with all kindness to permit we to live and trade among they free and quiet new governor arrive ignorance of a new governor must excuse we of the charge of a new present to he it be needless to press with the inconvenience which may arise from deny we trade who be able to force it and hinder other from come the fear of which have cause some already to pass by this town to head and beard we shall live as secure from hurt as in our own land we ask what security he will give we beside his oath he answer his firman under his chop and procure the like from the bassa with this we seem content and give he thanks nor do ever people seem more willing to give content than they which I think arise not from conscience or love but fear see we able to their trade after some question of our ambassador now reside at Constantinople and touch the portugal and spaniard which he say be proud and unfaithful nation some speech happen of sir h. Middleton we demand the cause of that treachery towards he he answer the Vizier at that time be a bloody cruel cause of turkish treachery to sir h. Middleton let english christian read blush and amend and ill-minded man of himself and make worse by the instigation of other turk and arab of this town who observe the uncivil behaviour of our people as piss at the gate of their church force into man house to their woman and be daily drink in the street will fight and quarrel with the people thing hateful in these part these thing be in part but the governors covetousness hope to get their ship and good be the main cause of that ill deal for which and many other bad action he be not long after send to Constantinople to answer it and be either dead or life in disgrace to this day we dine with the Scrivano and hire a house of Hassana give one of our pledge at seventy rial of eight the monson which be all one with the yearly rent the Scrivano will needs swear himself our friend on his Koran yet deny this governor to be the man which captive sir h. likewise neither more nor less but as it be contract by our agreement that no inhabitant of this town nor people of the country neither Turk nor Arab shall injure they but they shall have their liberty to their content and that this my firman and contract be give they with a good heart and true meaning to see it perform I witness the truth before the most high GOD and our holy prophet sign Pallambam point so soon as we descry they we make towards they with all speed and they in a careless fashion ply it to and again with their top sail half mast down dutch bravery and at length as we draw near unto they the admiral and the rest bear up with our ship be the window most of our fleet and give we two shot one through the ship side under the half deck and the other in the steeridge side this I declare because man may the better understand the insolency vinivalencie of the dutch. or rather vinivalencie of of this arrogant nation to come on with such a spanish bravado and so soon to run away they have no soon begin but they be as quick answer from our ship in such a measure that within the space of two hour by the gracious assistance of almighty God we make they as quiet as lamb the admiral that first give the onset be the first that run away their flight and after he all his fleet who we chase until night and then find they too light of foot give over the chase the night we stand over towards the second in the afternoon we anchor again in the road of Bantam this day we have news from jacatra that one of the two dutch ship aforenamed be fast on ground hard by their castle and that they themselves at sight of sir Thomas Dales fleet have set she on fire dutch ship burn and another cast away the other ship which take in some rich good out of the castle be likewise cast away upon certain rock ten league to the eastward of jacatra the four we receive the letter from io. powel reside in jacatra that sir tho. dale depart from thence the first of march with the moon the hound the rose and the bee to search out the Fleming that be cast away the fourteen in the forenoon we have news from sir Thomas dale that he have get almost in shot of these four ship and then they be take with a calm the space of twelve hour and after this calm there do arise a tempest in the night which scatter they so far asunder that the next morning they be out of hope of their chase and so return to point air again a tempest determine forthwith to come unto we with the moon and to leave the rest of his fleet to take in some provision from jacatra the of march we Achen Teco and Bantam and of the surprise the dragon bear expedition etc. in a letter to the company to the honourable governor and right worshipful committee of the company of the english trade in the east INDIA etc. honourable and right worshipful sir the passage of your business in captain Bonner voyage to and at surat till then and long after very hopeful you have by ma^^ advise from themselves and several relation from other large and particular understand wherefore I shall therein be purposely silent intend according to my poor mean and ability the one be lose with your ship and the other have always be very small to acquaint you only with such accident as until the say ship take happen wherein I shall humble beseech that you will be please to pardon my presumption in offer to your view these imperfect and unworthy line not doubt but other better able will more accurate perform what be by i omit requisite your knowledge than my insufficiency especial at this time be able to express and poor employment in your service afford not to be make partaker of dragon part from the Anne 17. Febr. near surat before Dabull a junke of Dabull lade and find for the red Sea the dragon and other ship of that fleet part with the Anne the seventeen of February 1618. the one and twenty follow anchor before the road and town of Dabull it be former order by consultation to touch there and not long after come a boat from the governour-deputie to learn what and whence we be whereof be certify he again return ashore and towards night a grave man captain of a juncke then in the road lade and find for the red sea with his son come aboard bring ten ox ten goat three hundred hen with great store of rice fruit etc. for a present to confer with our captain about such thing as shall be propound and that night they lodge aboard the morrow after they remain for pledge master salbanke and master Fursland go ashore to the deputy the governor himself be then at court eight day journey distant the chief of the town kind entertainment at Dabull the dabull^rs desire ^rade with we store of refresh at Dabull and good cheap promise to buy quantity of cloth hereafter and l^ad but we can not pu^ of any of the lion remnant the captain of the jun^ke desire a english bible to cau^e to be translate into Arabeck as they affirm entertain they very kind profess likewise that they be much content with the english arrival and have long desire to have commerce with they and to that end entreat to have a factory leave or the ship to ride till notice thereof may be give to the governor because without his approbation they can not conclude of any thing we have at this place great store of very good refresh indifferent cheap large beef for six rial a piece and fruit etc. great plenty for small price but none of the old remnant in the lion can vend yet upon future hope they promise fair to deal hereafter for large quantity of broad cloth lead and other english commodity captain Bonner defer enforce advise thereof to surat that the next year fleet may do to they as occasion require the six and twenty the aforesaid Noghoda land to who be give a fair in-laid musket with the furniture thereof he also earnest desire a english bible which be give he say he will careful keep till some english be there resident and then with their help will have it translate into Arabeck for his own use it have be I presume long since relate unto your worship how that during your fleet abode at Swally two Mallabar frigate put themselves under command of your ship affirm themselves subject to a of Echaree near Goa and pretend to be send by the king their master to capitulate with the english about establish a trade with he for pepper his country by their report yield yearly sufficient to lade two great ship the trial whereof be by consultation assent unto they both attend the fleet to this place and here one of they desire leave to depart before to the king to advise of our come that his pepper may be in more readiness against our arrival and that a english merchant may accompany he to view the commodity and cut price with the king for who sufficient hostage shall be leave abo^rd the dragon which be likewise agree upon master wight merchant and i^o Tucker with he for linguist the history of the offer pepper at Bataquala be dispee with he and eight of the prime man in both (@) leave for pledge the lion be former dispose of for the red sea it be order that thou shall keep the other ship company to Dabull there to vent if possible part or all those remnant bring from the r^d sea for ready money or to force they trade and the proceed thereof to be towards lade the expedition with pepper at (@) but the unfitness of th^se commodity for the dabulleer their fair promise and kind usage procure their quiet this year the lion dispee to the red Sea six hundred that then we shall make sign for his come he then send we back with one of his kinsman to the merchant house will we there to stay till he either come himself or send order for dipatch but there we attend while past noon and then not hear aught return to the king who by his jurabassa fall to discourse of our country manner have tumbler play before he and with such trifle delay put off the time till near four after noon when we entreat he to give we a answer that we may return to the captain who all this while expect our come whereupon take we aside into a room from sight of his people he tell we that he have many matter of import whereof to confer with the captain which he will not have his own people to take notice off and to that end have appoint a private house to be prepare for his entertainment not far from his court and therefore will that master wight shall tarry and accompany he present thither and that I shall return to the captain and bring he to the place assign I desire to see it but he refuse appoint one of his attendant to go with i to the seaside there to tarry captain Bonner land and conduct he to the foresay house but by the way consider how indiscreet it will seem to motion his go to a place I have neither see nor know especial in such a treacherous place I tell my companion that unless I may first see where the king intend to meet I will not advise the captain land he perceive i resolute leave i and direct one of his slave to show it i who lead i near two english mile up into the country and at length bring i to a little house but handsome enough site in the midst of a small wood about which be a fair plain a quarter of a mile every way and without that round environ with thick and high wood which place minister just great cause of suspicion I return to the king who I meet upon the way with forty or fifty attendant come thither with he also master wight to who I show my opinion of the place and that it now grow late and therefore nothing to be do that night come to the house the king sit a good while muse without speak when we desire leave to depart it be now near night and past time for the captain land and that if he please we shall again return on the morrow as also to certify his desire of private conference with the captain but withal entreat that we may lose no more day but that according to his former conclusion we may dispatch our business after a little pause he command all his own people out of the room leave none but master wight Ino Tucker linguist the Samorine deny to perform with we according to his promise under forty rial the candee and myself the door be shut he beckon we and then ready find his Portugese tongue till then conceal tell we resolute that he can not perform at the price contract for the pepper be none of he but the merchant of the town and that under forty rial of eight the candee he can not accomplish and if they or any other will sell cheap he give licence Bonner unto Teco and Bantam send the Portugal pinnace for Bantam and by the way to touch at Teco to learn the estate of that factory if any be to stay there four day and at Bantam ten and then unless by captain jordaine detain long to make all haste possible back to Teco there to attend the dragon arrival from argin to inform the company affair at Bantam in she be appoint William Rickes master with twenty other and my unhappy self also that factory be likely to want attendance and I willing to my best service though in so mean a condition as it have please your worship to dispose i the four and twenty about four after noon we part with the ship they stand away for Achen and we for Teco of who proceed there I be altogether ignorant and shall therefore presume to refer your worship to master Nichols his advice if as I much fear have happen the rest from the factor there have with your ship miscarry the six of April 1619. we arrive at Teco and hear nothing at this place save what your ^ have long since be acquaint with have water and send advice to captain Bonner of our arrival etc. the eleven follow we set sail for Bantam have have diverse day calm and sometime the wind contrary the three and twenty we anchor betwixt the salt h^ls in the straits of and the seven and twenty towards night a small gale blow we weigh and intend to have put into Bantam ride before day but the usual calm force our anchor some four mile short of poolo-paniang and in the morning the pinnace arrive among our ship near Bantam the 23. April ready to set sail we descry ten ship and four junck ride under the foresay island who with that breath weigh and stand towards u^ we know not what to conceive of they little expect to have find so many english especial those ship in that place the better to make they we hoist out our praw and in she three man to row until they can make their colour and if dutch to repair back to we if english to go aboard they the latter whereof they do ere long the admiral be thwart of we who master Rickes salute with three piece he answer with one and send his Skiffe aboard will our master to weigh and stand after he to Morrogh and i to come aboard his ship and bring such letter as I have with i which I present do where I have relate all those miserable and lamentable accident which I presume your worship long since understand by the james safe arrive home the nine and twenty the fleet anchor Morrogh and the next day sir Thomas dale captain bring etc. come aboard our pinnace and dispee she for Bantam if possible to get som^ provision for the ship as also to learn if any flemish ship be at jacatra or thereabouts but speed of neither we return to the fleet the second of may. the ten ship then at Morrogh cap. jordain in the Samson and hound go for jambe Pata Syam to visit those factory about the 9 of April be the moon Clove globe peppercorn the james royal gift unicorn advice rose and bee captain jourdaine be some fourteen day before our come go with the Samson and hound for jambee Patania Syam and other place beside the four junck three whereof be from China the other from Patania and our pinnace new also by sir Thomas dale order for to attend his fleet the first of May the China junck begin to be romidge and their good take into your ship for debt owe by the chinese to your worship after which four China junk take by our ship their good lade in to the james etc. the 1. may 1619. Owen bodman be execute the 24. may 1619. our ship set sail out of the straits of Sunda the 25. of may. a junke of Rice belong to the dutch. our fleet sir tho. dale be admiral with all the rest of our ship do set sail out of the straits of Sunda 25. may 1619. some go to Ingano to weigh the money and ordnance leave in the sun our fleet purpose to return again to Bantam by the last of sept. the pinnace send back again from Bantam to Teco Priaman and Achen the pinnace passage from Teco to Achin rich. crane miraculous save price Hawkins strike with lightning but partly recover the pinnace drive back again to Teco cut down their mast yard and sail to prevent their lade the pepper at Bantam leave they there ride the quantity and quality of those good exceed my knowledge to advise I be both a stranger and by your worship order not to meddle in business of that nature the four and twenty of May Owen bodman be execute at the yard arm in the moon this day the fleet fit to sail and the rose in stead of the pinnace be intend for Teco and Achen to advise captain Bonner of proceed there with a cargazon of Rice steele etc. confine to master Fursland at Achen in which ship also it please sir Thomas to appoint my return one of the foresay junck be of Patania and most of her lade Rice belong to the plemming so much thereof as be think fit each ship provision be take out and she this day dismiss the five and twenty the fleet set sail sir Thomas dale with the moon Clove globe peppercorn advice and pinnace stand for Ingano to recover if possible part of the money lose in the sun and to relieve those man leave there if any be alive and captain bring with the james royal gift unicorn and bee for the coast intend there all to meet and to come with their joint strength to Priaman there to meet with the ship from England and also captain bonner and altogether to go to Bantam the fifteen of june we arrive at Teco where we make little stay but have water etc. and left letter for captain Bonner of the past proceed at Bantam and future purpose for this place depart thence the nineteen from Achen go betwixt the main of sumatra and the shoalds which from Teco lie four degree or more of north latitude and stop every night the nine of july about six in the evening a storm begin at northwest we be then anchor some fifteen league to the northward of barrou which increase in great extremity till about midnight with very fearful thunder lightning and terrible rain we have but one anchor aground have the shoalds and the main on every side of we within two league in this extremity not know what course to take but only to attend God mercy in our deliverance our cable break and we bare room back over these shoalds in a exceed dark night with which former we dare scarce deal at noonday yet the never forsake mercy of the almighty preserve we from all those danger and with daylight also send we fair weather when necessity enforce determination to bear back again for Teco it be say we be the first ship that ever go this way and I think no man that dare depend upon his skill to adventure without sight of land will ever sail that way again the one and twenty we have another great storm which begin about two after noon with very much wind thunder and rain which last above four hour split our main sail and blue away our spritsail rich. crane one of our company be then upon the yard arm the brace lift and all the rig of the spritsail yard at once break and he with his head downward hang at every set of the ship cover with the sea above a glass space no man be able by any mean to succour he till at last faintness and weariness make he let go and as he drive by the ship side take hold of a rope by which mean next to the almighty mercy his life be beyond expectation miraculous preserve another name price hawk stand in the waste be by a flash of lightning strike dumb and lame over all his body lie in most lamentable plight for many day yet God be thank his speech be a little return but a kind of dead numbness in both his leg and arm make he still continue a very miserable man distress as aforesaid the three and twenty we return to Teco and by reason of our want both of cordage sailes and ground-tacke of which there be no more in the ship than be at that time in use no more than one hogshead of flesh no bread but rice and that not sweet no other drink for sick man etc. but water but nineteen man in the ship whereof five very sick and diverse other lame it be resolve through importunity of the company thereto to remain there and attend relief from the dragon or other english but in the interim a rumour of flemish ship come from Bantam force we change resolution and the six with our weak crew put to sea in hope either to meet the ship from Achen or to get our intend park and by that mean to ease ourselves of some of those misery the dragon and expedition go to Teco have have since our departure from Teco a very fair gale the ten to our great comfort we meet the dragon and expedition betwixt the island N^mtam and Batta so soon as we come near captain Bonner send his Skiffe aboard to who I go and deliver his letter from master spalding master ball etc. sir tho. dale by reason of his sickness have also refer he to they for advice the next morning at a consultation it be conclude two month trade obtain at Teco 1500. bahars remain at Achen unbought for lack of mean that the rose shall return back to Teco in regard of her unfitness for any voyage as also for that the good in she will vend so well here or better then at Achen the invoice whereof be enclose in a letter seal and direct to master rich. Fursland which I then likewise deliver by captain Bonner I understand of two month trade grant at Teco of above one thousand and three hundred bahar of pepper then in the dragon and of more than one thousand and five hundred remain at Achen unbought for lack of mean to the end that so little as may be of our short time shall be lose the fifteen in the night captain Bonner send off his barge with master Nichols and myself to go ashore and acquaint the king etc. with our licence for trade as also to take a house and so much as may be to set each thing in a forwardness the king seem very willing appoint as we desire a very convenient house close by the sea side next to the customhouse and promise so soon as he see the king letter muster of our good and have conclude of the price order shall be give for present weigh the nineteen master Nichols go aboard the dragon ride two league without the road and bring the king letter ashore with he which see and read proclamation thereof be present send into the country and many in the town have good quantity of pepper which they will not sell till the king have first begin the one and twenty the dragon etc. come into the road pepper buy at Teco and muster of good land the great part whereof be cainkeene blue selas and the price be conclude fifty selas thirty five cainkeene sixteen blue byronne the price of pepper and of surat good red selas thirty two and of baftaes according to the goodness eight ten and twelve piece for a Bahar which value according to the rate worth in ready money twenty rial the Bahar and it be agree that the next morning the king shall begin to weigh the custom of good not to be pay in kind but to land whatsoever we will and to pay fourteen the hundred custom fourteen custom at Teco little hope ever to have the great custom abate fire and treachery usual in Teco alteration of the price of pepper in rial of eight for all the pepper shall be pay either with good or money a very hard condition and wondrous unadvised consent to by those former there employ but now it be continue and little hope to get it ever reclaim some good be this day land be first open above and send ashore in bag to prevent wet and small quantity at once for fear of fire and treachery both which be very usual here but especial the latter more than in any part of India the two and twenty the king etc. return to the bailey refuse their former contract and will not himself sell under forty cainkeene and sixty blue selas the Bahar but give free leave to any other that will which be nothing for till he begin none will sell a Catee so that necessity enforce our assent the six and twenty our trade begin and this day weigh the first pepper the content whereof and of the succeed day I forbear to recite have collect it together in a note herewith unto your worship master Nichols etc. be aboard the dragon this day captain Bonner discourse of the business pass at Bantam and his own at present in the dragon fear lest at the fleet arrival the pepper in she shall be take out and send home upon some other ship that have be long in the country as also dread the fleming arrival of who he be always wondrous suspicious affirm Bonner be very suspicious of the hollander and dispose himself for a man of war he have no intent to lade more pepper in the dragon till he know certain how he shall be dispose of but will take it into the expedition whereto he say she shall be present fit and the dragon keep clear and pretty for a man of war in case the fleming shall come his reason be that he can not at any time after take it into his ship of which if he can dispose he can likewise by the same power command the expedition and good therein in which determination he seem to be firm and give order for the expedition fit room upon the arrival of the bear Bonner alter his resolution of fit his ship for a man of war and lade she into England the dragon pester the dragon uncivil but the next day after arrive Henry bate merchant from the ship bear who the day before anchor at Priaman and the eight and twenty of August aforesaid arrive at tecoo at instant of who come but upon what presumption or report I can certain determine captain Bonner change resolution and proceed to lade the dragon fill each place with lumber rummage her bread-roome and so cloy her deck as be not poss^ble to use her piece in great extremity by which unhappy accident we your poor servant have with loss of life or good or both endure excess of most base and past compare contemptible usage from a ingrateful and uncivil nation with many other never to be satisfy or forget injury the seven and twenty all night be very tempestuous fearful thunder and lightning and abundance of rain we have under our house in a room for that purpose some small store of steel Bettle box and such like where also lie two man appoint by capt. Bonner to watch the house discourse of theft in Teco the seven and twenty of August the boat be leave behind they ashore that night John Cocket alias Tucker a youth who have long live at surat and he also lodge there about midnight come thief to open the door which one within perceive with cry out scar they away two hour after they return and one of they put in his arm be strike at with a sword but miss flee away the second time and they within make the door so fast as they can which be but hurdle about four in the morning come again and open the door one go in take some brass Bettle box our man be all fast asleep and in return rub against tucker leg John Tucker slay the seven and twenty of Aug. who start up catch hold of he and cry a thief I have he which scarce pronounce with a pitiful accent cry out again oh he be go and have stab i with his creeze which be so sudden do as those who lie by he have not time to rescue he there be at that time aloft the surgeon of the dragon etc. who present run down with a light but too late the villain have with a knife give he two wound one whereof to the heart who without speak more word then lord have mercy upon i present die we in vain search each bush and place about our house and I go to call the cowal or waiter who every night till this keep watch in a bailey within twenty pace of our house miss who I go instant to the Pongolo Cowallas house and call he ask he where be the watch he say at the bailey which I deny he affirm to have charge one that night then I tell he we have a man slay and will he to search narrow if any suspicious person can be apprehend he forthwith go and acquaint the king therewith who present come down with the chief thereabouts see the dead body and affirm he will do what may be to find the murderer master Nichols charge the cowal to be actor or author hereof and require to have they all send for and one after another to touch the corpse whereto the king give order and when each one have take he by the hand and no cause to suspect any appear master Nichols demand if there be no more cowal it be answer no more save one who be sick and keep his bed he the king command to be send for who very look and demeanour condemn he in the opinion of all to be the villain seek for the king command to take the dead man by the hand which with extreme quake and many distract gesture and answer he do but will not hold it any time master Nichols urge this to be the man and require justice. a story of trial of a malefactor in a strange manner the king cause he to be find and profess in his conscience that be the man who kill he but that he must be try by their law also whereto the fellow assent and while preparation be make thereto we send word to captain Bonner who come ashore to see the event hereof present after who come a fire be make and a iron pan with a gallon of oil set thereon which leisurely boil till it come to such a degree of heat that a green leaf but dip therein be sodden and shiver the prisoner then call and persist in denial of the fact be in testimony of his innocence to take out of the say oil a small ball of brass little big than a musket shoot with his naked hand and that if any burn or scald appear thereon he be content to die which he address himself to perform strip up his sleeve above the elbow and take a kind of protestation desire that as he be clear thereof so he may prosper in this act dip his hand to the wrist in the burn oil take out the ball hold it fast and cry Basar or twenty two rial a Bahar of pepper at tecoo the dragon go out of the seven of march we depart out of Macasser road with the Solomon the Thomas and the attendance master cassarian davis being our chief commander of all the ship the thirteen of the same month be near calm with little wind easterly we tow with our boat and make the best mean we can to get the island the dutch ship have the wind of we bear with we at two a clock in the afternoon the great Bantam vice-admiral get within shoot of we and ply her best to we and we requite she to our power at four a clock the star which take the swan and the swan likewise get within shoot of we at eight a clock at night the admiral get within a ship length of we and ply their great ordnance upon we kill three man and hurt thirteen or fourteen man but will not board we command the chief of we to come aboard their admiral and to strike down our sail and to take in our flag which master cassarian cause to be do and command the Skiffe to be man to go aboard of they and likewise master jackson in another boat to go aboard another of they they be there I can hear no answer from any of they the dutch have our two boat aboard with our chief commander send their four large boat full of man to the number
