the eleven of April by master Thomas Spurway and the thirty of june by master stacy I receive understand thereby of the occurrence happen in Banda which albeit in many thing contrary to our expectation yet as now not to be avoid nor by any fair course hope to have it amend be it to be doubt that surrender be make to his majesty of England of those place and his subject in possession that in so apparent and just cause the fleming dare have fall out into open hostility with we in take the swan and make themselves owner of the defence with the imprisonment of our man but now we have too manifest a proof of their insolency and that they dare do any thing that be not above their force and make the best show of a bad meaning they pretend contract with the king of ternate for defence of his country and with his subject for their epice and all trade whatsoever even to the exclusion of all other nation justice be too weak to deal with force and consequent no plead with they without force which I hope we shall have be able this year to have effect albeit that it fall out to the contrary but the next I doubt not but we shall have force to make they know that free gift and possession be better than contract and that they be not to conquer country to themselves under pretence of defend the king of ternate be to they in nature of a prisoner that be in no command of he in the mean time our endeavour must be for the right of our king and honour of our country to make good what we have master Spurway in his return be charge into botone by the fleming and so belay for that have not the king of that place stand his very good friend he and his company have fall into their hand but by this mean while the fleming wait before the mouth of the river for their come out they be convey over a neck of land and so escape for Maccasser where meet the attendance they take passage and come hither Stacie that owl blind in his self will cast away his praw upon Botone the good all lose the man only save where he leave the Ban^anezes who choose to stay there in hope to save something for themselves and by the king favour get a praw and come thither by the way of seven of june we be send for Pooloway the four humble petition of the prisoner in Nero Road. the four of june 1618. humble show unto your good lordship that whereas your lordship poor petitioner and prisoner be altogether doubtful of any speedy releasement and desirous to avoid the danger of sickness and mortality incident to all man in these unwholesome country do therefore beseech your lordship that it may stand with your lordship pleasure to grant unto your lordship say petitioner licence and favour to go for Holland this year in your lordship ship and so your lordship poor prisoner shall do our best endeavour to do your lordship service in our passage wish there may be a good end of all these difference and thus hope of your lordship favourable charity herein towards we poor prisoner we will pray for the prosperous success of your lordship affair the petition will be grant the five on the second of july humble show unto your lordship that we poor prisoner now in this castle of November with five ship wherein be admiral for the sea sir Thomas dale knight we understand so many injury and insolence do to our nation aswell in those part as in all other place of the India we take one of their ship call the red lion lade with Rice pepper and other commodity whereupon out of their great pride they imprison two of our merchant at jacatra and chain they in their gatehouse to the view of all the country people and not content herewith their house be strong fortify with much ordnance in it shoot at our goodoung and set fire to it and burn it to the ground as also they shoot into the java quarter into the king house and kill many javas and raze the China quarter to the ground with their ordnance and with fire and the king have shoot some ordnance against their house or fort and have have many skirmish with they so that of both side there have be slaughter but most of the javas now the king of jacatra see himself in a strait send a messenger to Bantam desire aid of we and call here a council conclude to send a fleet of eleven sail of ship wherein go sir Thomas dale and captain bring commander not only to surprise their ship but also to destroy their fort if it please God to give a blessing thereunto which be once effect by God grace we determine to proceed for Banda and the Moluccas hope in God that we shall be able to lay some part of their insolent pride if not altogether this year yet the next we expect a far great fleet thereby at once to finish all and whereas the proud Laurence real the dutch general that be have false report that he have letter patent from his majesty of England to surprise we in those part of Banda and the Moluccas we take notice thereof and will put it in print among the rest of their lie out of who mouth there come not a true word we like very well of your former proceed and of your large advice concern those part pray you to continue therein and with a steadfast resolution notwithstanding the hollander threaten to defend the place until we send further aid and no doubt but the honourable company will high reward you and all those that faithful and true do their endeavour in their affair thus leave further to insert at present refer all thing to our next in which God willing we will write you more at large pray God to prosper your proceed to his glory and your heart desire Bantam the three and twenty of come to you I be appoint chief for siam and go with the precedent for Patania where we fall in the hand of our enemy and in the defence of our ship and good perform what we be able but the element fight against we for contrary to the common course we have neither wind nor tide to thwart the ship to bring our ordnance to bear and they breathe themselves to our great disadvantage which we may have help overnight if the precedent have not stand too much upon point of honour in the sight of the country people which in his own person he endeavour to maintain with as much resolution as ever do any commander and most part of we second with our best endeavour as long as we be able until many of u^ be kill and hurt then the precedent sound a parley and in talk with henrike johnson receive his death wound with a musket and they present surprise our ship make pillage of all we have but give most part of we our liberty by reason of our wound where I continue four month in miserable torture with the loss of my right leg shoot off with a canon for want of medicine to apply to it afterward we come to seek our fleet in three prawe and leave two of they with master weldin and forty man for the defence of our factory at jambe the residue be six and twenty with myself come for Bantam this king to have find our fleet where we be surprise with their ship and boat and now remain prisoner with they which be more grievous to i then the re^t by reason of the want of my leg and urge i to solicit to go home in their ship which will be a unseasonable and discontent passage at this time but in the case I be in I do not much value my life and have every day less comfort and courage to remain in these part for either you or myself howsoever I make no question our honourable master will true vain your desert God send you well home to receive the guerdon thereof and the comfort of your friend who as I hear be very desirous to see you his name Robert holding now at japarra and your from their factour about the month of December 1620. the dutch general have prepare a force of sixteen ship declare to our precedent that he intend a exploit for the good of both company without mention any particular of his design and see we to have no such force ready to join with he he say he will attempt it alone and the three of january 1620. he do set sail from jaquatra with his say force and arrive at Banda about the three of February follow present upon his arrival he make great preparation against the island of Lantore which island be former by the inhabitant thereof deliver over unto our people for the use and under the subjection of the king majesty of England whereof our captain of the i will of polaroone have take possession and have also settle a factory there when our chief factor * * this be m. hayes captain of the English in our say isle of polaroone hear of the purpose of the dutch general against the say i will of Lantore he write a letter unto the say general advise he that the say i will of Lantore do belong unto the king of England and that therefore he shall not attempt any violence against it see there be a accord make in England between we which letter the say general throw from he in a great rage scarce vouchsafe to read it over and cause the messenger to be thrust out of door require he to advise our factor of polaroone present to send to Lantore and fetch away all such of our people and good as be upon that island for whosoever he shall find there he will take they as his utter enemy and they shall fare no better than the inhabitant and within ten or twelve day after he land all his force there and subdue the say island so long as the fight endure our factor and servant there be three English and eight chinees keep themselves within door and afterward our people come out of their house and tell they the house wherein they be be the english house and that therefore they shall not meddle therewith nevertheless they sack our house take away all our good murder three of our chine servant find the rest as well English as Chinezes hand and foot and threaten they to cut their throat bind they three several time to several stake with their weapon ready draw out Robert Randall and do put a halter upon our principal factor neck draw up his head and stretch out his neck ready to put they to death yet do not execute they but as they be find hand and foot as aforesaid tumble they down over the rock like dog and like to have break their neck and thus find carry they aboard their ship and there keep they prisoner in iron fourteen or sixteen day after the conquest of the island of Lantore the dutch general threaten to do the like unto polaroone wherefore our principal * * this be m. welden factor of polaroone be there but new arrive go unto the dutch general unto the castle of Nero and tell he that he hear that he purpose to take polaroone by force which he can not believe although his own messenger send to polaroone to speak with our factor have give it out also that the general himself shall say that if the english do not come present unto he and yield the say fort of polaroone unto he he will send his force and overrun all the country but hope he will enterprise no such thing against that place consider the article of agreement and know how many year to the great loss and charge of the company we hold possession and maintain the place to the use of his majesty of England the say general make little answer to it as though there be no such matter intend whereupon our say factor take his leave and come away but the next day he be follow to polaroone with a armado of twenty six prowess and one ship which do put the inhabitant of polaroone in such a fear as they know not what to do whereupon our chief factor there ask the commander of those force what his purpose be with such a fleet there and that if he attempt any thing against poolaroone it be a breach of the article it be in our possession this can not prevail with he but say the land be they and they will have it by fair mean or force and as for our profession they will not acknowledge it the inhabitant and not we be master of the place and so the dutch commander go ashore unto the inhabitant whereupon the say inhabitant ask we if we can and will defend they but perceive we be not able to defend ourselves much less to secure they they be force to yield themselves and the island into his hand the dutch take down the english colour and set up their own and cause the inhabitant present to bring in all their weapon and to throw down all their wall and will have force they to have take all our ordnance out of our fort which they at the first refuse to do allege that they have former give and surrender the land to the king of England and in respect they have live so long with the english they will not now offer we any injury or violence and when our chief factor go ashore to expostulate the matter with the dutch commander he can obtain nothing at his hand but that the land be they and thing must be so and shall be so whereupon our say factor go again unto the dutch general to the castle of Nero to confer with he thereabouts but he will give no other answer but that he have refer those business to his say lieutenant send thither with who he may confer who in the absence of our chief factor have bring some of his soldier ashore upon poolaroone and force the islander to throw all our ordnance over the rock from the place where they be plant be nine piece whereof four break with the fall and be all carry away by the dutch. moreover our captain of who have defend the island four year together Nathaniel Courthop go to Lantore at the request of the inhabitant to receive the surrendry thereof for our king majesty use as aforesaid and return back again about the begin of November 1620. be slay by the dutch. and it be very probable they do it after the time they have intelligence of the publication of the accord at Bantam in march 1619. for present upon the say publication they send secret to the land in those part where they have trade to prevent we of our part of the spice due unto we by the accord after the say dutch general have subdue the fore mention island of Lantore he constrain they to deliver unto he the principal of all their child for hostage then he take away from they all their small vessel and boat and then he also require all the man of Lantore to be bring unto he and they bring he all the principal man but this do not satisfy he but he will have all the Bandanezes which have aid they as also all their wife and child small and great to be bring as prisoner aboard his ship which when the Bandanezes perceive doubt that he mean to make they all slave and Adrian jacobson jacatranenses Batavos love brother I have receive your letter and according to your desire have return these few line in answer thereunto if I have not so full satisfy the particular of your letter as I wish and purpose I pray you impute it not to any want of will but unto my disacquaintance with your dutch tongue and hand I shall peradventure have give you better satisfaction than now I do if you have write to i in the latin tongue but to leave excuse and come to the matter the thing you touch in your letter be but too too true to wit that the hatred and dissension among christian if it continue as God defend it shall be and will be the cause of much innocent bloodshedding among friend and of estrange the heart of heathen from the worship of the true God and therefore that enmity among friend may cease and that such as be yet without may be allure to submit themselves to the sceptre of jesus Christ it stand we upon who be preacher of the gospel of peace to be instrument of peace which for my own part how willing I be to do be not unknown to such as know myself and among who I do daily converse I have always both in public and private by letter to our worshipful company in England and by lively voice to our commander here in the indies declare how good a thing ^t be for we that be christian profess one faith one Christ one baptism to live in peace and to dwell together in unity and of this my earnest desire to be a peacemaker master Brancraft your master of the black lion who remain after his take some week aboard of the royal james can give evident testimony and witness and now that you have write to this end I will stir up myself and set afresh upon the work of reconciliation it be pelf indeed and pride that be the makebate breed strife and discord for have not the riches of the molu^^as and the rob of the chinees and other by you under the english colour father thereby your theft upon we cast you into a deep and deadly lethargy you will not as you have do have abuse your best friend abroad that have shed so much of their dear blood in defence of you and your country at home but now you be free from the Spaniard at home you fall out with your friend abroad be this the recompense of our love and blood show unto you and shed for you to keep you from the suppose thraldom of Spain do David thus reward his three worthy who adventure their life to satisfy his long and to quench his thirst do he not say lord be it far from i that I shall do this be not this the blood of the man that go in jeopardy of their life 2. sam. 23.17 do you thus requite we as lot do Abraham who when as he with the three hundred and eighteen that be bear and bring up in his house do recover lot and his good and woman out of the hand of the conqueror care not for he but to serve his own turn and be deliver do in a manner scorn Abraham company well though Abraham be the elder and worthy may have stand upon his right yet yield of his interest that he and lot may live as brother and the rather because both of they at this time sojourn among the canaanite and Pheresites who be ready to take notice of their discord and so to curse their god and holy religion yet what gain lot by separate company but a shower of fire and brimstone which rain upon Sodom wherein he live and will have consume both he and he if God have not be merciful unto he at Abraham request it be not long of the english that we expose ourselves to the mockery of infidel our company love peace and trade peaceable they have put up for peace sake more wrong at your hand than they mean to do again you write and publish to the world that the sea be free and ytt by your encroach upon it be not you both the mother and nurse of discord one of our commander write as I think or at least send word by one of special note among yourselves to Coen your commander concern a parley before the shoot down of our turret at jacatra but the first and last news we hear of he be it not the beat down of our house there and the defame of our nation with Penoran at Bantam and other here and think you that this be the way to make peace the present captain of deposition further open the iniquity and cruelty of the dutch. @. i. a true relation of that which pass in the land of Banda in the east indies in the year of our lord God 1621. and before print at Amsterdam 1622. all the land of Banda from the ten of August 1609. by a special treaty and agreement make with the ^ranka^es or magistrate of the foresay land be put under the protection of the high and mighty the state general of the unite province on condition to defend they from the Portugal and other their enemy provide that they of the say land be find to deliver unto the fort call nassau or unto the committee of the say company all their fruit or spice at a certain price and so forth as by the say treaty of agreement more at large appear these article of agreement be for a time by they perform be afterward break and violate as well in keep back and withhold the say fruit and spice which they be tie to deliver to the Netherlands company as also enforce and rob their warehouse and contrary to solemn treaty and promise murder at sundry time and place diverse of the principal officer committee and servant of the say Netherlands company in take away diverse small ship provision their open invade of the place and country withstand also late under the subjection of the high and mighty the state general and in conquer the inhabitant thereof who with a strong hand they force from be christian to become Moor again or those which withstand or gainsaid they they sell as slave and in commit all kind of perverse wickedness and treachery during which passage and do there be again certain contract on the aforesaid condition agree upon with the say Bandaneses as in May in the year 1616. by one of the Netherlands commander call Lam and by their governor general Laurence real in the year 1617. which indeed be short after break and violate by the bandanese and that through the animate by the english who do open aid and assist the foresay land and maintain they in warrage the Netherlands company with victual and munition great ordnance man and ship thereby to withhold from we the fruit and spice which the bandaneses be tie to deliver in this wilfulness the bandaneses continue till in june 1620. till that at jacatra be publish both among the english and the Netherlands fleet then ride there in the road the treaty conclude and agree upon between his most excellent majesty the king of great Britain and the high and mighty lord the state general for to reconcile upon certain condition the english and Netherlands east India company the which treaty and by conference of handle concern the moluccaes Amboyna and Banda all dispute and difference between the english and the Netherlands company concern the same be to that time abolish and a general force of ship of war be ordain between they for the defence of both company in their right and the commerce which they have obtain in the indies the reduction of the wilful bandaneses unto the Netherlands camp be hinder a year or two through the actual proceed which the english in Banda itself since the year 1616. and afterward in the year 1618. about the coast of java and whole India through by open hostility do attempt whereby the aforesaid bandaneses be encourage and make bold do withdraw themselves whole from under the subjection of the castle of Nassaw do unto we and we all wrong and hostility and withhold from we their fruit to say nutmeg and mace which they do not only sell unto the english and to the indian but also to the portugal who be both their and our enemy with who they seek to make near alliance of friendship as already in the great island name Banda be come fifty or threescore Portug^ls who by some more assistance consider the natural force of the say island will have be sufficient to have deprive both the english and the Netherlands company of the right therein and the fruit thereof without hope hereafter to have any redress in regard of those inconvenience after the publication of the contract that be make the general of the Netherlands company in the common council for defence consist of Englishmen and netherlander propound the necessity of the take of Banda as also the redress and assure of those quarter and of the trade in Amboyna and moluccaes to the which end both the company according to the contract be find together to use all the force and power that he can for the preservation of the place as much as concern the trade for both the company and it appear by the act make by those of the say counsel for defence bear date the first of january 1621. that the english committee there declare that the necessity of the business be well know unto they as also that they be very willing together with we to do some common exploit but for that as then they want both power and mean of man and ship that they can not for that time furnish any thing towards the same whereupon the Netherlands governor general declare that with the particular power of the Netherlands company he will take the same in hand and effect it in such manner as God shall be please to prosper his proceed and to that end upon the t^^rtenth of january the governor general go from jacatra to Amboyna where he arrive upon the fourteen of February and from thence go to Banda to the castle of Nassaw lie in the island Nero upon the seven and twenty of February 1621. in the mean time one of the english counsel for defence that have be at jacatra upon the first of january 1621. and be privy to the contract make lie then in Amboyna when the governor general go from thence to Banda sent-letter in our own ship to the englishman lie in the small island Polaroon and make know and discover unto those of Banda in what manner the general of the Netherlands company intend to assail the great island of Banda and when the say governor general be come to the fort of Nassaw in Banda he understand that the englishman in Polaroon have add they of the town of Lantore in the great island of Banda with four piece of great ordnance and that if they have have long time that the entrance of the general of the Netherlands army into Lantore haven shall have be let and withstand by a great battery as also that some englishman in Lantore assist these of Banda we and according to the contract their enemy both with counsel and force encourage they with their presence and notwithstanding that the say general require the say englishman of Lantore to leave the town for the cause and reason aforesaid as also for that they themselves according to the contract and order make by the counsel of defence before that time may not buy any fruit in Moluccas and Banda as after the publication of the contract they may do and that only together and in common place with the netherlander yet some few of they stay still with they of Banda our common enemy notwithstanding also that the governor general protest that he be not therein to be blame if by that mean any hurt be do unto they be among and with our common enemy from who they shall and ought to have separate themselves first the governors general determine to assail the great island of Banda on the south side by some call Lantore because the principal town be so call by land in a place call Luchny and to that end cause the ship call the hart to anchor thereabouts which lie not long there but it be shoot at by a english piece of ordnance whereby our man be force to tow the say ship with a galley from the shore and to leave two anchor and two cable behind they or else it have be in great danger of sink or burn our man assure we that a english gunner have shoot at they and that they perfect descry and see he although the englishman seem to deny it whereby alter of their first purpose the general of the netherlander resolve to land upon the inward part of the island of Banda there to encamp themselves and then to go up upon the hill and there to plant their ordnance and to that end upon the eight of march 1621. land with seventeen company between Comber and Ortatten they march along the shoareside within the reach of three piece of great ordnance lend then by the englishman and not long before plant there whereby if they have march forward many of our man have be slay and so we shall have find no place there to encamp ourselves but the enemy from the hill will have domineer over we no man know what counsel to give whereby we may get up upon the hill the way whereon above three year before we have be be all entrench whereupon the general determine to enter again into his ship with the whole army to take another course they of Banda not once pursue after we but with flout and mock let we go and so think thereby that they have get the upper hand of we most part of they bring their wife and child again into Lantore after these two erterprise partly hinder by the english ordnance be in that manner cross the general for a three resolution determine to assail the great island of Banda on both side that be on the inner side of the land with six company and on the south side with ten company that they on the inner side shall land a hour before the other shall land by that mean to draw the enemy forth and so to make place on the other side while a company of choose man shall land on the north side to climb up upon the hill and other in other place of the land shall also be in a readiness be three hundred and thirty person whereof one hundred and fifty be musketeer appoint for the man and assure of thirty boat which the say company will bring on the south side of the island this be effect upon the eleven of march and according six company by break of day go on land between Comber and Ortatten captain Voghel with certain choose soldier march forward who climb up upon the hill find such resistance that all their powder be spend they be in great danger to be spoil but be well follow and second by the rest the enemy be force to retire and while this skirmish continue the other ten company land out of the say thirty boat go on shore upon the south side of Banda in a small bay some with ladder and other without climb up upon the cliff and be get up th^y march to the backside of Lantore without any resistance but only those that set upon the first troop be some ten or twenty musketeer by who one of our man be slay and four or five hurt whereby Lantore be take on the south side by the say ten company while the other five company skirmish with those of Banda upon the hill and as soon as Lantore be take those of Madiangi Luchny Ortatten and Sammer present forsake their town in the say island when they of Banda see the aforesaid thirty boat they think we will have sail round about the land as we have do three time before whereupon make no reckon of our land they be sudden surprise by break of day as soon as Lantore with the rest of the place aforesaid be win the rest of they of Banda namely Slamma Comber Owendender wayer and those of the land of rosinging and poolaroone make composition with we which we grant upon condition that they shall break down their fort and wall and give we their shot piece and musket etc. which by they be do all of they together according to their contract and promise yield to hold their country and land of the lord the general state of the unite Netherlands province promise to do whatsoever they shall be command and acknowledge the say lord the general state for their sovereign notwithstanding their former oath take unto any other those of Lantore and other be first overcome and vanquish and that save themselves among other of Banda also ask pardon and seek for peace which be grant unto they upon the condition aforesaid though they hardly hold the same and secret seek to begin a new rebellion and be command by the ge^^^all to show themselves all together upon the strand that they may be appoint in some other convenient place to live as fellow citizen free together without the loss of their good which they then have whereunto some of they obey but the great part flee upon the high mountain in the great island of Banda to who also many other town resort and slay a Netherlands merchant one other and a boy where they be enclose and hinder from victual by our man by this mean all the town and place in Banda be win and make sure only poolaroone which be not meddle withal because they of Banda therein behave themselves peaceable for the aid or rather the service of those of poolaroone the englishman plant nine piece of ordnance upon a small have be do @ 2 a answer to the hollander declaration concern the occurrent of the east India contract somewhat brief than in the former impression there be of late two current publish bear date the hereby plain behold how kind we use his subject make they believe that englishman be their vassal and slave beside all this they keep many of we fast find and fetter in iron in most loathsome and dark lodging at their hand for want whereof many die who be fetch out of the dungeon and so base bury more like dog than christians about the five of May in the year of our lord 1619. we have over-passed many hungry day and cold night lodging in cold iron and dark dungeon and think it not possible able for we to endure those misery any long make mean that some of we come to John Peter Socoma their general that now be and desire his lordship which title he due look for in the east indies that he will consider of our extreme want and misery and help we to some better sustenance and further we desire he that he will be so much our friend as to ease we of our iron but for the day time whereupon the say general most wicked reply with base speech and bid we be go and trouble he no more for if we do he will cause we all to be hang speedy so that we be force to return from whence we come with heavy heart have no hope but in the almighty to who we pray to turn their heart and to release we of our misery upon the thirteen of May in the year of our lord 1619. the dutch go ashore at japara and there they wicked and malicious burn down the town and the english house there and from thence forcible take away the english flag japara the cruelty there and in great disdain of our country trail our flag after they in the dirt through the town and tow it aboard their ship at their boat stern but what they do with it afterward we know not upon the eighteen day of the month of November and in the year of our lord God 1619. they take one Bartholomew churchman and clap he up in iron and set he where he sit in the rain and cold storm of the night and in the day time where the hot sun shine upon he and scorch he without any shelter at all and this they do to he only because he strike a base fellow that speak such word against our late queen Anne majesty as be not fit to be repeat which word as also diverse other which they speak against our dread sovereign we dare not relate as be too odious to be use in a subject mouth touch his prince howbeit may license and freedom of speech be grant we to make know the base slanderous and detract speech of that nation against our king and country that we may not incur any danger of his majesty displeasure by the repeat they it will sufficient make know the pride and cruelty of that people who do not then let to say that they make no account of our king nor any of his subject the seventeen day of the month of march and in the year of our lord God everlasting 1619. their governor of the Moluccas give order for the release of the description of the chief land of Banda and Moluccas by captain HUMPHREY fitz-herbert in a letter to the company right worshipful it remain that before I leave these eastern part I note unto you some particular observe this voyage in Banda Amboyna and the Moluccas which although I easy believe be well know unto you already yet as of the letter of the alphabet well know to all man many unknown word be compose so these note thing either in respect of the time the matter or the manner of the delivery may bring some thing again to your necessary remembrance to your wise foreknowledge or to your further consideration leave japparra and Maccassar I will betake myself to the barrene place of the isle of Banda that be Gonahpee one of the Banda land with a burn top to Gonahpee at the top yield nothing but cinder fire and smoke on the surface below wood without water or fruit for the sustenance of the life of man nevertheless be sever from the island Nero but by a very small channel they together with Lantore on the other side do make a very fair and spacious harbour this island be very subject to earthquake earthquake which do trouble all other the land also and make the ship in the road to totter and tremble again since the surprisal of Nero by the dutch there be a fearful earthquake one most h^deous and horrible the say hill cast forth such hideous flame such store of cinder and huge steam that it destroy burn and break down all the thick wood and mighty tree overwhelm they as it be she own vomit so that a green leaf can not be see in all that part of the island nor do Nero escape these hellish blast which blow these steam and cinder into the castle and country near adjoin in such abundance that it invite all man that see it to her funeral burn up all the fruit tree and cover all the country about it and have like to have sink the ship in the road it be credible report by those that see it the violence be so great that it carry stone of three or four ton weight from the one island into the other and into the Road. the castle stand close on the waterside in the plain it be fair large and strong build but weak situate by reason of the rise of the hill to the landward within less than musket shoot it have a hillock high than it by at the least twenty fathom which do command it at pleasure to prevent which mischief the dutch have build thereon a small fort but in vain the same be under command of another aswell as the former the castle be a matter of great charge castle weak situate both in respect of itself as also in respect of the soldier and altogether unnecessary but for dwell house and magazine the other fort be great enough and strong enough for the defence of this place here be in this castle about forty piece of ordnance in the other some eight or ten the most of brass the dutch have not receive the fruit of this island since their come thither be always overmaster by the black both by sea and land but the gain of Lantore have make all thing quiet now I pray GOD make it profitable hereafter Lantore Lantore be the great and rich island of all the isle of Banda strong and almost inaccessible as it be a castle there be scarce a tree on the island but bear fruit the bandaneses leave it for want of military policy but he must have a politic pate I believe that gain it again the town be situate on the brow of a sharp hill the ascent as difficult as by a ladder while they stand peevish to the defence thereof to the roadwards the dutch land with much ado on the other side of the island and surprise they at unaware right over the town the dutch have build a fort on the top of the hill to prevent the like inconvenience as also to keep the same in better subjection it be but small and while I be there the foundation scarce finish if the english have come thither a month or six week before the dutch make this spiteful expedition I dare avouch it they may have near lade the best ship your worship have in India with nutmeg and mace from these land Pooloway Pooloway be the paradise of all the rest entermit pleasure with profit there be not a tree on that island but the nutmeg and other delicate fruit of superfluity and withal full of pleasant walk so that the whole country seem a contrive orchard with variety they have none but rainwater none but rain water which they keep in jarres and cistern or fetch it from the abovenamed land which be their only defect the sea shore be so steep that it seem nature mean to reserve this island particular to herself there be but one place about the whole island for a ship to anchor in and that so dangerous that he that let fall his anchor seldom see the weigh of it again beside he incur the imminent danger of his ship how this island be win by Derrick Lam the castle poolaroone or lose by captain castleton I can well relate it have on the eastern side a fair and strong castle a regular Pentagonon well fortify and furnish with all manner of provision and soldier and be hold to be the strong castle the dutch have in the indies and the most pleasant residence poolaroone in imitation of her sister the other land be turn dutch. there be in she neither pleasure every prunage have his vintage a rarity it seem to i in nature I see in the wood of this island a plant or tree or neither or whether I shall call it I know not in substance much like to the body of our ivy in form like a hal^er of five or six inch in length five or six fathom bare without sprig or sprout the one end fast in the ground the other fix to the limb of a great tree a fathom and better distant from the body thereof and so perpendicular that it be very disputable whether it grow up from the ground or from the limb of the tree to the ground this rope be of firm solid wood without any concavity and yet it yield excellent good fair and sweet water and as fresh as from the fountain nor do it herein admit any distinction or difference unless it be the more delicate according to your company cut more or less thereof distribute every one the quantity of two foot or thereabouts and they shall have sufficient for every piece will run to the value of a pint or thereabouts and that in we can nor will sell to any other nation but only to the king of England his subject according to the true meaning of our covenant and surrender of the two foresay land to his majesty with all that be in they to be sole at his dispose which be and shall be the reason that we can trade with any other and whereas all the Orankayas of the two foresay land have make this agreement let it be credit that it be not make in madness or loose as the breathe of the wind but because it be conclude upon in their heart they can revolt or swerve from the same again moreover all we together do desire of his majesty that such thing as be not fit in our religion as unreverent usage of woman maintain of swine in our country forceable take away of man good misse-using of our man or any such like that be except against in our law that they be not put in practice be out of our use and custom that they may not prove a blemish unto our religion and that we may receive no occasion to deal unkind with the English furthermore if any Englishman will beeome of our religion we will accept of he upon counsel or if any of our people will become a Christian he shall be so likewise upon like counsel desire this promise that such thing be not do in such manner as may breed discontent betwixt we and the english which we do very earnest desire of his majesty final at this time all the Orankayas of Pooloway and poolaroone do again make a covenant with Nathaniel Courthop captain of the two ship ride here Sophon Cozocke and Thomas Spurway give ground and surrender the two foresay land unto the king of that whereas in the time that the country of Banda be in trouble by reason of their enemy so that they be no long al^^ to withstand they they therefore agree with Nathaniel Courthop Sophonie Cozock and Thomas Spurway thus much in effect that be that they do surrender the country of wayre and the island of rosinging unto the king of England in respect that they be not able any more to stand for orankaye can in our conscience dissolve it again but that it shall last for ever until the last day of doom and that the english shall be as the man of the country of wayre in all privilege furthermore the man of the aforesaid country of wayre and the island of rosinging do promise and agree to send unto the king of England one branch of nutmeg as a token of there foresay agreement of all we the aforesaid orankaye on condition that the say token of our agreement be not out of memory nor dissolve nor we dis-esteemed and we do wish that almighty God will vouchsafe to give prosperity any other but only to the king of England his subject because we have whole unto he surrender the foresay two country of wayre and rosinging with all that therein be or whatsoever it do or shall yield it be the king of England his own and this shall stand for a reason that we cann^t trade with any other nation moreover we entreat the king majesty of England in earnest manner that such thing as be not befit to our religion as unmannerly usage of our woman maintain of swine in our country beat and abuse of our man or take away of they perforce against their will as if they be their own slave or any other such like attempt that be hold unbeseeming in our law we say that we do entreat his highness that none of these or such like be put in practice by his subject because they be thing disallowable in our law and so be commit will redound to the overthrow thereof and we thereby may be force to deal unkind with the english therefore moreover if any of the english hereafter shall have a affection to be circumcise and become as one of we it shall be do upon sufficient counsel between the rest of the english and we or if any of we will become a christian in that cause the like counsel shall be hold and this shall not be do for any misdemeanour of the party will so to turn because that may breed a dissension between the english and we and whereas this agreement be make in the presence and by the consent of the king and Sabander of wayre the Sabander of rosinging Emmon Hattib and all the rest of the orankaye of the country of wayre and the land of rosinging this shall be for a testimony that it be not do in madness or in the manner of the breathe of wind but that it be also aswell think in our heart as speak with our mouth and therefore we can nor will go from it again but that it shall so stand until the dissolution of the world neither shall there any doubt rise in our heart of any other but that we the man of wayre and rosinging be only the king majesty of England his subject and if any trouble hereafter do happen in the foresay country we will be content aswell to die as to live together with the english because we will be subject to one king and this shall stand for a reason that any be in league with we shall also be in league with the english and he that be near the english shall be near we because we will by no mean again divorce ourselves one from the other final at the time this agreement be make all the orankaye of Pooloway and poolaroone be witness thereunto all the orankaye of Pooloway and rosinging have unto the aforesaid premise set government it be a thing certain that be it good or bad the profit arise according for we daily see and find that by negligence and ill government a great estate be soon bring to nought and on the of all be require a good understanding and experience which I persuade myself have be and be in many of the major without all doubt but that be not enough except there be care and diligence withal but what care and diligence can be expect from they who be so continual employ in their public office and function beside their particular affair that they can scarce once or twice in a week spend a few hour in this weighty business which indeed have need of a constant and continue sale according as the greatness and importancy thereof require etc. further be require in every mayor that he by all mean seek to procure the common good of that which be commit to his charge seek their own private benefit and not his particular but how or wherein have they hitherto seek the common good of the company so long as they take a liberty to sell the company good unto themselves in which sale they no doubt seek their own particular profit and not the company at sometime one mayor buy the company good of another mayor and at another time it happen quite contrary viz. that he which be at first the buyer be now become the seller to he that former be the seller himself one may well conjecture how these thing be thus carry by such who it may be be not so honest as they shall be what hindrance hereby befall the adventurer and what profit to the major one may well conjecture by the small profit which the adventurer have make and the great wealth which the major have attain unto when as the major have buy great quantity of the company good for themselves be to be imagine what kind of advice they will send to the indies concern such good as themselves have buy and whether their advice shall not tend to their particular profit etc for may one peruse their book no doubt thereby will be find that many among they have little or no adventure at all with the company and it will plain appear the major have little or no adventure with the company that their provision or factory concern they near than the profit of the stock they have there to respect and therefore do ready resolve to the set forth of great ship or fleet when as few and small will have be sufficient for conquest and few for trade from port to port whereof that fleet which go through the straight of magellane be one which fleet alone do charge the company with more than a capital it be likewise the practice of these kind of major know the choice to be in their own power to prefer their friend and kindred to the government prefer their friend to government and exclude those that be great adventurer take ofttimes such as be none but such as when they stand in nomination to be do then begin to buy conditional so they be choose than their buy to stand but if not than the barga^ne to be void what good service the company be to expect by such nimbling may well be conjecture beside they ofttimes prefer their friend to be send as committee and other officer to the indies committee se^t by their procurement great have so base vild and proud insolent committee in the indies further what loss the company be put unto by the build of so great and costly ship each chamber strive which shall make the great ship and yet God be praise with less hurt than I can have imagine thus have compass the three last mention ship and luff to rejoine with our own fleet which all this while hold the benefit of the wind play a surcease from so toilsome a work and anchor after midnight in their before usual Road. in this fight the London and hart receive very little hurt in their hul and tackle less or none among their man touch the fight I have add this letter or relation send to the company from the chief of the Fleet. relation of the fight of four english ship with four Portugal ship two galliat and ten frigate in the gulf of Persia in the month of December and january 1620. the London and the robucke arrive at surat the nine of December there understand that the portugal have send into the gulf of Persia a armado purposely to attempt the english ship at their come thither whereupon it be forthwith resolve by the english factor at surat and the commander of the abovenamed two ship that they shall apply themselves to the gulf of Persia to rejoine themselves with two other english ship namely the hart and the eagle which part from the London and Robucke before their come to surat and be go direct towards jasque in the say gulf of Persia and so the say London and Robucke set sail from surat towards jasques the nineteen day of November and the first day of December follow they meet with the hart and the eagle about eighty league short of jasque where all the four ship join together they receive most certain intelligence by a Portugal frigate which they meet that the Portugal Armado consist as aforesaid of four galleon two galliat and about ten frigate be attend they at the easter end of jasques road where the english ship must come and so go along towards the same where the sixteenth day they find the say Portugal Armado consist in these particular before name the general or chief commander whereof be name Ruy Frere de Andrado who themselves call the pride of Portugal the vice-admiral John Boralio and inhabitant of Ormus and late admiral of those sea of the other two ship the commander be Anthonio musket and Balthasar di chave this day prove calm so that it be night ere they come in shot one of another the seventeen of December be the lord day we intend to have sanctify his service be under sail a league to sea-boord of they but about eight of the clock with the land turn they weigh anchor and bear up with we for who albeit they have the wind we shorten sail and stay near about nine of the clock we join fight with they which continue until the darkness of the night just challenge a end to so long and weary a work they like a kind host to stranger leave we their anchor place to lodge in and retire some ten or eleven mile to the eastward there to amend and repair themselves we can true particulate unto you their hurt and loss in this fight save by report of our merchant that John Boralio their vide-admiral and the captain of one of the other ship be slay with some thirty or forty man out of their admiral the rest yet unknown the loss or hurt of our man in your own ship the enclose note of this seventeen present will make manifest thus for a time we be not disturb by our enemy though by contrary wind we can not get into the usual road before the twenty current the twenty one and twenty two the most part of your good be land and descry the Portugal galleon open of the road to come in as we suppose with the sea-turne we therefore set sail and stand off with they but after some small show of bear up with the sea-wind they clap upon a lake and be so fortunate until the eight and twenty day that either they be to windward we can not come at they or else at anchor we can not without our great disadvantage meddle with they the eight and twenty be innocent day both fleet ride at the easter point of the road not a mile distant one from the other we omit no opportunity to give battle to our wary protract enemy who as by his work appear if he can have avoid fight and by linger delay and the benefit of his frigate have hinder we from the prosecution of your persian designment he attain unto the full height and scope of his employment but about one of the clock the lord send we a pretty gale our fleet weigh and put all thing in order for to fight the London and hart next anchor within a cable length from they upon their broad side and so endure the hot brunt of this two day fight for no soon be they at anchor but it fall calm and so continue all day insomuch that the roe Bucke and eagle who be somewhat a stern and steer near the shore with intent to anchor one upon the bow of the Portugal admiral and the other upon the bow of the vide-admiral can not notwithstanding all diligence use come to do any service in half a hour space but be come near anchor and all our ship so fit to keep our broad side full upon they the great ordnance out of our whole fleet play so fast upon they that about three of the clock in the afternoon not willing to endure so hot entertainment they cut their cable and with the tide drive down from we until be without reach of our ordnance their frigate come and tow they away wonderful mangle and tear for their admiral in the hot of the fight be enforce to heel their ship to stop his leak his main topmast over board and the head of his main mast the three ship both his topmast mizon mast and part of his bow spirit be shoot away the lesser ship have never a shroud leave stand nor never a topmast the vide-admiral escape best for most common he have one or other of their ship between he and we all this night we keep they company with hope the next morning to have give they all or some of they their passport but survey our shot and find no great store leave and withal consider the great weight and import of the voyage we have to perform we resolve our return to jasque for the speedy dispatch of our business in hand thank God for put our enemy to flight before we of who unto the present writing hereof we have hear no news neither be any of they arrive at Ormus or muscat as our merchant report only it be rumour by some caffaire who by swim escape ashore that Ruy Frere de Andrado * * this prove not true be slay all your ship praise be God remain serviceable and not above five man slay on our part in these two long and great battle and not many wound as by the list of their name here enclose will appear among who our worthy admiral and kind commander receive a great and grievous wound through his left shoulder with a great shot which hurt he with such courage and patience underwent that give great hope to we all of his much wish recovery but have beside his former wound two of his uppermost rib on the left side break the six of januarie he depart this life show himself as ever before a resolute commander so in his passage through the gate of death a most willing humble constant and assure christian his body we intend to have carry to surat and there according to his desert to have perform his last funeral right the chyrurgians confident promise by embalm and waxe-cloth to preserve he without annoyance thither but notwithstanding this cost and their promise his body in regard of his great wound prove noisome we be enforce to bury he at jasque which be effect the seven current with what respect solemnity and decency the time require the thirteen of january 1620. aboard the ship London in jasques Road. underwritten by all the four master of the four ship ri. blyth chr. of trade from England unto the east indies answer to diverse objection which be usual make against the same write by t. mun. the trade of merchandise be not only that laudable practice whereby the intercourse of nation be so worthy perform but also as I may term it the very touchstone of a kingdom prosperity when therein some certain rule shall be diligent observe for as in the estate of private person we may account that man to prosper and grow rich who be possess of revenue more or less do according proportion his expense whereby he may yearly advance some maintenance for his posterity so do it come to pass in those kingdom which with great care and wariness do ever vent out more of their home commodity then they import and use of foreign ware for so undoubted the remainder must return to they in treasure but where a contrary course be take through wantonness and riot to over-waste both foreign and domestic ware there must the money of necessity be export as the mean to help to furnish such excess and so by the corruption of man condition and manner many rich country be make exceed poor whilst the people thereof too much affect their own inormity do lay the fault in something else wherefore industry to increase and frugality to maintain be the true watchman of a kingdom treasury even when the force and fear of prince prohibition can possible retain the same and therefore as it be most plain that proportion or quantity must ever be regard in the import of foreign ware so must there also be a great respect of quality and use that so the thing most necessary to be first prefer such as be food raiment and munition for war and trade which great blessing when any country do sufficient enjoy the next to be procure be ware fit for health and art the last be those which serve for our pleasure and ornament now forasmuch as by the providence of almighty God the kingdom of England be endow with such abundance of rich commodity that it have long enjoy not only great plenty of the thing before name but also through a superfluity have be much enrich with treasure bring in from foreign part which have give life unto so many worthy trade among which that unto the east India by name the report whereof although it be already spread so famous through the world yet notwithstanding here at home the clamorous complaint against the same be grow so loud and general that my self be one of the society it have much trouble my private meditation to conceive the mean or true ground of this confusion but at the last I resolve myself that the great number of these exclaimer be lead away in ignorance not have as yet discern the mystery of such weighty affair some have be transport with envy as not participate in the say society or be thereby hinder as they conceive in some other trade and other whole corrupt in their affection who whilst they willing run into these error do also labour diligent to seduce other that so this good and glory of the kingdom may be subvert by ourselves which by the policy and strength of stranger can so easy be abate wherefore it be now a fit time to meet with such injurious course by a true narration of the passage in the say east India trade answer to those several objection which be so common make against the same that so these misunderstanding and error may be make know unto the whole body of this kingdom which at this present time be most worthy represent to those noble assembly of the high court of parliament where I hope the worth of this rich trade shall be effectual inquire and so in the end obtain the credit of a honourable approbation the first objection it be a happy thing for Christendom say many man that the navigation to the east indies by way of the cape of good hope have never be find out for in the fleet of ship which be send thither yearly out of England Portugal and the low-countreye the gold silver and coin of Christendom and particular of this kingdom be exhaust to buy unnecessary ware the answer the matter of this objection be very weighty and therefore it ought to be answer full the which that I may the better perform I will divide the same into three part in the first I will consider the necessary use of the ware which be usual bring out of east India into Europe namely drug spice raw-silke indigo and calico in the second I will imitate the manner and mean by which the say ware have be heretofore and now be bring into Europe in the three and last I will prove that the treasure of England be not consume but rather great to be increase by the performance of the say trade touch the first who be so ignorant in any famous commonwealth the first part concern the use of indian ware which will not consent to the moderate use of wholesome drug and comfortable spice which have be so much desire in all time and by so many nation not thereby to surfeit or to please a liquorish taste as it often happen with many other fruit and wine but rather as thing most necessary to preserve their health and to cure their disease sir Thomas eliot his castle of health rembert Dodoneus his history o^ plant the french academy second part and other even as it be most notable set forth by some learned man who have undertake to write upon this subject and therefore it shall be altogether needless here to discourse upon their several operation and virtue see that he that list may be well instruct therein if he will peruse the volume which be pen by the learned for the benefit of all those who shall make use thereof but if peradventure it be yet further urge that diverse nation live without the use of drug and spice the answer be that either s^ch people know not their virtue and therefore suffer much by the want of ware so healthful or else they be most miserable be without mean to obtain the thing which they so much want but sithence I intend to be brief I will insist no further upon this point for the obiecter may aswell deny we the use of sugar wine oil raisin fig prune and currand and with far more reason exclaim against tobacco cloth of gold and silver lawn cambric gold and siluer-lace velvet satin taffeta and diverse other manufacture yearly bring into this realm for a infinite value all which as it be most true that while we consume they they likewise devour our wealth yet nevertheless the moderate use of all these ware have ever suit well with the riches and majesty of this kingdom France and the low-countries (@) late year do make gre^t quantity of wrought silk of which ware they be heretofore serve from Italy France Italy south Barbary and other country but I will come to the raw silk and indigo this be so excellent for the die of our woollen clothes thereby so much esteem in so many place of the world that ornament together with the great relief and maintenance of so many hundred of poor people who be continual employ in the wind twist and weave of the same insomuch that by the cherish of this business as his majesty for his part be gracious please to perform in remit the impost of silk it may well be hope that in short time industry will make the art to flourish with no less happiness to this kingdom than it have do through many age to diverse state in Italy and late also to the kingdom of France and to the unite province of the low-countreye now as touch the trade of calico of many sort into which the
