the world for poor and rich complain they never have enough but it seem the malady be grow mortal here with we and therefore it cry out for remedy well I hope it be but imagination make we sick when all our part be sound and strong for who know not the inestimable treasure of this kingdom in plate possess by the people thereof almost of all degree in such measure as never have be see in former age and for his majesty mint it be well know that there have be coin in five year together since the east India company begin six thousand two hundred fourteen pound weight of gold and three hundred eleven thousand three hundred fourscore and four pound weight of sterling money all which gold and silver do amount unto the sum of twelve hundred thirteen thousand eight hundred fifty pound of sterling money how then do this trade turn the currant and employment of the mint but upon the sight of this truth perhaps it will be say that we must resort unto the present time the mint be idle now to which I answer that likewise the mint have little or no employment for coinage of silver in former time when the say company do not export above fifteen or twenty thousand pound sterling at the most no nor yet in the year 1608 and 1612 when in the former they ship out but six thousand pound and in the latter but one thousand two hundred and fifty pound sterling so that both way we see that the mint have have very great employment five year together sithence the east India trade begin and also it have be without employment diverse year when the east India company have send away but very small sum of money wherefore of necessity there must be some other cause and mean whereby our silver be not export only but also it be not import into the realm as in former time for we have not have the mean by our own plenty nor by the scarcity of our neighbour for the space of the last fourteen year together to send out hundred of ship lade with corn as in time past which be return home in silver but rather of late year as be much to be fear a great quantity of our money have be carry out of the kingdom for that corn which have be bring we from the east country and other place to supply our want thus time do change and our fortune change with they neither listen I to make this matter plain by set down those mean which heretofore bring we store of money even out of France and other place which now be cease but without any further meddle in the mint I will come to the remedy which some propound by put down the east India company but here our comfort be that the objector be not our judge who wisdom and integrity labour for the honour of his majesty and the good of his kingdom will soon perceive the mischief of this supposed remedy and that the pretend evil which many with malice chase be that great good which other nation seek by policy and strength to keep and likewise to obtain in which proceed it concern we especial to observe the diligence and practice of the dutch who with more gladness will undertake the whole trade to the east indies then with any reason we can abandon that part thereof which we now enjoy neither can our restraint from the indies keep our silver from thence as long as the dutch go thither for we know that device want not to furnish such design and when their ship return from India shall not our silver out again to help to pay a double price or what they please for all those ware which we shall want for our necessity thus shall the dutch increase their honour wealth and strength while we abate grow poor and weak at sea for want of trade and call you this a remedy no rather term it ruin destruction or what you listen and so I come unto the conclusion or last part and here I must confess myself aground for this matter be much too high for my handle beside my excuse be fair have already do my task to clear the east India trade from imputation the which for want of learning although I have perform without variety of word or eloquence yet it be do with all integrity of truth in every particular as I shall be ready to make proof upon all occasion which may be offer and yet before I make a end although I can satisfy every man desire in such measure as be necessary yet I think it not amiss to perform the same so far as I be able by common practice and my observation in the trade of merchandise which be my profession and first therefore all man do know that the riches or sufficiency of every kingdom state or commonwealth consist in the possession of those thing which be needful for a civil life this sufficiency be of two sort the one be natural and proceed of the territory itself the other be artificial and depend on the industry of the inhabitant the riches of a kingdom be of two sort the realm of England praise be God be happy possess of they both as first have great plenty of natural riches both in the sea for fish and on the land for wool cattle corn lead tin iron and many other thing for food raiment a^d munition insomuch that upon strict term of need this land may live without the help of any other nation but to live well to flourish and grow rich we must find mean by trade to vent our superfluity therewith to furnish and adorn we with the treasure and those necessary ware which foreign nation do afford this kind of industry make some country which be poor of themselves to grow rich and strong by other nation who have great mean and be less industrious four principal cause which carry away our gold and silver and here industry must begin to play his part not only to increase and guide the trade abroad but also to maintain and multiply the art at home for when either of these fail or be not effect with such skill as their mystery shall require then do the commonwealth abate and grow poor neither be it easy perceive at first until some evil accident do stir up our diligence to search out the true cause that so they be remove the effect may cease and this be the subject of our discourse which we now pursue that which I have hitherto deliver have be altogether negative still defend and prove by argument that the east India trade have not hurt this commonwealth and now change my style I must affirm as fast the true cause of those evil which we seek to chase away these cause then as I conceive be principal four the first be the breach of intercourse by foreign nation the second be the abuse of the exchange betwixt we and other country the three be neglect of duty in some subject the four be our damage in commerce with stranger now concern all these I may make a very large discourse but my purpose be only to explain the meaning of every point in order as brief as I can and first for the breach of intercourse by this I understand those nation the first cause concern the standard proceed against intercourse who have either debase their standard or else over value the price of their coin from that equivalence which former they have with the standard and money of this realm and also do tolerate not only their own money but also the coin of other country and especial of this kingdom to be current with they at high rate than the price of the exchange by which course be direct against the intercourse there be a great cause give of exportation of the money of this realm than otherwise there will be for although this be do with great danger to the exporter of the same it be a act against the law of the land yet notwithstanding covetousness be ever conversant in wicked action think nothing unlawful which promise a certain gain and how to remedy this evil practice I find it not easy for the debase of the coin or raise the price thereof in this realm will much impoverish the estate of particular man and yet in the conclusion will prove a business without end for who do not conceive that which will follow beyond the sea upon any such alteration here with we so that still the evil will remain until we find some other remedy and for the exchange of money use betwixt nation the second cause concern the exchange of money with foreign country the practice of those stranger here in this realm who make a trade by exchange of money foreign ware bring in with our ready money carry out of this realm the three cause concern neglect of duty our heavy money be convey beyond the sea and melt down into plate here in the realm although the true use thereof be a very laudable and necessary practice for the accommodate of merchant affair and furnish of traveller in their occasion without the transport of coin from one state to another with danger and loss both to the public and private wealth yet be the abuse thereof very prejudicial unto this kingdom in particular while in the interim the benefit do arise unto other country who diligent observe the price whereby the money be exchange may take advantage to carry away the gold and silver of this realm at those time when the rate of our sterling money in exchange be under the value of that standard unto which place they be convey for in respect the price of the exchange do rise or fall according to the plenty or scarcity of money which be to be take up or deliver out the exchange be hereby become rather a trade for some great moneyed man than a furtherance and accommodation of real trade to merchant as it ought to be in the true use thereof and thus many time money may be make over hither by stranger to a good gain and present carry beyond the sea to a second profit and yet the mischief end not here for by this mean the taker up of money in foreign country must necessary drive a trade to those place from whence they draw their money and so do fill we up with foreign commodity without the vent of our own ware but for this great evil there be a easy remedy and so I come to handle the next cause which be neglect of duty neither be it my intent to write of duty in their several kind but only of that kind of duty which be here think to be neglect by some man in their several vocation as it may peradventure come to pass in those who have the work of his majesty coin either gold or silver if diligent care be not have in the size of every several piece to answer just to his weight for howsoever upon trial of many piece altogether the weight may be sound according to the covenant and within the remedy ordain in the indenture yet notwithstanding many of those piece may be size too light and other as much too heavy which give the great advantage to some people to carry away that which be over-weight and so to leave we they which be too light if they leave we any and this mischief be not single for thereby also some gold smith regard profit more than duty may be the more ready draw to melt down the heavy coin into plate and other ornament both of gold and silver but what may we think of those man who be place in authority and office for his majesty if they shall not withal dutiful care discharge their trust concern that excellent statute wherein it be order that all the money receive by stranger for their merchandise shall be employ upon the commodity of this realm 17. Edward 4. the due performance whereof will not only prevent the carry away of much gold and silver but also be a mean of great vent of our own ware whereof I purpose to write some thing more in the next part which concern our commerce with stranger the four cause concern our commerce with stranger unskilful merchant overthrow our trade and now I come to the last point which I fear be not the least among the cause of our want of money so far as any such may be and let it not seem strange to any man that trade shall hurt and impoverish a commonwealth since it have be always account a excellent mean to help and enrich the same for as this truth can be deny with reason so it be likewise most certain that the unskilful manage thereof have ever prove a great decay unto those nation who have be entangle with such error and be not the example too frequent in many of our own merchant who not only by the peril of the sea and such like misfortune lose their good but also even through want of knowledge wise to direct their affair do overthrow their whole estate neither may we proper call this their loss but rather the kingdom loss in they wherefore it be to be wish that this mystery of merchandise may be leave only to they who have have a education thereunto merchant by education be only fit to trade in foreign part and not to be undertake by such who leave their proper vocation do for want of skill in this both overthrow themselves and other who be better practise but there be yet a far great mischief by our trade beyond the sea when peradventure there may be import yearly a great value in foreign ware then by any way or mean we do export of our own commodity which can otherwise come to pass then with a manifest impoverish of the commonwealth how rich commonwealth may become poor foreign ware bring in for trans to can hurt but great help the commonwealth hope to increase trade by exportation of indian ware to foreign part for as it be a certain course to make we rich both in stock and treasure when we shall carry out a great value of our own good than we bring in of foreign ware so by consequence a course contrary to this must of necessity work a contrary effect neither be this importation mean otherwise then concern those ware which be consume in this realm for the commodity which be bring in and after carry out unto foreign part again can hurt but do great help the commonwealth by increase of his majesty custom and trade with other employment of the subject by which particular I may yet set forth the glory of the east India trade which have bring into this realm in fif^eene month space not only so much spice as have serve the same for the say time but also by the superfluity thereof there have be export into foreign part for about two hundred and fifteen thousand pound sterling so then let all man judge for what a great value we may hope hereafter to export yearly when unto these spice we may by God assistance add the infinite worth of raw silk ^ndicoes calico and some other thing all which be to be issue in the nature of cloth lead tin or any of our own merchandise to the enrich of this kingdom by increase of the common stock so then to conclude this point we ought not to avoid the importation of foreign ware but rather willing to bridle our own affection to the moderate consume of the same the particular trade to the east indies will bring great store of treasure into this realm if the general trade of this kingdom do not hinder and consume it the dutch in particular be say to reap such infinite wealth yearly by this fish trade that without more certain knowledge thereof I dare not set down the sum it seeme^meth so incredible see hereof d. dees book as also cap. smiths for otherwise howsoever the east India trade in particular be a excellent mean great to increase the stock of money which we se^d thither yearly by return home five time the value thereof in rich commodity all which in short time may be convert into treasure as be plain show already yet notwithstanding if these indian ware thus bring home can be spare to serve for that purpose of treasure but must be send forth together with our own native commodity and yet all little enough to provide our excess and extraordinary consume of foreign ware then be it likewise as certain that the general trade of this kingdom do hinder and divert the come in of the say treasure by overbalance the value of our ware export with the importation and immoderate consume of foreign commodity therefore forasmuch as the number of the people in this realm be think to be great encreas^d of late time both in themselves and stranger whereby necessary the commodity of this kingdom and also foreign ware be the more consume and waste a double mean to abate the commonwealth it therefore concern we all in general and every man in his particular to stir up our mind and diligence to help the natural commodity of this realm by industry and increase of art see that the material can be want to make such stuff and other thing as be daily bring unto we from foreign part to the great advantage of stranger and to our no less damage neither shall we neglect the riches which our sea afford while other nation by their labour do procure themselves great treasure from the same and as the diligent performance of these thing will plentiful maintain the poor and much increase the common stock of this kingdom so likewise for the better furtherance thereof we ought religious to avoid our common excess of food and raiment which be grow to such a height in most degree of people above their ability that it be now beyond all example of former age neither be it needful for i to set down the particular of these abuse for they be too well know and I be confident that the wisdom of our government do endeavour to see they as well amend to the glory of God the honour of the king and the good of the commonwealth amen courteous reader I can have add other endeavour in this defensive argument for the east indian trade and especial that of that learned gentleman sir dud. diggs but because himself be now absent in weighty employment and I
